campaigns/dungeonvice.title: DungeonVice (2025)
campaigns/dungeonvice.content:
DungeonVice (2025)
A 2025 campaign DM’d by Jake, following a team of city inspectors — part detective squad, part
magic-powered task force — working cases for the Council of Turgeth. Only session 3 has been
transcribed and extracted so far; sessions 1 and 2 are not yet in the archive, so the party’s formation
and earlier cases are unknown. As of session 3 the campaign is mid-arc, hunting a new troll crime lord
and dangling a lead on a devil-bargain and a city-wide drug conspiracy.
The party

Rich (played by Rich) — Rich’s Monk (DungeonVice), a monk (Crane Style, Stunning Strike, flurry of
blows); carries the party’s shared platinum piece in his handy haversack.
Nutty (played by Nutty) — Nutty’s Arcane Combatant (DungeonVice), an arcane combatant wielding a
bladed tail weapon, casting Web and a touch-spell/weapon combo nicknamed “Washashaka.”
Ozan (played by Ozan) — Ozone, a bard-type with a disguise kit/hat of disguise, a net as signature
weapon, and Glitter Dust.
Pat (played by Pat) — Pat’s Wizard (DungeonVice), a wizard, mostly absent in session 3.

Not present in session 3: Donnie, Jess, Connor — unknown whether they have characters in this campaign.
Timeline

Sessions 1–2 — not yet recorded/transcribed.
2025-03-31 — The inspectors interrogate a prisoner who engineered her
own capture to hunt a golden ticket to hell, learn the drug Maka is secretly run by the
College of Turgeth, and raid a dockside warehouse belonging to The Boot, killing Fugly
(nicknamed “the captain” by the players mid-fight — see The Guard Captain) before the Boot escapes
by ship — session ends mid-chase.

Major threads
Resolved

The warehouse raid itself — guards killed, Fugly dead, the warehouse burned
2025-03-31

Dangling / open

Hunt for the Boot — the Boot himself escaped by ship, last seen with Rich in pursuit, hasted and
ethereal, as the ship left harbor.
Retrieve the Golden Ticket — the prisoner’s one-way pass to the devil holding her husband
Riggs’s soul was never retrieved.
College of Turgeth Drug Pipeline — the college is secretly the source of the drug Maka, worth
~75,000 gp/week; not yet investigated directly.
Aqueducts Assignment — offered by Volto at the top of the session, not pursued.

Unresolved
Sessions 1 and 2 of this campaign have not yet been transcribed/extracted, so the party’s origin, how
they became inspectors, and any earlier cases are unknown.

campaigns/jakedm.title: JakeDM's Campaign (2023)
campaigns/jakedm.content:
JakeDM’s Campaign (2023)
A 2023 campaign DM’d by Jake, running a mercenary crew through a doppelganger-infiltrated bank heist,
an accidental city-leveling catastrophe, a refugee flight, and a magic-carpet death race — six sessions
recorded so far, the last ending on an unresolved cliffhanger. One session in the middle is a disconnected
one-shot DM’d by Pat instead of Jake, almost certainly mislabeled into this slug (see Interlude, below).
Shape of the campaign: main arc + a mislabeled interlude

Main arc — Heist, Firestorm, and the Carpet Race (Sep–Nov 2023). The party, a band of mercenaries
raised together by an unnamed “adopted father” benefactor, is hired by Mitch Copperhead to rob a
bank in Lidurithal and kill its doppelganger head of guard, Cadillac. The heist succeeds in
part — the Dyson Dynamo is recovered, but Cadillac escapes — and the party’s own fire magic,
amplified by the soul-charged Dynamo, levels an entire city. The survivors flee as refugees, flying
ahead of the column to Lutathal to enter the Magic Carpet Race, pick up a new party member
(Gang), and draw the attention of a planar law-enforcement agency hunting the Dynamo — ending
session 6 on a fresh cliffhanger as a demon rises through the city streets.
Interlude — Hawthorne and the Tomb of Horrors (session 3), DM’d by Pat. 2023-10-08
is titled “Copperhead the Doppelganger” and slotted into this campaign’s session list, but its content
has nothing to do with the heist arc: it’s run by Pat, not Jake, and follows two entirely different
characters — Jace Gandolfini (Jake) and Sarkhan Vol (Nutty), wizard-professors at Hawthorne
College — setting out after the Tomb of Horrors. No on-mic connection to the main arc exists. Treated
here as a stand-alone interlude rather than invented continuity.

The party (main arc)
Character names and even classes are inconsistently stated across sessions (several PCs are never named
on mic at all); see each PC page’s own “Unresolved” section for specifics.

Pat — Pat’s Wizard, a tiefling wood mage with a prehensile tail; later described as a sorcerer with
a luck-dragon familiar named Randy
Donnie — Colt Hopper, a grippli (frog-folk) gunslinger, later named Donovan; also fields a second
character, the witch Aisling
Connor — Jim Jones (nickname only), a human/cursed Oracle
Rich — Richard Findelberg, an android wizard/crafter
Nutty — Seabreeze, a Strix archer also described as a Druid
Ozan — Frankie, a Paladin/Bard with very high Charisma
Jess — Jess’s Witch, a witch (later revealed to be a changeling) who owns the folding boat Nessie
therealvossi (“Ty”) — Gang, a half-orca bar bouncer recruited into the party in session 6

Timeline

2023-09-12 — Mitch Copperhead hires the party
to rob a bank in Lidurithal and kill Cadillac; they infiltrate the city, dodge the guard, and
enter the bank just as a rival crew tunnels in using giant burrowing creatures — cliffhanger.
2023-10-01 — A three-way vault brawl against Cadillac’s crew;
the party recovers the loot and the Dyson Dynamo, but Cadillac escapes under cover of his own
wizard’s Darkness spell.
2023-10-08 — Interlude, DM’d by Pat: [[Jace
Gandolfini]] and Sarkhan Vol decipher a cursed map and prepare to set out for the Tomb of Horrors.
2023-10-15 — An ambush by Copperhead’s doppelganger caravan
turns into a magical firestorm when the Dynamo mirrors the party’s own fire spell across the city of
Godoy, killing roughly 90% of its population; the party loots the ruins and covers its tracks.
2023-10-24 — The party flees Godoy with the refugee
column, flies ahead to Lutathal to enter the Magic Carpet Race, scries on Cadillac’s purge plans,
and falls out with a carpet-shop sponsor, Greg.
2023-11-28 — Planar investigators from the
TIU confront the party over the Dynamo and mark them as suspects; the party recruits Gang,
bait-and-switches a race carpet, and the session ends as a demon rises through the city streets.

Major threads
Resolved

The bank heist for Mitch Copperhead — bank robbed, Dynamo recovered, though Cadillac escaped
2023-10-01
Copperhead’s doppelganger caravan ambush — caravan killed/burned, Copperhead himself killed
2023-10-15

Dangling / open

Cadillac himself survives, now plotting to purge changelings near the king
2023-10-24
The Dyson Dynamo’s soul-harvesting nature and how the party means to recharge it going forward
Covering up the destruction of Godoy (~90% mortality) — no in-fiction consequences yet
The TIU’s manhunt — the party is now flagged as suspects in the Dynamo’s disappearance
2023-11-28
The Magic Carpet Race (the Rug Mandela) — entered via a bait-and-switch carpet, race not yet run
The demon rising through the city streets — brand-new cliffhanger, completely unresolved
Richard’s indentured servitude to the rug shop, bartered away to avoid paying for a carpet — never
revisited on-mic after session 5
The Tomb of Horrors expedition (interlude) — map deciphered, party preparing to depart; no further
session has picked it back up

Unresolved
Whether session 3’s Hawthorne/Tomb of Horrors content belongs to this campaign at all, or is simply
mislabeled with the “jakedm” slug, is never clarified — it shares no characters, DM, or plot with the
other five sessions. Several locations across the main arc (Lidurithal vs. Godoy) may be the same
city under different transcribed names; see each place page’s own Unresolved section.

campaigns/ravenloft.title: Ravenloft (2022–2023)
campaigns/ravenloft.content:
Ravenloft (2022–2023)
Pat ran the party through the classic 1980s Curse of Strahd/Ravenloft module (confirmed by Pat
OOC as the original 1984 TSR adventure, not the 5e remake)
2023-01-30 @ 05:36:35,
2023-03-18 @ 00:33:00. A mysterious letter and dinner
invitation lure the party into the fogbound land of Barovia, ruled by the vampire lord
Strahd von Zarovich. After one scene-setting session in the village, the remaining seven sessions are
an almost continuous dungeon crawl through Castle Ravenloft itself, with the party never leaving the
castle again.
The recorded campaign ends mid-dungeon, unresolved: Strahd is still alive, one former party member is
lost in the Astral Plane, and the party’s last on-screen action is splitting up to chase a screaming noise
toward a glowing tower. The group’s next recorded sessions move on to a different, unrelated campaign
(JakeDM’s), so it’s unclear from the transcripts whether Ravenloft was ever formally finished or simply
left behind.
The party

Todd (Todd Stone) — played by Nutty — human fighter, dual-shield tank, carries the party’s torches.
The most consistently-named and stable PC across the whole campaign. See Todd Stone.
Jacques Luceau (aliases: Woo-woo, Wu, JB) — played by Jake — a Vanara (monkey-folk) monk, flurry of
blows, later elemental/flaming fists. See Jacques Luceau.
Raven / Donovan — played by Donnie — a human witch with a brain-hungry zoog familiar. Dies near
Strahd’s coffin and rises as his vampire thrall, later revealed to have secretly betrayed the party
before being defeated and lost into the Astral Plane. See Raven.
Xarthax (heard as Zyrtax/Zarthax/Zarafax) — played by Rich — an android arcane caster, immune to
necrotic damage, fear, aging, and mind-affecting effects. Note: session 1 instead describes “Rich’s
character” as an unnamed drow bard and a separate absent “Jeff’s character” as a mage; it’s unclear
whether either is meant to be Xarthax, who appears from session 2 onward. See Xarthax.
Alumbra (heard as: Ulumbra, Alhambra, Olumbra, Lulu) — played by Jess — a ninja/rogue with a katana,
sneak attack, and a handy haversack (later destroyed). See Alumbra.
Ozan’s alchemist (heard as: Zendrick, Lobel, Nadi, “Woo”/“Wubu Tang”) — played by Ozan — an
alchemist/investigator who disables traps, brews potions, and shares them mid-fight. See
Ozan’s Alchemist.

Timeline

2022-12-06 — A shared prophetic nightmare and a forged plea
letter draw the party into the mists around Barovia; they meet Ismark and Irina Indirovich, shelter in
the village church, get a tarot reading from Madame Eva, and arrive at Castle Ravenloft’s doors by
carriage.
2022-12-18 — Strahd greets the party for
dinner and vanishes after being hit with a thrown roll; the party fights skeletons, finds the cursed
Tome of Strahd, and falls through a trap door into a flooded dungeon level.
2022-12-26 — A poison-gas trap gets set on
fire and burns for most of the session; the party meets the pet-murdering armor Bartholomew and Jake
claims a shapeshifting magic sword from the flames.
2023-01-30 — The party invents “piss coat” to bypass warded
bars, clears the catacombs beneath the castle (killing a banshee wife and a vampire bride of Strahd),
learns Strahd’s Tatiana backstory, identifies the Sun Sword’s blade, and loses Donnie’s witch to
vampirism at Strahd’s coffin.
2023-02-12 — Donovan (now a vampire thrall) flees as mist;
the party opens Strahd’s empty coffin and teleports into a brutal boss fight with Strahd himself, who
dominates several PCs before escaping as mist.
2023-03-12 — A riddle-trapped treasure room animates two iron golems;
the party nearly loses Alumbra to poison and a critical fumble before grinding both golems down.
2023-03-18 — Donovan is revealed
to have secretly turned traitor; the party defeats him and a demon, then accidentally flings Donovan
into the Astral Plane while trying to contain his mist form. A later ghost ambush in a dining hall
nearly wipes the party.
2023-03-18 — A short continuation: Todd explores
alone, the party levels to 7 and handles character-build bookkeeping, and the session (and the
campaign’s recorded run) ends early when the battle map breaks.

Major threads
Resolved

The dinner invitation / tarot prophecy — overtaken by events once the party committed to the castle.
The basement’s rumored magic item — the shapeshifting sword, later identified as the Sun Sword’s
blade — 2022-12-26,
2023-01-30.
Petrifying wards guarding Strahd’s crypt — bypassed with “piss coat”
2023-01-30 @ 04:25:30.
The riddle/golem trap room — both golems destroyed
2023-03-12.
Donovan’s betrayal, as a live threat — defeated and removed from play (flung into the Astral Plane)
2023-03-18.

Dangling / open

Kolyan Indirovich’s disappearance and Irina Indirovich’s vampiric bite — never followed up on
once the party moved on to the castle.
The “tool of evil” from Madame Eva’s tarot prophecy — never explicitly identified; possibly the Sun
Sword, but this is never confirmed on-screen.
The Sun Sword’s missing hilt — never recovered.
Strahd von Zarovich himself — still alive and un-fought-to-a-finish as of the last session.
Donovan’s fate in the Astral Plane — had two hours to find a resting place or be destroyed
forever; never resolved on-screen.
The stolen copy of the Tome of Strahd — taken by a group of ghosts who captured (rather than killed)
the party; never recovered.
The tower with the pulsing red glass “heart” — discovered but unexplored at the very end of the
campaign’s recorded run.

Unresolved
Whether this campaign was ever actually finished, abandoned, or picked up again off-mic is not something
the transcripts say — the recorded sessions simply stop here and the group’s next recorded games are a
different campaign (JakeDM’s).

campaigns/the-gang.title: The Gang (2019–2021)
campaigns/the-gang.content:
The Gang (2019–2021)
A long-running, free-wheeling homebrew campaign DM’d by Pat, running from October 2019 through at least
November 2021 (the latest recorded session). The table calls it simply “the campaign” — “The Gang” is
this wiki’s label for it. Tonally it swings from dungeon-crawl pulp (pyramids, sphinxes, golems) to
cosmic/planar horror (the Abyss, the Nexus, Lovecraftian artifacts) to outright slapstick (urination as
a puzzle solution, a hat that renames people “Steve”). Pat has stated at the table that the party has
previously fought in an Orc War, run a casino heist, killed a lich, and been trapped in a Titan’s pocket
“fish tank” universe — all backstory from before this wiki’s transcript coverage begins.
Across its recorded span the party acquires, loses, or gets stuck with a long chain of reality-bending
artifacts (a planeshifting ship, the Apocalypse Box, a Ring of the Hive Mind, a newborn god),
gets yanked into the Abyss and back out, and survives several player-character deaths — almost always,
per Pat’s own observation, “from a cursed item turning players against each other,” not from monsters
2020-03-24 @ 03:23:59.
Shape of the campaign: two arcs + an interlude
Character names, classes, and even species change substantially over the recorded timespan, with real
gaps of months between sessions. This wiki splits the record into two loose arcs plus one outlier
one-shot, rather than assume continuity the transcripts don’t support:

Arc I — The Ship (Oct 2019 – Apr 2020). The party raids a pyramid, steals a mage’s
planeshifting/blood-fueled ship, gets dragged through the Abyss, Hell, and the Feywild, and ends up
raising a newborn god. Core cast: Tick-Tick (Jake), Mori Yoshinari (Donnie, the ship’s
captain), Dread Pirate Bobbert (Rich), Ozan’s bard/fey character (see Kurt Furbane), and
Nutty’s healer (unexpectedly possessed by a demon for several sessions).
Interlude — The Kidnap Job (Sep 2020), DM’d by Ozan. A single one-shot heist session with an
entirely different cast of goblins and a dwarf monk, run by Ozan instead of Pat while Pat played a
PC. See 2020-09-28. Not clearly connected to either
main arc; treated here as a stand-alone interlude.
Arc II — The Nexus (Oct–Nov 2021). After an ~18-month real-world gap, the party (now playing
Alexander, Fish, Miss Cleo, Nutty’s fire sorcerer, and Jess’s magus) is deep in an
unrelated-looking cult/portal-hopping plot that ends with them trapped in a planar prison called
the Nexus. Whether/how this connects to Arc I is never stated in the transcripts.

The party (by arc)
Arc I

Jake — Tick-Tick, later Paladin of Pelor; earlier an unnamed earth-gliding shapeshifter in the
pyramid session
Donnie — Mori Yoshinari / Donovan, the ship’s captain, bonded to an enslaved air elemental
Rich — Dread Pirate Bobbert, wizard
Ozan — bard/fey performer, see Kurt Furbane; killed and True-Resurrected mid-arc
Nutty — healer/alchemist, unknowingly possessed by a demon for several sessions
Ryan (Rawntrail) — Obadiah Jones, Loxodon cleric, joins partway through

Arc II

Jake — Alexander, android
Donnie — Fish (Donovan), alchemist; piloted by Rich when Donnie was absent
Rich — his own unnamed tank/healer character, and stand-in pilot for Fish
Ozan — Miss Cleo
Nutty — fire sorcerer, “the character formerly known as Ari”
Jess — unnamed elf magus/dhampir with a bat familiar

Timeline

2019-10-15 — The party fights through the
pyramid’s “Tests of the Pharaoh,” destroys clay golems, and is ambushed by shadow-doubles of
themselves before a half-finished boss fight against an awakened, staff-wielding figure.
2020-01-20 — Looting the dead mage’s ship,
the party accidentally triggers its plane-shift crystal, strands itself on a new continent, and has
an air elemental permanently bound to the ship so it can fly.
2020-01-28 — Shopping, scrying a hunter-paladin, and a
doomed feast in an isolated mountain village end with the ship accidentally yanked into the Abyss.
2020-03-16 — A Whimsy Wall roll conjures the
Apocalypse Box, which curses Jake to carry and (daily) risk opening it.
2020-03-24 — A demon secretly possessing
Nutty kills Ozan and then Jake; Jake dies and is reborn a Paladin of Pelor, lifting the box’s curse.
2020-03-25 — The party finally escapes Hell/the Abyss via the
ship, after a side-dungeon demon fight, and lands (not quite safely) in the Feywild instead of home.
2020-04-06 — Trapped in an escalating monster
trial, the party frees a frozen Loxodon cleric (Obadiah Jones) while a demon drags Jake into the
Ethereal Plane.
2020-04-13 — The party adopts a newborn god, then kills a
glabrezu demon disguised as a paladin mid-knighting-ceremony, leveling to 12.
2020-09-28 — One-shot interlude, Ozan DMing: the
party (as goblins and a dwarf monk) infiltrates a mansion banquet to kidnap a goblin, Littlepen.
2021-10-19 — A talking Sphinx painting’s riddles open
the way into a Nexus-portal complex; the party scouts and steps through into a frozen plane.
2021-11-02 — The party fights free of a frost
giant and golems on the frozen plane, loots a haul of magic items, and learns they’re trapped in a
planar prison called the Nexus, with no way back.

Major threads
Resolved

Escaping Hell/the Abyss with the ship — 2020-03-25
The Apocalypse Box’s compulsion curse on Jake (lifted when he died and was reborn a Paladin) —
2020-03-24
The demon possessing Nutty — banished the same session
Ozan’s death and True Resurrection — died 2020-03-24, confirmed alive again by 2020-04-06
The kidnapping of Littlepen — 2020-09-28

Dangling / open

The Apocalypse Box itself was never destroyed, only stopped being Jake’s problem
The green death-bubble sealing the Isle of Death, and the lich it may be tied to
The freed djinn the party keeps failing to locate/scry
The Church of St. Cuthbert’s manhunt for Mori Yoshinari
The newborn god-baby’s upbringing and future religion
Jake’s interrupted duel to the death at Clydewell
The miasma death-cloud and the never-found “Miasmic Cloud Monitoring Agency”
The Grimson Knights cult and “Brother Felhorn”
Escaping the Nexus — the campaign’s last recorded session ends on this cliffhanger

Unresolved
The exact relationship between Arc I and Arc II — whether Arc II’s cast are new characters in a new
campaign thread, or a direct continuation nobody explained on-mic — is never stated in the transcripts.
A reader submission to Rugby’s Roaming Gazette by “Dr. Boom,” a rat and war veteran, published
2019-04-22 (before any recorded session — the first is 2019-10-15), describes joining a small merchant
boat crewed by a cat captain and a druid searching for a lost dinosaur, capturing a pirate ship and
freeing two prisoners (one “the true embodiment of chaos,” the other rapidly “plunged into evil
acts”), and selling a stolen drug shipment for gold at a pirate town 2019-04-22. This reads
like it could be an in-world account of the party’s own early, unrecorded adventures from the era this
page describes as “backstory from before this wiki’s transcript coverage begins” — but no PC or NPC on
this wiki matches the rat, the cat captain, or the druid, and no session confirms or denies it. Recorded
as a possible but unconfirmed parallel, not an identification.

factions/aspis-corporation.title: Aspis Corporation
factions/aspis-corporation.content:
Also heard as: Aspis Consortium
A faction providing security and guests for a lavish mansion banquet in the one-shot kidnap job session;
likely the table’s name for the Pathfinder Society’s “Aspis Consortium.” Hostile to the party after the
kidnapping.
History

Hosts/attends the banquet where Littlepen is a guest
2020-09-28 @ 00:08:48.
An Aspis Corporation guard engages the fleeing party during the kidnapping’s getaway, landing hard hits
on Jake, Donnie, and Rich 2020-09-28 @ 02:27:01.

factions/college-of-turgeth.title: College of Turgeth
factions/college-of-turgeth.content:
A magic college in Turgeth specializing in aberration and self-protection magic, likened to “Notre
Dame” and said to exist on every continent. Secretly the true source of the drug Maka.
History

Riggs’s Widow reveals the college secretly supplies Maka, worth ~75,000 gp/week
2025-03-31 @ 00:24:08-00:24:19, @ 00:25:03.
Jake establishes its specialty as aberration/self-protection magic
2025-03-31 @ 00:32:02-00:32:34.

DM notes (spoiler)
The college’s drug pipeline is confirmed by Jake as true (not a prisoner’s lie), but the party has not
yet investigated it directly — see College of Turgeth Drug Pipeline.

factions/grimson-knights.title: Grimson Knights
factions/grimson-knights.content:
Also heard as: Brimson Knights
A cult whose abandoned underground complex the party explores in Arc II, found via red robes, a ledger of
cult expenses, and desiccated bodies with their hearts magically removed. Planning a ritual gathering to
welcome a new lord, Brother Felhorn.
History

The party finds the cult’s hastily-abandoned living quarters, robes, and a ledger of expenses
2021-10-19 @ 00:07:22–00:09:24.
A recovered note announces a ritual gathering in a graveyard under the next full moon to welcome “our
new lord and life, Brother Felhorn” 2021-10-19 @ 00:14:57.
Several desiccated, heart-removed bodies are found preserved rather than killed violently, implying
ritual victims 2021-10-19 @ 00:18:33.

Unresolved
The cult members themselves and Brother Felhorn are never found or confronted in the recorded sessions.

factions/tiu.title: TIU
factions/tiu.content:
A planar law-enforcement organization out of the city of Chrome, whose agents astral-project rather than
travel physically. Hunting the Dyson Dynamo and now the party, whom it has marked as suspects.
History

Investigators Thornshade and Iron Soul confront the party over the Dyson Dynamo, warning it “could
unravel the fabric of reality” 2023-11-28
@ 00:37:54–00:38:31.
Thornshade is defeated in a brawl with Gang, shows his real badge, and explains the Dynamo harvests
souls @ 01:01:49–01:12:08.
Marks the party as suspects regardless of Donnie’s bluff denying any knowledge of the Dynamo, then
leaves after a gold-compensation offer is rebuffed @ 00:39:10–00:40:15, @ 01:14:51–01:18:33.

Unresolved
Thornshade vows to return; no later session has done so yet.

factions/the-agency.title: The Agency
factions/the-agency.content:
A group of space-time-crime investigators founded by Dr. E Brown, centered entirely on the
flagged 4900-paradox issue — see timeline. Never mentioned again in any other issue.
History

Investigates “crimes against space-time” tied to a major event the group calls “Day Zero,” believed
to be rippling through and reshaping the multiverse; sends agents backward in time on one-way
missions to “course-correct” history 2019-05-12.

Unresolved
Appears only in the issue dated APRIL 17 4900 — fifteen years after the surrounding issues’
in-world 4885 setting. The very next issue in publication order reverts to 4885 and continues the
ongoing war coverage as though the 4900 issue never happened; no later issue references The Agency,
Dr. E Brown, or Day Zero again.

factions/the-changeling-nation.title: The Changeling Nation
factions/the-changeling-nation.content:
Also heard as: The Changelings
A doppelganger-run political faction that takes over the country of Cacoal and, after the
Binneth–Squiyles war, the majority of fallen Squiyles itself — ruling “with an
iron fist” and hosting (then sabotaging) an international peace summit.
History

Early infiltration panic in Ezaso City is publicly denied by Captain Tartan and the king, who
attribute strange behavior to “flu” 2019-04-01, 2019-04-09.
The country of Cacoal is fully overrun and self-declares the “Changeling Nation,” seeking
recognition as a sovereign nation and closing itself to outsiders; former resident Gerard Twombly
objects publicly, and King Stroth makes no statement 2019-07-15.
After Squiyles’ collapse, changelings take over rulership of the majority of its former territory
2019-10-07, continuing to rule “with an iron fist” into the post-war years
2022-12-18, 2022-12-26.
Hosts an international peace conference in the former Squiylian capital, inviting representatives
from Hawkthorne, Gaithyre, McCathlyre, and Turgythe, in a bid for diplomatic legitimacy and
stability 2022-12-18.
The summit collapses into chaos and violence when several changeling delegates are revealed to have
used their shapeshifting to infiltrate the conference disguised as other nations’ own rulers and
diplomats, trying to influence the proceedings from within; the scandal leaves other nations’
leaders humiliated and relations between empires uncertain 2022-12-26.

gazette/2019-04-01.title: 2019-04-01 · Gazette, April 1 4885
gazette/2019-04-01.content:
In the news: places/Ezaso City, Cacoal, places/Isle of Torta,
npcs/Hammond Hardle, npcs/H.G. Higgins, npcs/Captain Tartan, npcs/Rex Sauvage,
Desna, places/Somic City
Astronomists Puzzled
Stars continue to disappear from the sky! Is the end coming?! Omen or Explainable Phenomenon?
“Unexplainable” “Preposterous” “Undeniable”
These are the things you hear outside the Astronomy Summit this last weekend in Ezaso, the Capital city of Cacoal.
Interviews with various attendees ended with more questions than answers. No one seems to be able to explain the strange disappearances of the stars. Many are worried of the coming of the great black sky. Worried that eventually they may all just go out!
“Everyone needs to just calm down” Says Hammond Hardle, The Royal Astronomer and Astrologist to the king of Binneth. Who believes this is a message from the gods. When we asked what the message was we didn’t receive a comment from Mr. Hardle. Whatever the cause, it sure is causing a buzz throughout the land!
BLUE DRAGON WREAKS HAVOC
Manufacturing mages demand wage increases!
Multiple reports! Detailed accounts of the beast!
ON THE RISE
Longer hours and faster output requirements have blue collar conjuration mages sacrificing weekends and holidays to meet consumeristic demands without fair compensation. “The amount of gold they pay is ridiculous!” Says one local magic laborer “How am I supposed to support my family?”
Concerns rising as outsourcing manufacturing to other dimensional planes gains popularity.
TERRIFYING!
Stories keep coming in! Blue light dazzled and amazed onlookers (Those who weren’t instantly vaporized by the monsters blast). Nearby royal guards of the Kingdom of Binneth say “Good Riddance!” as the attack happened on the remote island of Torta, an area of contention between local officials and the many criminal organizations that frequent it. More sightings reported as the beast seems to be moving inland from the island toward populated cities and towns.
Caption: Artists rendition of the attack. Drawing by H.G. Higgins
DOPPELGANGERS INFILTRATE EZASO CITY
Captain of the guard issues call to arms!
SHAPESHIFTING MENACE
Numerous reports involving loved ones acting strange and visual reports of shapeshifting has led Captain Tartan of the Ezaso City Guard to make an announcement last week calling attention to the crisis. And advising the locals to “Trust No-one”. We requested an interview for more information. Captain Tartan will be interviewing with us later in the week. More details on this hopefully to come in next week’s issue!
FIELD REPORT
From the journal of the daring Rex Sauvage!
Caption: Rex Sauvage
AT IT AGAIN!
I barely escaped with my life, the darkness was approaching fast. I was dangling from the edge of a cliff about to strike the group of lizard-men that had been ravaging the locals. They spotted me! “En Garde!” I yelled as I flipped down from my perch sword at the ready!
One, two, three flicks of the wrist and half of them were dispatched. Stab, twist, dodge! Parry! The other half downed as well! Just one left. Their leader was a slight challenge for a swordsman as skilled as I. I dove right, he dove left, I jumped on his covered wagon, he smacked the horses to scare them, attempting to knock me off. No such luck! I’m as nimble as I am handsome! I landed easily and brought my sword up to his with a loud CLANG! Twist of the wrist, and my steel found his heart.
In the end he proved to be no match for…
…Rex Sauvage.

Whether it’s just a scratch or a full on limb regeneration, we’ve got you covered!
Come on down to the church of Desna! Our clerics are ready to help you get back in the action!

gazette/2019-04-09.content:
In the news: Bostur, Gorthak, places/Kingdom of Squiyles,
npcs/King Stroth, npcs/Captain Tartan, npcs/Rex Sauvage, npcs/H.G. Higgins,
places/Somic City
TROUBLES IN THE EAST!
City of Bostur Overthrown as Nayesche Orc tribe incursion continues!
Tribal land disputes took a bloody turn this week.
The Kingdom of Squiyles has long been in land disputes with the Nayesche Orcish barbarian tribe that claim the kingdom “Over reaches their rule”.
Reports keep pouring in regarding Bloody Tuesday. The name coined for the events that took place. Here’s what we know:
Duke Harrington of Squiyles’ head was ceremoniously “rolled and kicked” through Bostur City after City hall was attacked by the Nayesche warriors. City hall was razed to the ground. Plans for an Orcish conquest-hall are underway to take its place.
“All who place a claim our lands will join the Duke in the underworld” Say’s Garthok [no surname]. When we asked Garthok for an interview he proclaimed dominance over the earth, while feasting on the remains of the locals.
Caption: Portrait of Gorthuk [no surname], courtesy of Theon Thrivent [survivor]
Our on site representative left the field shortly there after and we were unable to get additional interviews. The Tribal leaders also let us know to “Spread the word of our conquests!” and to let our readers know that “No one is safe!”.
Red Dragon of Stroth Castle Escapes
It just gets wilder folks! There are now TWO beasts on the loose!
TWO DRAGONS!
A hole in the southern side of the King Stroth’s castle in Squiyles was opened by a bolt of lighting this week from the dragon release from the Isle of Torta!
Inside a second dragon being held captive by the king was released. In an impressive show of fire and lightning, over half the castle was destroyed! Royal evacuations began during the chaos to get the king and the royal council to safety as the royal army scrambled together to defend against this surprise attack.
By morning only 20% of the army is reported to have survived the ordeal.
Caption: Two dragons reported attacking Stroth Castle. Drawing by H.G. Higgins
CAPTAIN CALLS FOR CALM
Captain of the guard says doppelganger threat “over exaggerated”
NOTHING TO WORRY ABOUT
“Disregard everything you been hearing” says Captain Tartan “Things have been a little crazy lately but that’s mostly been attributed by some kind of flu going around”.
He made this statement tuesday morning addressing the public, accompanied by the full regiment of the city guard.
The King has backed up the Captains announcement with a similar announcement asking for the public to “go about their business” and “stop bringing this up” as well as “If I even hear the word doppelganger spoken to me again I’ll throw you in the dungeons”. It seems all is back to normal is Ezaso City.
FIELD REPORT
From the journal of the daring Rex Sauvage!
A MAN OF ACTION
Caption: Rex Sauvage
I received word from king Fashim Thoronor directly, He and I are good friends you see, that their kingdom was in peril!
At once I flew to the kingdom to aid them in their time of need. Riding my trusty Griffin Sterling, we soared through the skys. To my surprise I was ambushed by a band of murderous harpies! What cowards to attack in such a large group! No matter. I jumped from Sterlings back and drew my sword! Swish, Swosh, Stab! One after the other I sunk my blade into their bodies. One by one they started falling to the earth! I kicked off the final one and shealthed my sword as I was diving toward the ground.
All four were dispatched during my decent! Sterling was quick to swoop under me and back in the saddle I was! To continue on towards the kingdom of Turgyth!
Just a day in the life of…
…Rex Savauge

435 counts elven trafficking
Simultaneous operation of numerous diamond mines
Organ harvesting

Duke Harrington of Squiyles was killed during the Bostur attack; his head was paraded through Bostur City.
Bostur’s City Hall was destroyed by the Nayesche warriors; an Orcish “conquest-hall” is being built in its place.
Garthok (no surname) is a Nayesche Orc leader/spokesperson who claimed dominance over the land and that locals were being eaten.
Gorthuk (no surname) is another named Nayesche Orc, pictured in a portrait courtesy of survivor Theon Thrivent — note the paper spells this orc’s name both “Gorthuk” (portrait caption) and “Garthok” (body text), likely the same figure.
A hole was blasted in the south side of King Stroth’s castle in Squiyles by a bolt of lightning, releasing a dragon that had escaped from the Isle of Torta.
A second, captive dragon held by King Stroth was released during the ensuing chaos; over half of Stroth Castle was destroyed by fire and lightning.
Only 20% of King Stroth’s royal army reportedly survived the dragon attack on the castle.

AIRSHIP RACE
Do you have what it takes to take first place!
OPEN INVITE. Racers from around the globe are gathering at Laudir in the Kingdom of Squiyles for the annual airship races!
Do you have the mustard? Be it crew-man or captain, thousands are gathering. The route will take racers west off the peninsula leaving Laudir and heading toward the skies of Victrum, over the surrounding islands and onward toward Tredexum where the race will end.
“We’ve been training for this race all year” Say’s local air captain Reginald Woolrick. Ever since last years explosion officials have been doing more and more inspections into the safety of the event as well as the onlookers.
Since the race takes place mostly over the ocean there is limited risk of spectators getting injured.
Foul play was suspected last year however.
According to investigators there wasn’t hard evidence to support the allegations being thrown around.
Either way it’s surely going to be another great race! Rugby’s Gazette with be on the scene to report the action!
COULD WAR BE ON THE HORIZON?
Yearly alliance meeting gets heated as King Stroth loses temper.
PEACE? OR WAR!
An argument broke out during the annual meeting of the kingdoms of Binneth and Squiyles yesterday. “King Stroth is usually very reasonable” said city negotiations host Brennen Ragard. Shortly after the annual land and trade negotiations began, King Stroth grabbed hold of King Tygard and dangled him over the edge of the meeting hall 3rd story window and was reported screaming a litany of insults at the man.. “It was tense” said onlookers. The meeting came to an abrupt halt as threats for war were overheard being thrown around during the exit of both royal parties.
Caption: Near Defenestration of King Tygard. Illustration by H.G. Higgins
FIELD REPORT
From the journal of the amazing Rex Sauvage!
ELECTRIC BEAST
I awoke in the middle of the night to an odd sound… But one I’d heard before. You could smell the air was electric, an energy was crackling outside my tent.
Who would be foolish enough to attempt to ambush me? Rex Sauvage! My armor was off but no matter. I grabbed my trusty sword and dove outside the tent. A gigantic thunder wolf tore into the tent at that same moment. Electricity crackled from its fangs as it turned its head toward me. It leaped, I dodged, It bore its mammoth paws into the ground and lunged at me again. I flipped backward and barely escaped his powerful jaws.
As the beast stood there growling and teeth showing, there was a glint in his eyes. I’d seen this before. I dug my sword deep into the ground and held it tightly. The beast let out a howl, and with it a storm followed. Winds powerful enough to sink ships came out of the beast’s maw.
The strain to hold onto my sword was tremendous, but I held fast. The winds that came howling from the beast were followed by a thunderous clap that destroyed the tree’s around me. The moment the beast let up for breath I struck. Before a second had past I was already standing behind him with his blood on my blade. One strike was all it took from…
Rex Sauvage.
Caption: Rex Sauvage
ORCISH INCURSION CONTINUES
City of Kafka Falls to Orcish Warriors. Local farmers stood no chance.
ORCS DEMAND MORE LAND
The march continues as the Orcs from the East work their way slowly into the belly of the kingdom. Agriculture hub and one of the largest potato exporters, Kafka, attacked invaded and enslaved. By Garthok’s army.
“There is no royal protection presence in Kafka. Lending to its ease of defeat” says war-time strategist Martin Graybeard. “I would recommend families who live in nearby cities to either evacuate to a neighboring territory or prepare for the incoming attack. The royal army is a powerful force but it takes time for a king to amass an army and coordinate an attack. And in that time a lot can happen. I fear the worst for many of those in the warpath.”

gazette/2019-04-22.content:
In the news: places/Thorhofn City, npcs/King Stroth, npcs/Rex Sauvage,
places/Ezaso City, Gorthak, npcs/Dr. Boom, the-gang,
places/Kingdom of Squiyles
MORE HELLFIRE
A third dragons joins the furious dragon attacks!
It was a hard day for the people of Thorhofn today. Tadmenroe Cathedral was set ablaze by three dragons in the early hours of the morning. The cathedral had been under renovations, and therefore no one was injured in the attack.
Witnesses claim to have seen the red blue and green dragon’s responsible for the attack flying east out of the city shortly thereafter.
“So much vibrant history lost” Says head cleric Morin Claust. “These vile beasts desecrate our places of worship!” “May the gods cut their wings and spill their blood!”
It was truly a hard sight to see. The 700 year old church had been an iconic holy place for many followers from all different races and walks of life. Many people would take pilgrimages to this holy place. In hopes to get closer to the heavens.
Caption: (photograph of a cathedral spire burning, a dragon overhead)
ROYAL ARMY CALLS FOR DRAFT
For the first time in 90 years a royal draft begins
PREPARE FOR WAR
King Stroth of Squiyles has declared a military draft today. This marks the first time a draft has been instituted since his grandfather ruled 90 years ago, which took place during the war of the falling moon.
Punishments for those attempting to dodge the draft are rumored to be severe. Weapons and armor manufacturing labor camps have been reported under construction. Many are concerned of the economic and political ramifications this will have on the kingdom as it gears up to support a larger military force.
BY ROYAL DECREE
April 12, 4885 a draft is hereby declared by King Stroth of Squiyles
Every able-bodied male citizen of the kingdom shall report to local city council or active military command wherein a judgement for royal draft eligibility will be assessed. Failure to report will be a punishable offence
FIELD REPORT
From the journal of the dashing Rex Sauvage!
ENCHANTED EYE
I was en route in one of my many formal garments to the Hawkthorne Royal Gala. Only the most influential individuals of our time attend these sorts of gatherings. on my way there I noticed the driver of my carriage seemed out of place.
The man quickly turned on me! halting the carriage and attempting to wrestle his way into the back with me. He wore an eye patch and lifted it to reveal an enchanted glass eye! He looked right into my soul and being with it and it took every ounce of my energy to resist the magic from within it. I could tell he was attempting to take control of me with it! My will was too strong for him and I snapped out of it.
With a flurry of well placed attacks I resolved the threat. I tied him up for the local guard to take care of, Back on my way to rub elbows with the elite.
Just another evening with…
…Rex Sauvage
CHILDREN SLAIN IN MARKET
“Howled until blood spilled from the ears of children”
MURDER IN THE STREETS
Normally street urchins getting cut down in the streets isn’t exactly news-worthy. What makes this story so interesting is the manner in which it happened. An Orcish man 6’ tall with blue tinted skin wearing a brutal wooden mask with horrid images carved into it reportedly “Vomited swarms of spiders” and “Howled until blood spilled from the ears of children”
Not kidding folks. Some very strange stuff is going on in Ezaso.
Could This be a member of Gorthok’s Army? Something even more sinister?? Either way, If you have any information regarding this individual report it to the Royal Guards of Squiyles. According to officials as he is also a suspect in another case.
Ad: Shoot and Lute
Family owned and operated since 4867
Located in Wares District, Thorhofn City, Kingdom of Binneth
Ad: Daniels Extra-Dimensional Delights
Custom made extra-dimensional spaces of any kind. Only your imagination is the limit.
Located in Wares District, Thorhofn City, Kingdom of Binneth
FIELD JOURNALIST SUBMISSION
Submitted by Dr. Boom
CHAOS FOLLOWS
It was this time about two years ago that I faced the biggest bloodshed of my life. You understand that you’re signing up for bloodshed when you join the military. Not loss, though. Friends lost in battle bear heavy weight even as memories of bloodshed fade.
I went to Rickety Squibs to see good friend’s family. The war was “over” (hah!) and us soldiers had to waltz right back into daily life, so before I got on the first boat that’d pay me, I wanted to share my grief for a moment.
It was in Squibs where this whole situation started. I got on a boat along with some druid searching for a lost dinosaur, small fry “merchant” boat with a good professional captain (he was a cat and didn’t make much fuss about me being a rat) and a decent crew.
We were on our way to make a shipment when some rookie-ass pirates attempted to board our ship. Once they realized our… explosive… potential, I asked them consider whether it would be best if they drop their arms and hand over their ship, they thought that sounded like a reasonable exchange for their lives. They, as well as their two prisoners joined our crew and we set off to finish what they started but got distracted away from: delivering a drug shipment to a pirate town.
At this point, one of you dear readers will realize: “Oh shit, that’s the crew who stole my boat and my shipment.” To which I say: “You’re the one who made the mistake of hiring a shit crew to do a basic task. Get over it and do better next time.”
We converted our new-found drugs found in our new-found boat into cold hard gold, over at that one pirate town with the tree. Everything was going pretty swimmingly at the time, in terms of how I would imagine my career would go: I’ve gotten surprisingly far so fast in the last two weeks. From deckhand to counting gold by weight is not bad.
It turns out chaos has other plans for me besides gold and fortune, however. For example, it turns out the two prisoners we freed from the pirates may have had good reason to be locked up. I won’t go into details, but one is the true embodiment of chaos and the other has rapidly plunged into evil acts. Frankly, they’re not even my main concern right now, for reasons I will go into at a later time. Until then, I’ll leave you with a human spiritual song:
(The submission closes with several verses of the spiritual “Sinner Man” — “So I run to the Lord…” / “Ran to the devil, he was waiting…” — not reproduced here; see the page image.)
RUGBY’S GAZETTE PAYS FOR ARTICLES
We are always looking for article submissions from in the field journalists here at Rugby’s ◆ investigative ◆ action-packed field reports ◆ entertainment ◆ interviews with the famous
Mail articles to Rugby’s Gazette, Conopimalis, Erepec, Kingdom of Squiyles
Canon facts

This issue is dated APRIL 12 4885 (in-world) and was published in Conopimalis, Erepec, Kingdom of Squiyles (the 2019-04-01 issue said Kingdom of Binneth).
Three dragons — red, blue and green — burned Tadmenroe Cathedral in Thorhofn in the early morning; no one was injured because it was under renovation. The dragons flew east afterwards. “A third dragon joins” the attacks (cf. the blue dragon at Torta, 2019-04-01).
Tadmenroe Cathedral was a 700-year-old pilgrimage church; its head cleric is Morin Claust.
King Stroth of Squiyles declared a royal military draft on April 12, 4885 — the first in 90 years, since his grandfather’s reign during the War of the Falling Moon. Every able-bodied male citizen must report; draft-dodging is punishable. Rumoured weapons and armor labor camps are being built.
Rex Sauvage, on the way to the Hawkthorne Royal Gala, was attacked by his carriage driver, who used an enchanted glass eye (under an eye patch) to try to dominate him; Rex resisted and handed him to the local guard.
In Ezaso, street children were killed in a market by a 6-foot orcish man with blue-tinted skin and a carved wooden mask, who reportedly vomited swarms of spiders and howled until children’s ears bled. Speculation (rumour): a member of Gorthok’s Army. He is wanted by the Royal Guards of Squiyles and is a suspect in another case.
Ads: “Shoot and Lute” (family-owned since 4867) and “Daniels Extra-Dimensional Delights” (custom extra-dimensional spaces), both in the Wares District of Thorhofn City, Kingdom of Binneth.
Reader submission by “Dr. Boom”, a rat and a war veteran (“about two years ago”): after visiting Rickety Squibs, he joined a small merchant boat with a cat captain and a druid searching for a lost dinosaur; they captured a pirate ship (taking on its crew and two prisoners), and sold a stolen drug shipment for gold at “that one pirate town with the tree”. One freed prisoner is “the true embodiment of chaos”, the other “has rapidly plunged into evil acts”. This reads as an in-world account of the party’s own early adventures.
