2023-03-18 @ 00:34:16–00:35:05.

Unresolved
The book is never recovered after being stolen by the ghosts; its torn-out pages are never found or
explained.

items/wand-of-memory-lapse.title: Wand of Memory Lapse
items/wand-of-memory-lapse.content:
Pat’s wand; forces a DC 17 Will save to erase a target’s recent memory. Gained: already owned at the
start of episode 1. Used: twice on Mary to erase an awkward encounter.
History

Used twice on Mary: once to erase her memory of a gangbang-joke misunderstanding at her door, once
again after Connor insults her 2023-09-12
@ 02:56:41, @ 03:06:06.

items/whoop-whoop-whistle.title: Whoop Whoop Whistle
items/whoop-whoop-whistle.content:
Ozone’s magic item: a whistle with a knockout effect plus 1d4 lightning damage.
History

Jake reminds Ozan the item exists, having been forgotten about
2025-03-31 @ 01:29:47-01:30:04.

DM notes (spoiler)
Jake plans to “remix” this item’s mechanics after the session
2025-03-31 @ 03:19:44.

npcs/andrew.title: Andrew
npcs/andrew.content:
A sphinx-like winged creature encountered alone by Rich in a hidden underwater chamber inside the pyramid,
offering to answer a question about the temple if Rich could solve a riddle.
History

Meets Rich after his rope snaps and sweeps him into a hidden chamber; offers a classic
truth-teller/liar riddle in exchange for answering a question about the temple
2019-10-15 @ 01:13:40.
Rich stalls and ultimately swims back against the current without answering
2019-10-15 @ 01:21:10.

Unresolved
Andrew is never seen again in the recorded sessions; whatever he knew about the temple was never learned.

npcs/bartholomew.title: Bartholomew
npcs/bartholomew.content:
Also heard as: Spirit Armor
A sentient, multi-personality suit of full plate armor found guarding a dusty servant’s-entrance room in
Castle Ravenloft. Documented in-world as “full plate armor of pet murder by committee” — each piece of
plate carries a different alignment, with only one personality active at a time. Hunts and electrocutes
pets, but can be talked down rather than fought.
History

Encountered by the party, alternating between a murderous “pet murder by committee” persona and a posh,
amnesiac one; claims to have blacked out roughly 25 years ago after being arrested for killing a snake
in a town 2022-12-26 @ 02:09:05–02:20:25.
Identified via Knowledge (Arcana) as “full plate armor of pet murder by committee”
2022-12-26 @ 02:16:56.
Talked down by the party rather than fought; relationship left non-hostile
2022-12-26 @ 02:20:52.

DM notes (spoiler)
Bartholomew’s backstory was given directly to the players in-character, but its truth and significance to
the wider plot was never confirmed by the DM
2022-12-26 @ 02:19:07–02:20:25.

npcs/cadillac.title: Cadillac
npcs/cadillac.content:
Also heard as: Cadillac Daddy-O, Cadillac Huggins
A fox-person crime boss and the city’s head guard, confirmed a doppelganger; marked kill-on-sight by
Mitch Copperhead for the bank job, but survives every encounter with the party so far. Leads a gang
marked with a green bee insignia. Rugby’s Roaming Gazette, unaware of any of this, names him “Captain
Cadillac Huggins” and praises him as a dedicated hero of Godoy’s police force.
History


Named kill-on-sight target of the heist by Mitch Copperhead, who first describes him as the city’s
head guard and a doppelganger 2023-09-12 @ 02:16:04;
later confirmed a doppelganger/changeling by Mary @ 03:02:24.


Leads his own crew looting the bank vault ahead of the party; grapples and nearly captures Pat; counters
his Magic Missile via an ally mage; kills his own unconscious ally “Big Sleepy” with an opportunistic
attack; escapes under cover of his own wizard’s Darkness spell
2023-10-01 @ 01:18:33, @ 02:49:08, @ 04:12:40.


Scried on by Pat for seven minutes; shown privately planning to purge and re-vet changelings near the
king now that most of Godoy’s changeling population is dead; his mage group’s sigil matches the
Lutathal city guards’ 2023-10-24 @ 00:49:09–00:54:54,
@ 01:25:59.


The Gazette, dated DEC 19 4885 — before Godoy’s destruction, which it never anticipates — names
“Captain Cadillac Huggins” as a revered officer safeguarding the city and its bank amid a guard
shortage caused by an overly strict vetting process 2023-09-24. See Godoy.


Unresolved
Whether the fox-person seen arguing with bank tellers early in episode 2 is Cadillac himself or a
separate NPC/Fish’s character is ambiguous in the transcript
2023-10-01 @ 00:20:15.
The Gazette’s puff-piece framing of “Captain Cadillac Huggins” as a dedicated hero directly
contradicts his reality from the sessions — a doppelganger crime boss who grapples and nearly
captures a party member, murders his own unconscious ally, and escapes under cover of darkness. The
paper simply doesn’t know what he is. Recorded here as dramatic irony, not resolved one way or the
other 2023-09-24.

npcs/captain-hoolihan.title: Captain Hoolihan
npcs/captain-hoolihan.content:
Leader of the Kingdom of Squiyles’ Wizard Special Forces air unit.
History

Leads Squiyles’ wizard special forces in fireball attacks against Binneth’s navy from the skies,
burning ship after ship, though Binneth’s navy still outnumbers Squiyles’ fleet
2019-06-24.

npcs/captain-jamal.title: Captain Jamal
npcs/captain-jamal.content:
A widely known pirate captain who claims The Free Islands as an open pirate haven.
History

Claims the sparsely inhabited island chain south of McCathlyre, dubs it “The Free
Islands”/“The Free Isles,” and places an open invitation for pirates to settle and help defend it
2019-04-29.

npcs/captain-tartan.title: Captain Tartan
npcs/captain-tartan.content:
Captain of the Ezaso City Guard, first to publicly flag — then publicly deny — a doppelganger
infiltration crisis.
History

Issues a public call to arms over shapeshifting-menace reports, warning Ezaso residents to “Trust
No-one” 2019-04-01.
A week later, backed by the King, reverses course entirely, dismissing the doppelganger threat as
“over exaggerated” and attributing recent strange behavior to “some kind of flu going around”
2019-04-09.

npcs/corbin-strange.title: Corbin Strange
npcs/corbin-strange.content:
An exotic monsters and animals expert who consults for Rugby’s Roaming Gazette.
History

Theorizes that the dragons’ apparent pattern of burning churches of St. Cuthbert may be grudge-driven
revenge for decades- or centuries-old forgotten crimes, noting it is unusual for normally-solitary
dragons to coordinate like this 2019-06-10.

npcs/dex.title: Dex
npcs/dex.content:
Drunk dockworker at The Boot’s warehouse, secretly a lookout.
History

Gets high with Ozone (posing as “Mr. Vajidkas”), trading moonshine and cocaine for information
2025-03-31 @ 00:56:49.
Reveals the warehouse is finishing a shipment leaving that night, bound for “Rolesk”
2025-03-31 @ 00:58:50-00:59:19.
Fires a flare and pulls a gun, revealing himself as a lookout and triggering the warehouse firefight
2025-03-31 @ 01:05:14-01:06:02.

Unresolved
The ship’s destination, heard as “Rolesk,” is likely a mangled place name
2025-03-31 @ 00:59:19.

npcs/dr.-boom.title: Dr. Boom
npcs/dr.-boom.content:
A rat and a war veteran who submitted a first-person field report to Rugby’s Roaming Gazette, recounting
an adventure that reads suspiciously like an in-world account of a party of adventurers’ early exploits
— possibly, though never confirmed, The Gang themselves, in the unrecorded era
before any session was taped.
History

Submits a reader article describing a visit to Rickety Squibs roughly two years after a war, then
joining a small merchant boat (cat captain, a druid aboard searching for a lost dinosaur) that
captures a pirate ship, taking on its crew and two prisoners; the crew sells a stolen drug shipment
for gold at “that one pirate town with the tree.” One freed prisoner is “the true embodiment of
chaos,” the other “has rapidly plunged into evil acts” 2019-04-22.

Unresolved
No PC or NPC in any recorded session or existing wiki page matches a rat war veteran, a cat ship
captain, or a druid searching for a lost dinosaur. See the-gang’s Unresolved section for
the cross-reference — this may be an in-world account of the party’s own pre-recording adventures, but
it is not asserted as such.

npcs/dr.-e-brown.title: Dr. E Brown
npcs/dr.-e-brown.content:
Founder of “The Agency,” a group investigating crimes against space-time, centered on an event it
calls “Day Zero.” Appears only in the flagged 4900-paradox issue — see timeline.
History

A space-time magic wizard who wants space-time magic abolished altogether; founds The Agency to
investigate major space-time-altering events leading up to and after “Day Zero,” sending agents
backward in time on one-way journeys to “course-correct” history 2019-05-12.

Unresolved
Appears only in the 2019-05-12 issue (dated APRIL 17 4900, fifteen years after the surrounding
issues’ 4885 setting); the paper never references The Agency, Dr. E Brown, or “Day Zero” again in any
later issue. See factions/The Agency and timeline.

npcs/dr.-joanne-hingbrant.title: Dr. Joanne Hingbrant
npcs/dr.-joanne-hingbrant.content:
Lead researcher on the Kingdom of Turgythe’s space program.
History

Announces the kingdom’s plan to build the world’s first space program, funded under the Science and
Alchemy research act of 4870: “It is something discussed in fairy tales, we plan to make it a
reality” 2019-06-24.

npcs/fugly.title: Fugly
npcs/fugly.content:
The Boot’s orc enforcer, wielding twin machetes. His goat-like horns are growing back into his own
skull, slowly driving him mad.
History

Confronts Rich’s Monk (DungeonVice) alone deeper in the warehouse, named by Jake
2025-03-31 @ 01:39:02, @ 01:39:20.
Rich runs past rather than stopping to fight; Fugly’s follow-up attack misses
2025-03-31 @ 01:39:22-01:40:13.
Rich doubles back to fight him properly; Jake’s narration confirms it’s still the orc
2025-03-31 @ 01:41:11, @ 01:48:40.
Follows Rich down the stairs as Rich keeps chasing The Boot, and critically wounds him for 36
damage 2025-03-31 @ 01:52:32-01:53:30.
Flanked and killed by Nutty’s Arcane Combatant (DungeonVice) downstairs with a combined
weapon-and-shocking-grasp strike (“Washashaka”); Rich then loots his Boots of Haste from the
corpse 2025-03-31 @ 02:46:05-02:48:42.

Unresolved
Partway through the long fight, Rich and Nutty start calling this enemy “the captain”
2025-03-31 @ 01:43:49, @ 01:55:17, and the wiki previously tracked him as a
separate NPC, The Guard Captain. No second named enemy is ever introduced on mic, Jake narrates him as
“the orc” mid-fight @ 01:48:40, and he’s the one who follows Rich downstairs and whose corpse yields the
Boots of Haste — so this is almost certainly just Fugly, nicknamed “the captain” by the players once the
fight turned out to be much tougher than expected, not a distinct NPC. See The Guard Captain for the
remaining doubt.

npcs/gorthak.title: Gorthak
npcs/gorthak.content:
Also heard as: Garthok, Gorthuk, Gorthok
An orc warlord who rises from leading the Nayesche tribe to uniting every orc clan into a single
horde, becoming the defining military threat of the Binneth–Squiyles war. The Gazette itself spells
his name three different ways across issues — Garthok, Gorthuk, and Gorthok — explicitly flagging in
the 2019-04-09 issue that these likely name the same figure; this page uses “Gorthak,” the spelling
used when he is crowned ruler of all the orc clans.
History

As “Garthok”/“Gorthuk,” leads the Nayeshe tribe’s “Bloody Tuesday” sack of Bostur, beheading Duke
Harrington and razing City Hall; interviewed on-site feasting on the remains of locals and
proclaiming dominance over the land. The portrait caption spells his name “Gorthuk” while the body
text uses “Garthok” 2019-04-09.
His army conquers Kafka, a major agricultural hub, enslaving its farmers
2019-04-15.
Proclaimed ruler of all the orc clans — “GORTHAK UNITES ORC CLANS” — issuing a “call to return home”
to displaced orcs everywhere, accompanied by blooding ceremonies and sacrifices; his forces capture
and enslave the Squiylian cities of Morfi, Mever, and Holde 2019-04-29.
An orc scout captured by Binneth’s Royal-Elites speaks of Gorthak uniting the clans into a horde
he believes capable of conquering the entire continent 2019-04-29.
His forces wipe out an entire Binneth scouting party, sparing only one scout, who is mutilated with
a message carved into his back demanding the return of his son, Zakmed, from Binneth custody:
“RETURN ZAKME’D OR THE DARKNESS WILL FALL ON YOU AS WELL.” The scout dies of his wounds after
delivering the message 2019-06-10.
Zakmed’s parentage — Gorthak’s son — is confirmed when Binneth authorities examine sending stones
confiscated from captured orcs 2019-06-17.
A six-foot, blue-skinned orcish killer wearing a carved wooden mask, responsible for the deaths of
street children in Ezaso, is speculated (unconfirmed) to be a member of “Gorthok’s Army”
2019-04-22.
His successor-reporter Timothy Mantooth later writes that Rex Sauvage, the Gazette’s longtime field
correspondent, was “tragically killed while on a field report in the orc lands” — Gorthak’s own
territory, by then an established, lasting state 2022-12-18.

npcs/grandmaster-wizard-kirby.title: Grandmaster Wizard Kirby
npcs/grandmaster-wizard-kirby.content:
Also heard as: Grand Wizard Kirby
A wizard whose public “Immortality Lecture” ends in catastrophic magical failure at the Novaexum
Lecture Hall.
History

Advertises an “Immortality Lecture” (Methods, Tactics, Pitfalls) for May 1st at the Novaexum Lecture
Hall, Novaexum City 2019-04-01.
Days before the 2019-06-24 issue, attempts a theoretical spell-stacking technique meant to render the
caster immortal in front of a live audience; the spell catastrophically fails, shattering his
focusing mirrors and astral lenses and sending duplicate versions of himself tearing through the
crowd in explosions of light. He has not been seen since 2019-06-24.

npcs/greg.title: Greg
npcs/greg.content:
A carpet-shop owner and sponsor of the Magic Carpet Race in Lutathal; “it’s pronounced Greg” became a
running joke at the table.
History

Negotiates a race sponsorship deal with the party in exchange for 15% of winnings; the deal collapses
after Ozan jokingly offers Rich as collateral, and Rich threatens to burn the shop down
2023-10-24 @ 02:30:16–02:58:48, @ 03:10:05–03:12:57.
Cursed by Jess, compelling him to count every board in his shop, in retaliation for the collapsed deal
@ 03:15:01–03:18:00.
Referenced in session 6’s recap: the party nearly firebombed his shop; instead Frankie traded Richard
into indentured service rather than pay for a carpet
2023-11-28 @ 00:12:38–00:13:23.

npcs/h.g.-higgins.title: H.G. Higgins
npcs/h.g.-higgins.content:
Rugby’s Roaming Gazette’s staff illustrator, credited on multiple dragon-attack drawings during the
early days of the Binneth–Squiyles war.
History

Credited for the illustration of the blue dragon’s attack on the Isle of Torta 2019-04-01.
Credited for the illustration of the two-dragon attack on Stroth Castle 2019-04-09.
Credited for “Near Defenestration of King Tygard,” illustrating King Stroth dangling King Tygard out
a window 2019-04-15.

npcs/hammond-hardle.title: Hammond Hardle
npcs/hammond-hardle.content:
Royal Astronomer and Astrologist to the King of Binneth, present at the Ezaso Astronomy Summit and,
in the flagged 4900-paradox issue, the royal observatory’s final witness before evacuating to the
Feywild.
History

Addresses public worry over stars vanishing from the sky, suggesting (without elaborating) that it
is a message from the gods 2019-04-01.
In the 2019-05-12 issue (dated APRIL 17 4900, a flagged anomaly — see timeline),
makes the last recorded astronomical observation before the final star goes dark and the Material
Plane apparently ceases to exist, then evacuates through a Feywild planar gate set up by royal
wizards 2019-05-12.

npcs/ilestra'-tarmuhn.title: Ilestra' Tarmuhn
npcs/ilestra'-tarmuhn.content:
Fey High-Oracle who lives in “the book of wisdom,” appearing only in the flagged 4900-paradox issue.
History

Receives a prophecy (“Gone are the days…”) felt and understood by every magic user in the
Feywild, following the Material Plane’s apparent collapse and the rip in Carceri that dumped
nightmarish horrors back into the multiverse 2019-05-12.

npcs/irina-indirovich.title: Irina Indirovich
npcs/irina-indirovich.content:
Also heard as: Irena, Irene
Adopted daughter of the Burgomaster Kolyan Indirovich and sister of Ismark Indirovich. Bitten
twice by Strahd von Zarovich and slowly turning into a vampire — the crisis that draws the party to
Barovia in the first place.
History

Found barricaded in the family’s guest house, bitten twice by Strahd, casting no reflection
2022-12-06 @ 02:58:06, @ 02:57:51.
Refuses to be chained up for safety; Donnie’s Remove Curse has no effect on her
2022-12-06 @ 03:05:00, @ 03:08:25.
Orders the party off the family property alongside her brother
2022-12-06 @ 03:07:21.

Unresolved
Whether Irina ever fully turns into a vampire is never shown — she and her brother are not seen again
after the party leaves for Castle Ravenloft.

npcs/ismark-indirovich.title: Ismark Indirovich
npcs/ismark-indirovich.content:
Also heard as: Mark
Son of the missing Burgomaster Kolyan Indirovich and brother of Irina Indirovich. Wears a holy
ring his father gave him.
History

Meets the party at the Blood of the Vine tavern and confirms his father vanished eight days earlier
seeking outside help, and that neither of the party’s letters matches his father’s real handwriting
2022-12-06 @ 02:32:48–02:34:29.
Helps the party search his father’s office, then his sister’s guest house
2022-12-06 @ 02:44:57, @ 02:52:37.
Orders the party off the family property after they try to restrain his bitten sister
2022-12-06 @ 03:05:00–03:07:21.

Unresolved
Ismark is never seen again after the party is ordered off the property; his and Irina’s fate is not
followed up on in later sessions.

npcs/jerry.title: Jerry
npcs/jerry.content:
Also heard as: Cherry, Sherry, Terry
The inspectors’ teleporter operator/custodian. Apologetic, knits sweaters for his mother, refuses tips.
History

Returns to the office nursing a broken finger, courtesy of the new prisoner
2025-03-31 @ 00:05:58, @ 00:06:24.
Teleports the party to the Council chambers, then to the dockside warehouse
2025-03-31 @ 00:10:44, @ 00:40:27-00:42:21.

npcs/king-stroth.title: King Stroth
npcs/king-stroth.content:
Ruler of the Kingdom of Squiyles throughout the war with Binneth, known for a volatile temper and an
unpopular wartime draft.
History

Loses his temper at the annual Binneth–Squiyles alliance meeting, dangling King Tygard out a
third-story window; both parties leave threatening war 2019-04-15.
Declares Squiyles’ first military draft in 90 years, since the War of the Falling Moon under his
grandfather 2019-04-22.
Makes no public statement as trolls pour out of the Acatlalco mountains, nor as the country of
Cacoal is overrun and declares itself the self-styled “Changeling Nation”
2019-06-10, 2019-07-15.
Fields a Wizard Special Forces air unit under Captain Hoolihan against Binneth’s navy
2019-06-24.
Presides over a kingdom collapsing under civil unrest, famine, and a growing separatist uprising
whose leaders he has arrested for treason 2019-06-17.

npcs/king-tygard.title: King Tygard
npcs/king-tygard.content:
Ruler of the Kingdom of Binneth, nearly thrown from a third-story window by King Stroth during a
heated alliance meeting.
History

Attends the annual Binneth–Squiyles alliance/trade meeting, hosted by negotiator Brennen Ragard;
King Stroth dangles him out the meeting hall’s third-story window amid a screaming argument. Both
parties leave hurling threats of war 2019-04-15.

npcs/kolyan-indirovich.title: Kolyan Indirovich
npcs/kolyan-indirovich.content:
The Burgomaster of Barovia, father of Ismark Indirovich and adoptive father of
Irina Indirovich. Missing for roughly two weeks by the time the party arrives, having gone to seek
outside help.
History

His signed plea for help — describing his bitten daughter Irina — reaches the party
via a page 2022-12-06 @ 01:07:29.
His son Ismark confirms neither the plea nor the dinner invitation matches his father’s real handwriting
2022-12-06 @ 02:34:29.
His genuine handwriting is confirmed via a third letter found on a dead villager, implying a forger has
been producing near-identical letters 2022-12-06 @ 02:50:28.

Unresolved
Kolyan is never found in the recorded sessions — the party leaves Barovia for Castle Ravenloft without
resolving his disappearance.

npcs/littlepen.title: Littlepen
npcs/littlepen.content:
Also heard as: Little Pen, Lil Pan
A goblin, the kidnapping target of the party’s one-shot heist job, attending a mansion banquet as a guest
of the Aspis Corporation.
History

Attends the mansion banquet as an Aspis Corporation guest; nearly exposed when guards sweep for an
unregistered goblin 2020-09-28 @ 00:17:30.
Sickened by the party’s poisoned soup along with roughly half the banquet
2020-09-28 @ 01:26:38.
Struck non-lethally and beaten unconscious by Nutty’s character and Jake under cover of darkness
2020-09-28 @ 02:09:53–02:20:27.
Successfully carried off and secured aboard the party’s getaway boat
2020-09-28 @ 03:19:14.

npcs/loren-fenn.title: Loren Fenn
npcs/loren-fenn.content:
Council archivist in Turgeth who meticulously timestamps every visit and comment.
History

Logs the party’s visit to the Council chambers and clears them to interrogate the prisoner,
Riggs’s Widow 2025-03-31 @ 00:11:58, @ 00:14:20.

Unresolved
Mentions a “Captain Elas” once; could not be confirmed as a real recurring name or a mishearing
2025-03-31 @ 00:12:48.

npcs/madame-eva.title: Madame Eva
npcs/madame-eva.content:
A gypsy fortune teller who leads a roving encampment outside the village of Barovia, and had foreseen the
party’s arrival.
History

Gives the party a tarot (Tarokka) reading: Death (transformation, not literal death — reassuring Todd,
who learns he actually dies decades later choking on a sausage), a reversed card of conflict, and the
Fool, plus a prophecy about “a tool of evil” protected by darkness
2022-12-06 @ 03:44:15–03:52:28.
The reading is cut short when Todd, handed Donnie’s water skin for a drink, mistakenly splashes her with
Donnie’s holy water instead
2022-12-06 @ 04:00:19.

DM notes (spoiler)
Pat confirmed OOC that the tarot draws for this reading were genuinely random, not pre-stacked
2022-12-06 @ 03:44:21.
Unresolved
The “tool of evil” from her prophecy is never explicitly identified on-screen — possibly the
Sun Sword, but this link is never confirmed in-fiction.

npcs/mary.title: Mary
npcs/mary.content:
The party’s contact for the bank job, an older woman staying above the Howling Hooters in
Lidurithal.
History

Gives the party the bank’s layout and guard patrol schedule, and confirms Cadillac is a
doppelganger; agrees to hide the party for the night
2023-09-12 @ 03:01:14–03:05:01.
Has her memory wiped twice by Pat with the Wand of Memory Lapse, first to erase an awkward
gangbang-joke encounter, then again after Connor insults her @ 02:56:41, @ 03:06:06. (A separate,
later memory-lapse spell, cast by Connor’s Jim Jones, targets a guard who had learned Mary’s
whereabouts, not Mary herself @ 03:36:31–03:36:52.)

npcs/mitch-copperhead.title: Mitch Copperhead
npcs/mitch-copperhead.content:
Also heard as: Copperhead, Copperbeard, Copperfield
A dwarf mercenary recruiter who carries a two-handed axe and hires the party for the bank job in
Lidurithal. Revealed by Mary to be a doppelganger, and later turns out to be part of his own
caravan’s doppelganger crew.
History

Hires the party for the bank job, names Cadillac kill-on-sight, and is talked up from 5,000 to
8,000 gold by Ozan 2023-09-12 @ 02:12:06–02:17:57.
Sends his servant creature Gus (a large bulldog) to deliver the party’s gold payment, then drops the
party outside Lidurithal; the transcript doesn’t specify how Mitch himself departs
@ 02:19:46–02:32:53.
Confirmed a doppelganger by Mary @ 03:02:24.
Revealed mid-ambush, heard as “Copperbeard”/“Copperfield,” leading the caravan of doppelgangers
carrying the Dyson Dynamo; killed by Nutty and looted (nothing of value found) by Ozan
2023-10-15 @ 00:01:19, @ 00:36:05, @ 01:47:02.

Unresolved
The identification of the ep4 caravan leader as the same Copperhead from episode 1 is presumed from name
similarity and plot continuity but never stated explicitly on mic.

npcs/murph.title: Murph
npcs/murph.content:
A human prisoner found locked in a basement cell beneath Castle Ravenloft.
History

Freed by Ozan after Todd spends many rounds breaking down the
reinforced door to his cell
2022-12-26 @ 03:04:37.
Immediately steps on an undetected teleport trap and is zapped into a nearby flooded cell, requiring a
second rescue 2022-12-26 @ 03:07:18.
Mentions arriving at the castle “naked outside” and references a Baron’s invitation and drinking with
gypsies, echoing the party’s own entry into Barovia
2022-12-26 @ 04:08:17.

Unresolved
Murph’s fate after this session is not mentioned again in the recorded transcripts.

npcs/narfuuuk.title: Narfuuuk
npcs/narfuuuk.content:
A wealthy goblin noble whose nephew is kidnapped from the family’s inn near Balnaskor Mountains.
History

Places a 10,000 gold piece bounty for his nephew’s safe return after witnesses see the boy
manacled and led off by a group of adventurers heading into the mountains, suspected (unconfirmed)
of being slavers 2022-12-18, 2022-12-26.

npcs/petrina-velikovna.title: Petrina Velikovna
npcs/petrina-velikovna.content:
Also heard as: Patrina Velikovna, Iflishkova
A withered vampire bride of Strahd von Zarovich, found desiccated in a crypt in the catacombs beneath
Castle Ravenloft.
History

Accidentally awakened when Nutty pours his own blood into her mouth, not realizing what she is
2023-01-30 @ 03:15:51.
Knocked unconscious by Wu before she can fully transform, then beheaded; the party keeps her fanged
skull as a trophy 2023-01-30 @ 03:17:00–03:21:00.

Unresolved
Her name is inconsistently spelled/spoken across the session as “Patrina Velikovna,” “Petrina Velikovna,”
and “Iflishkova” — likely the same character referred to with two different names
2023-01-30 @ 02:19:40, @ 03:04:25.
Jake jokes in-character that killing her (“the boss”) should auto-cure Jess’s petrification “by Gorgon
rules” — Rich and Nutty immediately shoot this down on mic as not how it works. Jess’s character is
restored to flesh shortly after (@ 04:20:48), but the transcript ties it to a burned Fate Point in a
side exchange between Pat and Jess (@ 04:18:11, @ 04:20:10) that isn’t narrated on mic, not to Petrina’s
earlier death. A wiki draft previously credited Petrina’s death with the restoration; corrected here —
see Alumbra.

npcs/pop-jack.title: Pop Jack
npcs/pop-jack.content:
Also heard as: Pop Object, the air elemental, the ship's elemental
A large air elemental captured and permanently, forcibly bound to the party’s ship to give it flight.
Screams constantly in Mori Yoshinari’s mind after he bonds with it as captain; controlled through
charisma-based pain/threat domination.
History

Summoned, bound, and fed into a brass framework over two days by a Neo enchantress for 100,000 gold
2020-01-20 @ 02:29:27–02:33:00.
Mori Yoshinari speaks the command word “Pop Jack” to permanently bond with it
2020-01-20 @ 02:44:28.
Piloted via charisma-based pain/threat control to fly the ship to a capital city
2020-01-20 @ 02:53:03.
The ship is kept permanently parked thirty feet up by this point in the campaign “to dodge time
wizards,” implying ongoing routine use of the elemental’s flight
2020-04-13 @ 01:01:11.

DM notes (spoiler)
Elemental language is called “Orin,” and most elementals (and some monstrous races) culturally view
elemental enslavement as abhorrent — a detail the party has been told in-game but which underscores the
moral weight of binding Pop Jack permanently
2020-01-20 @ 02:37:03.
Unresolved
Whether Pop Jack is ever freed, or remains bound to the ship through the rest of the recorded campaign, is
not addressed after Arc I.

npcs/ray-parker.title: Ray Parker
npcs/ray-parker.content:
An investigator and field reporter in Godoy, chasing the story of a mysterious, unmarked airship
that appears over the city at night and leaves no trace.
History

Reports spotting a medium-sized, unmarked airship darting through the night sky beneath storm
clouds; it vanishes by dawn, leaving no arrival or departure record. “This case has a hold on me”
2023-09-24.

npcs/rex-sauvage.title: Rex Sauvage
npcs/rex-sauvage.content:
Also heard as: Rex Savauge
A dashing adventurer and longtime field correspondent for Rugby’s Roaming Gazette, riding his griffin
Sterling, “good friends” with King Fashim Thoronor, and protected by an amulet that blocks location
magic and scrying — until that same amulet makes him impossible to find when he goes missing for good.
History

“FIELD REPORT” debut: single-handedly defeats a band of lizard-men ravaging locals, including their
leader, near a cliff edge and a covered wagon 2019-04-01.
Flies to aid King Fashim Thoronor’s kingdom on griffin Sterling, fighting off an ambush by four
harpies mid-flight before continuing on toward the kingdom of Turgyth
2019-04-09.
Fights and kills a storm-summoning “thunder wolf” that ambushes his campsite at night
2019-04-15.
En route to the Hawkthorne Royal Gala, is attacked by his own carriage driver, who wields an
enchanted glass eye under an eyepatch to try to dominate his mind; Rex resists and hands the man to
the local guard 2019-04-22.
Goes missing: the Gazette runs a “MISSING PERSON” notice asking the public and local authorities for
information 2019-06-10.
Still missing weeks later; the Gazette’s scrying attempts to locate him fail because he wears an
amulet that blocks location detection and scrying — the same protection that made him a great
investigator now makes him unfindable. He has a wife and children worried for him
2019-07-15.
By JULY 4 4885, with no sign of him, the Gazette publicly solicits a replacement field journalist,
describing him as “our dearest and most respected journalist” and implying he is gone for good
2020-04-13.
Confirmed dead by his eventual successor Timothy Mantooth, who writes that Rex was “tragically
killed while on a field report in the orc lands” 2022-12-18.

npcs/riggs's-widow.title: Riggs's Widow
npcs/riggs's-widow.content:
Also heard as: the captured prisoner, the condemned prisoner
The widow of Riggs, Turgeth’s former crime boss. Sentenced to death. Engineered her own capture by
the inspectors to get close to a hidden golden ticket.
History

Flirted into talking by Ozone in her holding cell 2025-03-31 @ 00:15:20.
Reveals her husband Riggs lost a bargain with a devil and was dragged to hell
2025-03-31 @ 00:17:41.
Admits she used The Boot to get captured and track the party back to their HQ, hunting the
Golden Ticket to the Devil — a one-way pass to confront the devil holding Riggs’s soul
2025-03-31 @ 00:19:45, @ 00:20:31.
Reveals the drug Maka is secretly supplied by the College of Turgeth, worth ~75,000 gp/week
2025-03-31 @ 00:24:08-00:24:19, @ 00:25:03.

Unresolved
Her name was never stated on mic in session 3.

npcs/riggs.title: Riggs
npcs/riggs.content:
Former crime boss of Turgeth, running the city’s drug trade before The Boot. Husband of
Riggs’s Widow. Cut a deal with a devil for manpower, lost, and was dragged to hell.
History

Established by Jake as the previous boss, “sucked back into hell” 2025-03-31 @ 00:02:38.
His widow reveals he lost a bargain with a devil and was dragged to hell for it
2025-03-31 @ 00:17:41.
The Golden Ticket to the Devil his widow seeks would be a one-way pass to confront that devil and
reunite with Riggs’s soul 2025-03-31 @ 00:20:31.

npcs/sasha-ivliskova.title: Sasha Ivliskova
npcs/sasha-ivliskova.content:
Also heard as: Iflishkova
A banshee found in crypt #21 of the catacombs beneath Castle Ravenloft — revealed to be one of
Strahd von Zarovich’s wives.
History

Attacks the party when her crypt (engraved “Sasha Ivliskova, wife”) is opened
2023-01-30 @ 02:15:21, @ 02:20:26. (The timestamp previously
cited here, @ 02:19:40, is actually a different crypt’s reveal — see Unresolved.)
Killed by Donnie’s Ear-Piercing Scream hex after taking roughly 79 damage over the fight; Pat confirms
the kill on mic 2023-01-30 @ 02:59:16, @ 03:03:58.

Unresolved
Pat narrates the loot in her crypt — 3,300 gold pieces — as “Petrina’s treasure” immediately after
confirming Sasha’s defeat 2023-01-30 @ 03:04:25, even though
Petrina Velikovna’s own, separately-named crypt is found later in the session. Likely a DM slip
rather than a deliberate link between the two NPCs, but the gold’s true source is ambiguous on mic. The
“signet ring” previously credited to this crypt actually belongs to an unrelated, already-empty crypt
opened earlier 2023-01-30 @ 02:18:15 — removed from her loot
list here.

npcs/sergei-von-zarovich.title: Sergei von Zarovich
npcs/sergei-von-zarovich.content:
Strahd von Zarovich’s brother, murdered by Strahd out of jealousy over a shared love,
Tatiana. His preserved body was interred in the catacombs beneath Castle Ravenloft with the blade of
the Sun Sword and a suit of magic armor.
History

His preserved body is found in crypt #13 of the catacombs, buried with the Sun Sword’s blade and magic
armor 2023-01-30 @ 03:50:41.
Holy water splashed on his body by Donnie creates a mind-link, revealing that he and Strahd both loved
Tatiana, and that Strahd murdered them both out of jealousy
2023-01-30 @ 04:00:19–04:10:16.
His body crumbles to dust once the mind-link ends
2023-01-30 @ 04:10:16.

DM notes (spoiler)
His backstory is the motive for Strahd’s long-standing grief and villainy — Pat frames the original 1984
module’s Strahd as a villain with real motivations and grief rather than a generic monster
2023-03-18 @ 00:33:00–00:33:48.

npcs/sir-holton-albright.title: Sir Holton Albright
npcs/sir-holton-albright.content:
Also heard as: the Fiend Slayer, the glabrezu demon
A paladin, “the Fiend Slayer,” being knighted and anointed at a temple ceremony the party crashes while
claiming to represent a far-off church of Pelor. Revealed mid-ritual to have been possessed/replaced by a
glabrezu demon.
History

Introduced as the honoree of a lavish knighting ceremony the party infiltrates
2020-04-13 @ 01:40:56.
Shows signs of possession (dark circles, agitation) as he kneels for anointing
2020-04-13 @ 01:48:37.
Transforms into a glabrezu demon mid-ritual, instantly stuns and kills the officiating high priest, and
casts Confusion and Reverse Gravity on the assembled crowd
2020-04-13 @ 01:52:04–02:34:08.
Killed by the party (finishing blow from Kurt Furbank) after a running fight across the
ceiling and floor 2020-04-13 @ 03:35:05.

Unresolved
Whether the real Sir Holton Albright was killed/replaced before the ceremony, or possessed and killed
during it, is never clarified.

npcs/sphinx-painting.title: Sphinx Painting
npcs/sphinx-painting.content:
Also heard as: the Sphinx, the Phoenix
A sentient, talking painting guarding a secret door in a cult’s abandoned underground complex, demanding
three riddles be answered to pass. Later befriended by the party — especially Miss Cleo — and willing
to leave with them for a new home after centuries alone answering riddles.
History

Animates when Alexander steps on a rug in front of it, demanding three riddles be answered to pass,
lightning-zapping wrong guesses 2021-10-19 @ 00:27:24.
Poses the “letter N” riddle (a king has one, a nun has two, a whore has none), accepted after two failed
guesses 2021-10-19 @ 00:28:10–00:41:50.
Poses the “sawdust” riddle, nearly killing Miss Cleo before Nutty works out the answer
2021-10-19 @ 00:42:03–00:55:19.
Poses the final “time” riddle, answered correctly by Jess
2021-10-19 @ 00:56:20–00:58:02.
Befriended by the party, especially Ozan, and reportedly willing to leave with them for a new home; Ozan
buys a bag of holding to transport the painting
2021-10-19 @ 01:33:16, @ 02:32:22.
Left behind at the one-way portal with Donnie and Ozan rather than carried through
2021-10-19 @ 03:02:21.

npcs/strahd-von-zarovich.title: Strahd von Zarovich
npcs/strahd-von-zarovich.content:
Also heard as: the Baron, Baron Strahd, the Devil Strahd, Strad von Zerlvik, Strahd von Berowitsch, Strahd von Barovic, the Count, Lestrade
The vampire lord of Castle Ravenloft, who has terrorized Barovia for centuries. Lures outsiders to his
castle under forged invitations, then toys with them through illusions, domination, and mist form rather
than fighting to the death. Murdered his own brother Sergei von Zarovich and the woman Tatiana they
both loved out of jealousy.
History

Sends the party a dinner invitation under his seal, alongside a forged plea letter purportedly from
Kolyan Indirovich — both lead the party to Barovia
2022-12-06 @ 01:07:29, @ 02:15:24.
Greets the party for dinner, playing the organ with his back to them, then vanishes with a maniacal
laugh after being hit with a thrown dinner roll — locking down the castle’s doors, torches, and lights
2022-12-18 @ 00:42:14–00:45:43.
Leaves behind a rope-and-mirror-operated mannequin decoy of himself, later burned by Todd
2022-12-18 @ 00:52:39.
His own journal, the cursed Tome of Strahd, is found hidden under his mattress
2022-12-18 @ 02:09:47.
Carries the party to a prison cell atop his highest spire after a ghost ambush; appears briefly below,
waves, smiles, and turns to mist
2023-01-30 @ 01:10:34, @ 01:33:50.
Revealed via a mind-link from Sergei’s body to have murdered his own brother
2023-01-30 @ 04:00:19–04:00:36; the party separately pieces
together, minutes later, that he also killed Tatiana “when she wouldn’t marry him”
2023-01-30 @ 04:08:35.
Fatally drains Donnie’s character near his sealed coffin, turning him into a vampire thrall
2023-01-30 @ 04:56:54–05:19:31.
Found asleep in his coffin — empty but for a teddy bear and blanket when finally forced open; the real
Strahd is not there 2023-02-12 @ 00:43:16.
Ambushes the party in his audience chamber, dominating most of them; forces Todd to attack an ally and
Jess to nearly kill Jake, before escaping as mist after a drawn-out fight
2023-02-12 @ 00:58:14–02:23:45.
Mists away into the walls of his casket room before the golem-trap session begins
2023-03-12 @ 00:19:11.
Revealed to have secretly turned Donovan into his thrall and used him to ambush the party from
within 2023-03-18 @ 00:48:16
onward.

DM notes (spoiler)

The figure seen at the dinner organ may have been Strahd himself baiting the party, or another decoy —
Pat never clarified on-mic whether it was staged like the mannequin found later
2022-12-18 @ 00:42:14, @ 00:52:39.
Donnie’s death and vampirization near Strahd’s coffin was a deliberate trap tied to proximity to the
coffin, not random bad luck — Pat calls it intentional, “the only way he can solve it”
2023-01-30 @ 04:50:29.
Pat confirms OOC the module run is the original 1980s/1984 TSR Ravenloft, not the modern remake
2023-01-30 @ 05:36:35,
2023-03-18 @ 00:33:00.

Unresolved
Strahd is never defeated or even fought to a finish in the recorded sessions — the campaign’s last session
ends with him still alive and the party deep in his castle.

npcs/tatiana.title: Tatiana
npcs/tatiana.content:
A woman both Strahd von Zarovich and his brother Sergei von Zarovich loved. Strahd killed her when
she refused to marry him, along with his own brother.
History

Revealed via a mind-link from Sergei’s body: Strahd murdered Sergei
2023-01-30 @ 04:00:19–04:00:36. The party separately
concludes, a few minutes later, that Strahd also killed Tatiana “when she wouldn’t marry him”
2023-01-30 @ 04:08:35 — not part of the same mind-link vision,
as previously implied here.
The party realizes, after the fact, that a statue Nutty had smashed earlier in the dungeon depicted her
2023-01-30 @ 04:07:04.

Unresolved
Whether Tatiana’s remains or spirit can still be found anywhere in the castle is raised as a hook but
never followed up on in the recorded sessions.

npcs/than'-targuhn.title: Than' Targuhn
npcs/than'-targuhn.content:
A fisherman whose encounter near the Isle of Death gives the island its name.
History

While fishing near the island east of Sawyen, witnesses a skeletal, skinless flying horror
accompanied by roughly a dozen others, amid a flash of green light and noxious smoke: “I barely
escaped with my life. The screams, still howling in my brain…” 2019-07-15.

npcs/the-boot.title: The Boot
npcs/the-boot.content:
Current crime lord of Turgeth’s drug trade, a roughly 12-foot-tall troll who took over after
Riggs fell. Runs a dockside warehouse/shipping operation and is tied to the drug Maka.
History

Established as the new crime lord, replacing Riggs 2025-03-31 @ 00:02:38, @ 00:04:23.
Riggs’s Widow used the Boot’s operation to get herself captured and tracked back to the inspectors’
HQ 2025-03-31 @ 00:19:45.
Flees his burning dockside warehouse by ship as the party raids it
2025-03-31 @ 02:38:24-03:09:40.
Spotted on deck by a hasted, ethereal Rich’s Monk (DungeonVice), unaware he’s being watched, as the
session ends mid-chase 2025-03-31 @ 03:09:40-03:10:13.

Unresolved
Whether the Boot is captured, killed, or escapes is not resolved — the session ends mid-chase. See
Hunt for the Boot.

npcs/the-demon-in-nutty.title: The Demon in Nutty
npcs/the-demon-in-nutty.content:
Also heard as: Mohawk, the possessing demon
An invisible, chaotic-evil demon that secretly possessed Nutty’s character
after he touched a cursed soul gem sessions before the possession was revealed — a fact even Nutty’s own
player hadn’t fully known until it came out at the table.
History

Secretly possessing Nutty’s body for an unknown number of prior sessions; revealed when it attacks
Ozan’s character and Tick-Tick
2020-03-24 @ 02:43:50.
Kills Ozan’s character outright with a sneak-attack finishing blow
2020-03-24 @ 01:59:28.
Kills the unconscious Tick-Tick immediately after
2020-03-24 @ 02:22:31.
Describes its own “Possession” ability: if struck down near another creature, that creature must save or
be possessed in turn 2020-03-24 @ 02:58:15.
Banished by the newly-reborn Paladin of Pelor’s holy symbol
2020-03-24 @ 02:42:10.

Unresolved
The demon’s true name/species is never stated beyond the player nickname “Mohawk,” which may just refer
to its token art rather than an in-fiction name.

npcs/the-guard-captain.title: The Guard Captain
npcs/the-guard-captain.content:
Also heard as: the captain
“The captain” is Rich and Nutty’s own mid-fight nickname (never used by Jake as DM) for the tough,
twin-bladed fighter who followed Rich’s Monk (DungeonVice) downstairs and critically wounded him.
History

Follows Rich’s Monk (DungeonVice) downstairs and critically wounds him for 36 damage
2025-03-31 @ 01:52:32-01:53:30.
Finished off by Nutty’s Arcane Combatant (DungeonVice) (flanked, killed with the Washashaka
shocking-grasp attack); Rich then loots his Boots of Haste from the corpse
2025-03-31 @ 02:47:44-02:48:42.

DM notes (spoiler)
Jake tells the players (OOC) this guard was likely a level 10-11 fighter, info the characters never learn
in-game 2025-03-31 @ 02:55:27-02:57:32.
Unresolved
This page likely does not describe a separate NPC at all. The only named enemy Rich meets in this part of
the warehouse is Fugly (named by Jake @ 01:39:20); Rich runs past him, doubles back to fight him
properly @ 01:41:11, and Jake’s narration still calls him “the orc” mid-fight @ 01:48:40 — right before
this same enemy follows Rich down the stairs @ 01:52:32 and crits him. “The captain” is only ever Rich’s
and Nutty’s own guess at his rank 2025-03-31 @ 01:43:49, @ 01:55:17, never
confirmed by Jake as a second NPC. Treat this page and Fugly as almost certainly the same character
until a future session clarifies otherwise.

npcs/the-mage.title: The Mage
npcs/the-mage.content:
Also heard as: the wizard, the ship's original owner
The deceased wizard who built and ran the party’s planeshifting, blood-fueled ship as a deliberate trap
for thieves — draining their blood to power the vessel and fuel his own immortality. Killed by the party
before the recorded sessions begin.
History

Referenced as already dead; the party loots his ship, finds his cosmology journal and hidden spell
book 2020-01-20 @ 00:20:38, @ 00:48:54.
Pat (OOC) reveals his blood-draining trap existed to fund “immortality and interplanar travel powered by
the suffering of someone” 2020-01-20
@ 00:31:05.
His corpse is reanimated by Rich as a “bloody skeleton” undead minion, kept on hand as emergency muscle
2020-03-25 @ 02:19:47.

npcs/the-seated-man.title: The Seated Man
npcs/the-seated-man.content:
An unnamed, cobwebbed figure found motionless on a throne deep in the pyramid, holding a staff and wearing
a skull crown — implied to be the source of the visions that drew the party to the temple.
History

Found seated and statue-still on a throne, implied source of the visions that drew the party to the
temple 2019-10-15 @ 01:49:06.
Awakens hostile, eyes flashing, and joins the fight against the party after Rich fails to steal his
staff (even with a fate-point reroll)
2019-10-15 @ 02:43:22.
Commands a golden/bronze hand guardian built into the boss chamber’s walls
2019-10-15 @ 02:43:22.

Unresolved
The session ends mid-fight against him; his fate, and whether he really is the source of the party’s
visions, is never resolved in the recorded sessions.

npcs/thornshade.title: Thornshade
npcs/thornshade.content:
Also heard as: Thorne Shade, Thornblade
An investigator for the TIU, a planar law-enforcement organization out of the city of Chrome, hunting
the Dyson Dynamo. Appears only as an astral projection, not physically present.
History

Descends on the party outside the rug shop with his subordinate Iron Soul, identifies the
Dyson Dynamo as a reality-threatening artifact, and demands answers
2023-11-28 @ 00:37:54–00:38:31.
Revealed as an astral projection when Ashleen (leenmcweenersten’s witch) tries to pick his pocket for
a look at his badge and her hand passes right through him @ 00:43:08–00:43:22.
Grabs Ashleen’s hand after she casts Detect Thoughts on him, and warns the party that any further magic
will be treated as an act of aggression @ 00:43:41–00:45:22.
Fought and defeated by Gang in a brawl, his shimmering true form showing through each hit; concedes
@ 01:03:48–01:08:03.
Shows his real badge (TIU, city of Chrome), explains the Dynamo harvests “just and unjust souls,” offers
1,000–2,000 gold compensation, and leaves after the party is marked as suspects @ 01:08:41–01:18:33.

Unresolved
“Chrome” as his home city may be a mistranscription of a different fantasy name.

npcs/timothy-mantooth.title: Timothy Mantooth
npcs/timothy-mantooth.content:
Rugby’s Roaming Gazette’s new field correspondent, filling the hole left by Rex Sauvage’s death,
dispatching from the snowy Balnaskor Mountains.
History

Introduces himself as a successor “standing on the shoulders of a giant, my hero, Rex Sauvage, who
was tragically killed while on a field report in the orc lands”; reports from the Balnaskor
Mountains, gathering stories from sparse snow-dwelling orc clans, including rumors of a mysterious
mountain town shrouded in an inescapable fog 2022-12-18.

npcs/volto.title: Volto
npcs/volto.content:
The inspectors’ office/HQ chief.
History

Reminds the team about the still-pending Aqueducts Assignment, grumbling about funding from
“Captain Lieutenant Squats” 2025-03-31 @ 00:07:25-00:07:44.

npcs/worick-dragon-bane.title: Worick Dragon-bane
npcs/worick-dragon-bane.content:
A paladin of St. Cuthbert, blinded and robbed when thieves steal his church’s vessel out from under
him in Thorhofn City.
History

Napping aboard a Church of St. Cuthbert vessel at the Thorhofn docks, he is blinded by a group of
thieves who steal the boat; the ship is later found scuttled and burned near the Isle of Torta.
A surviving watchman identifies one of the thieves as a samurai, and the church plans to hire mages
to divine his location 2019-06-10.

npcs/zakmed.title: Zakmed
npcs/zakmed.content:
Also heard as: Zakme'd
Son of the orc warlord Gorthak, held as a war-criminal prisoner by Binneth authorities until
Gorthak’s demands for his return — and a mutilated messenger — forced the issue.
History

Held by Binneth as a war criminal, a key bargaining chip in the war against the orcs
2019-06-10.
Gorthak demands his return, killing an entire Binneth scouting party and mutilating the sole
survivor to carry the message 2019-06-10.
Confirmed via confiscated sending stones to be Gorthak’s son 2019-06-17.
Escapes (or is sprung from) Binneth custody under circumstances that baffle the authorities; the
Royal Guard warns the public he is dangerous and the king offers a hefty reward for information
leading to his re-arrest 2019-06-17.

pcs/aisling.title: Aisling
pcs/aisling.content:
Also heard as: Ashley, Ashleen, Ashlene, Donnie's witch
A second character fielded by Donnie alongside Colt Hopper: a small witch with a prehensile tongue,
dual ranged weapons, and hex magic. Her name is transcribed inconsistently as “Ashley,” “Ashleen,”
“Ashlene,” and “Aisling” — “Aisling” is used here as the best-guess spelling.
History

Glimpsed mid-session, 6’1” tall, described as towering over “the little frog dude” (Colt Hopper)
2023-09-12 @ 03:17:53–03:18:01.
Casts Vomit Swarm (wasps) and uses a hex build (Limp Lash, Misfortune, Cackle), targeting the enemy
healer-cleric with Misfortune shortly before the party finishes it off
2023-10-01 @ 00:34:21, @ 02:29:30–02:33:09.
Named among the party’s absent members (player not on the call) in session 4
2023-10-15 @ 00:27:29.
Named among the party’s absent members in session 5
2023-10-24 @ 00:41:43.

Unresolved
A witch named “Ashleen,” played by a different real person (leenmcweenersten, new to the table), appears
in session 6 — using Detect Thoughts and perceiving astral “silver threads.” It’s unclear whether this is
the same character handed to a new player, a coincidence of name, or an unrelated character; the session
6 notes list her separately. See 2023-11-28
@ 00:43:41, @ 01:20:38.

pcs/alexander.title: Alexander
pcs/alexander.content:
Also heard as: Jake's android
Jake’s Arc II character: an android (implied soul knight/psion type) who wields a “dislocator” gun named
Becky and carries a scouting Psycrystal.
History

Triggers a tripwire fire trap, then steps onto the rug that reveals the Sphinx Painting
2021-10-19 @ 00:24:48–00:27:24.
Takes two large lightning hits (30 and 53 damage) failing the Sphinx’s first riddle before Ozan’s
shared memories help him answer correctly
2021-10-19 @ 00:29:11–00:41:50.
Plants his Psycrystal in a dead body’s mouth to remotely scout the Nexus portal’s destination, a frozen
plane with ice golems and a frost giant
2021-10-19 @ 01:08:00–01:14:05.
Finishes forging the sword Ember at the complex’s blacksmith forge
2021-10-19 @ 02:56:23.
Uses his dislocator gun “Becky” to repeatedly teleport the frost giant’s golem escorts dozens of miles
away, removing them from the fight one at a time
2021-11-02 @ 00:20:53–01:16:00.

Unresolved
Whether “Alexander” is his full/official name or just a table nickname is unclear from the transcripts.

pcs/alumbra.title: Alumbra
pcs/alumbra.content:
Also heard as: Ulumbra, Alhambra, Olumbra, Lulu
A ninja/rogue with a katana, sneak attack, uncanny dodge, superior (120 ft.) darkvision, Kai points, and
a Shadow Clone jutsu. Owns a handy haversack, destroyed late in the campaign. In session 1, present
physically at Rich’s location without her own microphone, with Rich’s track picking up and relaying her
dialogue and rolls; from session 2 onward she appears on her own track.
History

Rolls the floating Ion Stone (+2 Constitution) as a starting magic item
2022-12-06 @ 00:52:52.
Finds the secret door behind the dining hall’s organ, leading to the Strahd decoy
2022-12-18 @ 00:51:24.
Gets surrounded and flanked early in the skeleton ambush
2022-12-18 @ 01:08:11.
Trapped in a burning cell during the gas-trap fire; rescued when Donnie’s Air Bubble buys time for
Ozan to pick the lock 2022-12-26
@ 03:30:56–03:53:00.
Turned to stone touching the petrification-warded bars at Strahd’s crypt (@ 04:14:49); restored to
flesh via a burned Fate Point in a side exchange between Pat and Jess, not Petrina’s earlier death as
previously claimed here — see Petrina Velikovna — Pat narrates her “turns back into flesh” only
after Jess steps into a private conversation and a Fate Point is spent
2023-01-30 @ 04:13:44–04:14:49, @ 04:18:11–04:20:48.
Under Strahd’s domination, forced to flank and sneak-attack Jake’s character for 21
damage, nearly killing him 2023-02-12 @ 01:20:30–01:27:00.
Takes heavy golem poison damage, rolls a natural 1 fleeing between both iron golems, and uses her Shadow
Clone jutsu to escape, saved by a burned Fate Point
2023-03-12 @ 01:11:50–01:35:24.
Kills the horse-headed demon with a sneak attack (a Kai-point double attack for 42 damage), and is
infected with Contagion by it
2023-03-18 @ 01:54:07–01:54:24.
Her handy haversack — being used to contain Donovan’s vampire-mist form — is destroyed by
Todd, tearing open a gate to the Astral Plane
2023-03-18 @ 02:30:46.

Unresolved
Her name is rendered inconsistently across sessions (Ulumbra, Alhambra, Olumbra, Lulu); “Alumbra” is used
here as the most frequent spelling in later sessions. Whether “Lulu” and “Alumbra” are the same character
is unclear from context around a trap-triggered disappearance
2022-12-26 @ 02:51:59–02:56:12.

pcs/colt-hopper.title: Colt Hopper
pcs/colt-hopper.content:
Also heard as: Donovan, Cole Hopper, Donnie's gunslinger
Donnie’s grippli (frog-folk) gunslinger, 2’2” tall, dual revolvers. Named “Colt Hopper” in session 1 and
“Donovan” in session 6; treated here as one continuous character on the strength of the matching
race/class, with the gap flagged below.
History

Introduced as a 2’2” grippli gunslinger, possibly also multiclassed into witch; buys a Cloak of
Resistance +1 and a Cackling Hag’s Blouse
2023-09-12 @ 02:04:50–02:10:29.
Claims the suitcase of revolver bullets, revolvers, and a gunsmithing tome from the vault chest
2023-10-01 @ 04:23:51–04:24:07.
Absent/played as an NPC fleeing the fight in session 4, shrunk and teleported clear of Godoy by Rich
2023-10-15 @ 00:27:29, @ 01:07:58.
Not present on the call for session 5.
As “Donovan”: demands ID from the TIU investigators; snorts “whimsy” and gains the ability to see
invisible pickpockets; bluffs a goblin racing crew about the party’s carpet; grabs one of the invisible
pickpockets by hand
2023-11-28 @ 00:38:48, @ 02:13:37, @ 02:21:02, @ 02:37:01.

Unresolved
Session 6 is the first to use the name “Donovan” for this character rather than “Colt Hopper”; no session
explicitly confirms they’re the same PC, though the race/class match and no new-character introduction is
narrated.

pcs/dread-pirate-bobbert.title: Dread Pirate Bobbert
pcs/dread-pirate-bobbert.content:
Also heard as: Bobbert, Barbert, Mr. Squires, Rich's wizard
Rich’s Arc I character, an arcane spellcaster (wizard, implied Universalist) who serves as the party’s
utility caster throughout — identifying magic items, flying the party around, and providing most of its
crowd control and escape options. Named “Dread Pirate Bobbert” from
2020-04-13 onward; earlier sessions refer to him only as
“Rich’s character.”
History

Casts Fireball and Hydraulic Torrent to help destroy a splitting clay golem, then is swept away alone
underwater and meets Andrew 2019-10-15
@ 00:51:36, @ 01:13:40.
Identifies the ship’s helm-room crystal as holding a plane shift spell (25 Knowledge: Arcana)
2020-01-20 @ 00:19:19.
Loots 87 gold, a Ring of Protection +1, and a potion from travelers crushed by the ship’s accidental
plane shift 2020-01-20 @ 01:11:29.
Scries the paladin hunting Mori Yoshinari using an enchanted true-seeing crystal ball
2020-01-28 @ 02:19:19–02:29:42.
Is teleported alone into a puzzle room via a circular key and found unconscious, being drained by a
soul-sucking demon; survives after Jake and Donnie intervene
2020-03-25 @ 00:57:32–01:35:19.
Breaks a petrifying basilisk-guardian’s gaze with Wall of Force
2020-03-25 @ 01:33:59.
Casts Disintegrate and summons three fire elementals to free Obadiah Jones from his ice prison
2020-04-06 @ 01:10:17, @ 01:37:47.
Named “Dread Pirate Bobbert” for the first time; mage-hands a damaged journal revealing the god-baby is
“touched by the gods” 2020-04-13 @ 00:32:59.
Hands out potions of fly and featherfall before the party infiltrates the knighting ceremony
2020-04-13 @ 01:28:42.

Unresolved
Whether Bobbert is the same character Rich plays in the 2021 sessions (his own unnamed tank/healer
character) is not stated.

pcs/fish.title: Fish
pcs/fish.content:
Also heard as: Donovan (Arc II)
Donnie’s Arc II character, a Master Chemist / Vivisectionist Beastmorph alchemist referred to as
“Donovan” in session notes and as “Fish” when Rich plays him in Donnie’s absence.
History

Crafts Cure Serious Wounds extracts and potions for the party; chooses to stay behind at the one-way
portal rather than step through
2021-10-19 @ 02:14:02, @ 03:02:34.
With Donnie absent, piloted by Rich; nearly dropped by the frost giant’s opening ranged freezing ray
2021-11-02 @ 00:10:37–00:11:45.
Lands a flanking sneak bite finishing off one of the giant’s golem escorts
2021-11-02 @ 01:05:21–01:06:26.

Unresolved
Whether “Fish” is a new character or the same “Donovan” alchemist from
2021-10-19 is clear from context (same alchemist build), but
whether this is the same character as Arc I’s Mori Yoshinari is not established — a large time gap
and total change of class/race separate the two. The party discusses at session’s end whether Rich or
someone else should continue playing Fish going forward, or roll a new character.

pcs/frankie.title: Frankie
pcs/frankie.content:
Also heard as: Ozan's Paladin, Ozan's Bard
Ozan’s Paladin/Bard, very high Charisma (23), given to preaching “the good word.” Named “Frankie” only
in session 6; unnamed in every earlier session.
History

Preaches at four city guards searching for Mary, rolling a natural 20 to pull their attention, then
holds it with a Fascinate as they all fail their saves, giving the bartender time to slip away
2023-09-12 @ 03:28:42, @ 03:30:06–03:31:46.
Turns invisible on a natural 20 stealth check and hauls the vault’s loot chest toward the exit
2023-10-01 @ 00:48:08–02:09:53.
While invisible, grabs the fallen Dyson Dynamo off the ground and flees with it into an alley;
does not grab Connor’s character, who is left behind to escape the firestorm on his own
2023-10-15 @ 01:18:46–01:19:16.
Disguises in robes and dirt for the refugee column; uses Fascinate to cover Pat’s escape from the
Lutathal gate guards 2023-10-24 @ 00:30:39, @ 01:33:04–01:34:51.
As “Frankie”: attempts diplomacy and casts Detect Evil on the TIU investigators (Connor’s sense-motive
check and Donnie’s read conclude the lead investigator isn’t evil, just on a job); bartered Richard
into servitude to a rug shop rather than pay for a carpet (per the session’s recap)
2023-11-28 @ 00:12:38, @ 00:49:18,
@ 00:53:14, @ 01:11:05–01:11:23.

Unresolved
Named “Frankie” for the first time in session 6; no earlier session gives this character a name.

pcs/gang.title: Gang
pcs/gang.content:
Also heard as: Gang Orca, the giant orca bouncer
A large monstrous-humanoid half-orca Blood Rager, originally a bar bouncer in Lutathal/Liduriel, recruited
into the party in session 6 — the first session for his player, new to the table.
History

Confronts two astral-projected TIU investigators on his boss’s behalf, biting and clawing Thornshade
until he concedes 2023-11-28 @ 00:57:45–01:08:03.
Recruited into the party outright @ 01:27:09.
Turned away from the racers’ club (the Pierrot) for his size, sneaks in through the basement
@ 02:09:01.
Takes the “whimsy” drug and sprouts an extra row of teeth, permanently upgrading his bite for a week
@ 02:29:00–02:32:38.
Blocks the exit to trap a fleeing pickpocket @ 02:39:20.

Unresolved
His size is stated as “14 feet tall, 1,500 pounds” at one point and “a 17-foot motherfucker” later in the
same session — inconsistent and never reconciled
2023-11-28 @ 01:00:08, @ 02:46:43.

pcs/jace-gandolfini.title: Jace Gandolfini
pcs/jace-gandolfini.content:
A tiefling abjurer, roughly 200+ years old, long-tenured and disreputable professor at Hawthorne College
of Enchantment. Appears only in the interlude session DM’d by Pat; see
2023-10-08 and jakedm Unresolved for
this session’s disconnect from the rest of the campaign.
History

Discovers library evidence a demi-lich may still be alive, and a field report about a map to the Tomb
of Horrors 2023-10-08 @ 00:49:09, @ 00:56:17.
Summons Sarkhan Vol back to Hawthorne via arcane message @ 01:00:30.
Slips his research to Professor Bumblebee during a dull faculty meeting @ 01:15:25.
Fails to dispel or disrupt the cursed map’s illusion @ 01:34:04–01:41:38.
Shares an identical dream with Sarkhan and accepts a Revelation Crystal from a skeleton child, waking
with a brand @ 01:56:37–01:58:19.
Bluffs and barters stockroom clerk Bart into lending crafting materials for bottles of air @ 02:48:26–02:59:42.

Unresolved
No later session returns to Jace, Sarkhan, or the Tomb of Horrors expedition.

pcs/jacques-luceau.title: Jacques Luceau
pcs/jacques-luceau.content:
Also heard as: Woo-woo, Wu, JB, Woo, Jake's monk
A Vanara (monkey-folk) monk, fighting with flurry of blows and later elemental (electricity, then fire)
-infused unarmed strikes. His name, Jacques Luceau, is only stated once on mic; he’s addressed by various
nicknames across sessions (Woo-woo, Wu, JB), which may reflect genuine in-fiction nicknames or
transcription drift — see Unresolved.
History

Owns the Shadow Well (a portable-hole-like item) and forces a goblin guide into manacles
2022-12-06 @ 01:17:14, @ 01:31:00.
Throws his dinner roll at Strahd, triggering the castle-wide lockdown that opens
the dungeon crawl 2022-12-18 @ 00:43:04.
Knocks out the deranged lantern servant nonlethally and loots his lantern and keys
2022-12-18 @ 01:56:11–02:01:03.
Escapes into the Ethereal Plane to survive the burning gas-trap room
2022-12-26 @ 01:19:14.
Braves the active fire trap to claim a shapeshifting magic sword, later identified as the
Sun Sword’s blade 2022-12-26 @ 03:58:19–03:59:58.
Knocks out a chained goblin accountant with a neck chop
2023-01-30 @ 00:22:31.
Co-invents “piss coat” with Todd to bend warded bars using a urine-soaked hide
2023-01-30 @ 04:25:30.
Dropped to -17 HP by a domination-forced sneak attack from Jess’s character; saved only by the party
burning its last two Fate Points on a reroll
2023-02-12 @ 01:20:30–01:30:46.
Lands two flaming Hurricane Kicks on Strahd, damaging him even in mist form
2023-02-12 @ 02:10:47, @ 02:22:21.
Takes heavy Constitution damage from golem poison breath but helps finish off both golems with
elemental-infused strikes 2023-03-12 @ 01:42:55, @ 02:12:36.
Is dominated by Donovan during his reveal as a traitor, and pulls a hot gem from a demon’s
corpse, swallows it, then vomits it back up after hearing whispers from it
2023-03-18.
Weighs Lightning Reflexes against Combat Reflexes on leveling up to 7th
2023-03-18 @ 00:38:38.

Unresolved
Whether “Woo-woo”/“Wu” and “JB” are both genuine in-fiction nicknames for Jacques, or the result of
transcription drift across sessions, is unclear — by the mistform session, “Woo” is instead applied to
Ozan’s character, raising the possibility of a mid-campaign nickname swap or
transcription confusion between the two players’ characters
2023-02-12.

pcs/jess's-witch.title: Jess's Witch
pcs/jess's-witch.content:
Jess’s witch, owner of a ferret familiar (Enfield) and later of the folding boat “Nessie”; revealed in
session 5 to be a changeling rather than human. Never given a real character name on mic.
History

Introduced as a witch with a ferret familiar, Enfield; a whimsy-table roll gives her a folding boat,
and a separate roll turns her into a weasel for the session
2023-09-12 @ 01:57:49, @ 02:20:35.
Casts Deep Slumber, putting enemies to sleep; jokingly nicknamed “Volvo Morton” by Pat (a pun on her
Discord handle); logs off mid-combat, tired, needing to be up for work at dawn
2023-10-01 @ 01:03:33, @ 01:04:53, @ 03:26:10.
Rolls a 30 (not a natural 20, despite Jake’s assumption) identifying the drained
soul device as plane-crossing; names her folding boat “Nessie” and summons it in its
full ship form (cabin, holds 15); revealed as a changeling
2023-10-24 @ 00:21:49–00:22:07, @ 00:43:45–00:44:41,
@ 00:46:17.
Curses carpet-maker Greg to compulsively count every board in his shop after a sponsorship deal
collapses 2023-10-24 @ 03:15:01–03:18:00.
Not listed in the session 6 party.

Unresolved
Her character’s real name is never given; “Volvo Morton” is a joke nickname, not a stated in-fiction
name. Across all three sessions she appears in, both Jake (DM) and the other players address her
exclusively as “Jess” — her real name — even in clearly in-character lines, including the scene where she
explicitly identifies as a changeling rather than human
2023-10-24 @ 00:46:09–00:46:17. No distinct in-fiction name
was ever used as an alternative.

pcs/jim-jones.title: Jim Jones
pcs/jim-jones.content:
Also heard as: the Oracle, Connor's Oracle, unnamed cursed Oracle
Connor’s human Oracle, afflicted with the Covetous curse (must wear 500gp+ of finery). “Jim Jones” is a
table nickname for the character’s cult-leader-flavored curse flavor, not a stated character name — his
real name is never given.
History

Introduced as a Heaven’s Oracle with the Covetous curse; this is his first time playing D&D, per the
table 2023-09-12 @ 01:39:48, @ 03:35:51.
Casts a memory-lapse spell on a guard who’d learned Mary’s location, wiping the last five minutes of
his memory and triggering it when he drops a coin
2023-09-12 @ 03:36:31–03:36:52.
Seen after the heist outside the bank handing out pamphlets with a falafel, apparently recruiting for a
cult 2023-10-01 @ 03:33:45.
Opens the doppelganger ambush with a surprise-round Hypnotic Pattern boosted by his Awesome Display
revelation; caught in the blast radius of Pat’s own fire spell; escapes the firestorm by swimming a
canal with a water-breathing spell 2023-10-15 @ 00:05:02,
@ 00:21:51, @ 01:29:43.
Present in session 5 with no race/class restated.
As an unnamed, lawful-evil cursed Oracle with a +1 chainmail attuned to an “ocular mystery” revelation,
present throughout session 6 without a distinguishing scene
2023-11-28 @ 00:52:30, @ 00:56:35.

Unresolved
His actual character name is never stated in any session; “Jim Jones” is purely a table joke about his
Covetous-curse flavor.

pcs/kurt-furbane.title: Kurt Furbane
pcs/kurt-furbane.content:
Also heard as: Kurt Furbank, Ozan's bard
Ozan’s Arc I character, a bard from the plane of Nirvana who teleports aboard the party’s ship and talks
his way into joining the crew. A character also called “Kurt Furbank,” with a different player and class,
appears later in the arc — see Unresolved.
History

Teleports aboard the ship via dimension door, nearly gets attacked by Nutty’s character, and joins the
crew after a charming bardic performance
2020-01-28 @ 00:17:59–02:10:34.
Ozan’s character — unnamed on-mic, a bard-like fey being with moth-like wings — performs music for
party buffs during the church-demon fight 2020-04-13
@ 00:11:46, @ 02:37:47.

Unresolved
A character named “Kurt Furbank,” played by Nutty and described as a rogue/sneak-attack type with magic
flying armor, lands the finishing blow on the glabrezu demon in
2020-04-13 @ 03:35:05. Whether this is the same character
(recast or misattributed in the notes) or an unrelated character who happens to share a near-identical
name is not resolved in the transcripts.

pcs/miss-cleo.title: Miss Cleo
pcs/miss-cleo.content:
Also heard as: Ozan's psychic, Ozan's bard-type (Arc II)
Ozan’s Arc II character, a psychic/bard-type with telepathy, memory-sharing, stoneskin, and buff/support
spells.
History

Shares two childhood memories with Alexander via psychic link to help him answer the Sphinx’s first
riddle 2021-10-19 @ 00:41:50.
Touches the riddle pad herself and nearly dies (dropped to 2 HP) botching the second riddle twice before
Nutty works out the answer 2021-10-19 @ 01:00:36–01:30:00.
Tells a stranger’s fortune at a town festival, has a true psychic vision of her murder that night, and
geases the woman’s companion instead of warning her directly
2021-10-19 @ 01:46:06–01:50:02.
Stays behind at the one-way portal with the now-sentient Sphinx Painting rather than step through
2021-10-19 @ 03:02:21.
Rolls the highest initiative (23) of the frost giant fight and buffs the party with stoneskin
2021-11-02 @ 00:05:25, @ 00:15:11.
Uses hideous laughter to leave the mimic prone and cackling before Rich kills it
2021-11-02 @ 01:55:17–01:55:50.

Unresolved
Whether Ozan’s vision of the fortune-telling woman’s murder was ever acted on further is not shown; the
outcome of the geas he placed on her companion is never revealed.

pcs/mori-yoshinari.title: Mori Yoshinari
pcs/mori-yoshinari.content:
Also heard as: Donovan, Donnie's character, the ship's captain
Donnie’s Arc I character: the party’s ship captain, bonded to the ship’s enslaved air elemental, wanted
by the Church of St. Cuthbert. Named “Mori Yoshinari” from
2020-01-28 onward; earlier sessions call him only “Donovan” or
“Donnie’s character,” with inconsistent class descriptions (Sword Saint samurai in the first recorded
session, a cleric-type with Use Magic Device by the time he becomes captain) — treated here as one
continuous character, with the discrepancy flagged below.
History

As a Sword Saint (samurai), lawful evil, uses iaijutsu strikes and survives near-death via Resolve and
fate points 2019-10-15 @ 01:56:31–02:00:47.
Finds the dead mage’s journal of planar cosmology aboard the looted ship
2020-01-20 @ 00:20:38.
Touches the ship’s planar crystal directly, triggering an accidental plane shift
2020-01-20 @ 01:02:51.
Elected the party’s Captain @ 02:40:23, then speaks the command word “Pop Jack,” permanently bonding
with the ship’s air elemental
2020-01-20 @ 02:40:23, @ 02:44:25–02:44:38.
Named “Mori Yoshinari” for the first time by a Church of St. Cuthbert priest, who recognizes him as “the
cat folk that seem to have caused issues with the church this year” and has been tracking him across
continents; the specific crime is never stated on mic (a previous session’s party-vs-paladin fight is a
plausible but unconfirmed link) 2020-01-28 @ 01:07:45–01:09:21.
The timestamp previously cited here, @ 00:52:22, is an unrelated scene (Donnie blacksmith-shopping).
Commissions mithril +3 “Eastern” armor and an enchanted katana in Neo
2020-01-28 @ 01:24:28–01:35:43.
Reveals the lore on how the Apocalypse Box can be destroyed (three survived monster-waves, then a
gold dragon crushing it) 2020-03-16 @ 00:44:54.
Straps drow bodies to the ship’s bloodletting tables to refuel it after escaping Hell
2020-03-25 @ 00:55:49.
Pilots the ship’s interplanar jump that accidentally lands the party in the Feywild instead of home
2020-03-25 @ 02:31:40–02:36:13.
Turned to stone by a basilisk and remains petrified for the entire session
2020-04-06 @ 00:24:06.
Fights in mithril plate with his katana in the temple battle against the glabrezu demon
2020-04-13 @ 03:08:50.

Unresolved
His class/fluff shifts across sessions — Sword Saint samurai, then a cleric-type with Use Magic Device,
then described again as a “samurai/fighter type” — without any in-game explanation; likely imprecise
session notes rather than an in-fiction change. It is unclear whether this is the same character Donnie
plays in the 2021 sessions as Fish, or a new character rolled after an off-screen gap.

pcs/nutty's-arcane-combatant-(dungeonvic.title: Nutty's Arcane Combatant (DungeonVice)
pcs/nutty's-arcane-combatant-(dungeonvic.content:
Nutty’s character in the DungeonVice campaign: an arcane combatant wielding a bladed tail weapon (treated
as a scimitar), casting Web and a touch-spell/weapon combo nicknamed “Washashaka” (also heard as
“Walshashah”). Speaks Common, Elven, Dwarf, Draconic, and Abyssal. Never named on mic in session 3.
History

Fights in the warehouse blind-crossfire alongside Ozone after Glitter Dust drops the guards
2025-03-31 @ 01:15:07.
Reminded by Jake of two forgotten magic items: the tail weapon and Ozone’s “Whoop Whoop” whistle
2025-03-31 @ 01:28:59.
Catches up to Rich downstairs and, flanking with him, finishes off Fugly with a combined
weapon-and-shocking-grasp strike (“Washashaka”) 2025-03-31
@ 02:46:05-02:48:22.
Gives Ozone a Ring of Protection +1 after the party levels up
2025-03-31 @ 03:19:55.

Unresolved
No proper name was given on mic for this character in session 3; the “Washashaka”/“Walshashah” ability
name is likely a mangled homebrew term 2025-03-31 @ 02:46:05, @ 02:46:46.
Jake (DM) addresses Nutty exclusively by his real name throughout the session, including mid-combat
callouts (“Nutty, Nutty making attack of opportunity” @ 02:05:46, “Nutty killed this motherfucker”
@ 02:47:54) — no distinct character name is ever substituted. Sessions 1–2 of this campaign, where the
character may have been introduced, are not yet transcribed.

pcs/nutty's-healer-(arc-i).title: Nutty's Healer (Arc I)
pcs/nutty's-healer-(arc-i).content:
Also heard as: Nutty's character, the possessed healer
Nutty’s Arc I character, an alchemist/healer whose body is unknowingly possessed by a demon for several
sessions after Nutty touches a cursed soul gem — a secret even Nutty’s own player hadn’t fully known until
it was revealed in-game.
History

Identifies the Ring of the Hive Mind with a natural 20 Knowledge: Arcana check
2020-01-20 @ 00:03:52.
Unknowingly possessed by a demon from a touched soul gem sometime before this session’s events are
recapped 2020-03-24 @ 02:43:50.
As the possessing demon, kills Ozan’s character and then the unconscious Tick-Tick
2020-03-24 @ 01:59:28, @ 02:22:31.
The demon is banished by the newly-reborn Paladin of Pelor; Nutty wakes disoriented, describing himself
as “an empty vessel” 2020-03-24 @ 02:50:25.
Soul restored to his body via the recovered soul gem after roughly a day and a half trapped inside it
2020-03-25 @ 00:42:10–00:44:47.
Opens the side door that leads to finding Obadiah Jones frozen in ice
2020-04-06 @ 00:49:11.

Unresolved
This character’s name is never stated in the recorded sessions. Across all four sessions he appears in,
Pat (DM) and the other players address him exclusively as “Nutty” — his real name — including during the
possession/killing scene itself 2020-03-24.
No in-fiction alternative name was ever used.

pcs/obadiah-jones.title: Obadiah Jones
pcs/obadiah-jones.content:
A Loxodon cleric, chaotic good, found frozen in ice by the party and freed mid-session; joins the party as
a new PC played by Ryan, a new player this session.
Summary
Obadiah had come looking for an ancient church tied to his unnamed deity alongside an adventuring party of
fellow loxodons, all of whom starved to death around him while he was frozen. He has no memory of how he
ended up sealed in ice.
History

Found frozen in a stone dais, elephant-headed, inside a man-sized block of ice beside his dead former
party’s skeletons 2020-04-06 @ 00:49:11.
Freed when Rich’s summoned fire elementals finally melt the ice; wakes disoriented, cold, and covered in
urine from the party’s earlier attempts to thaw him
2020-04-06 @ 01:45:29.
Casts Terrible Remorse on the demon holding Jake, staggering it for a round
2020-04-06 @ 02:05:59.
Fights in the temple battle against the glabrezu demon, falling back to support casting when his
offensive spells keep fizzling against its spell resistance
2020-04-13 @ 00:48:37 (ceremony/aftermath context).

Unresolved
His deity’s name and the “ancient church” he was seeking are never established in the recorded sessions.

pcs/ozan's-alchemist.title: Ozan's Alchemist
pcs/ozan's-alchemist.content:
Also heard as: Zendrick, Lobel, Nadi, Nadia, Woo, Wubu Tang
An alchemist/investigator-type character played by Ozan — AC 22, mithril shirt, thieves’ tools, low
Strength and high Dexterity. Handles most of the party’s perception, lockpicking, and disable-device
checks, brews and shares potions via “alchemical allocation,” and uses tanglefoot bags and Poison Lore in
a fight. The character’s name is never consistently stated; see Unresolved.
History

Fails to pick the dining hall’s locked bronze door, then buffs Ulumbra with an alchemical
“ablative barrier” extract 2022-12-18
@ 00:37:42, @ 01:14:41.
Spots the magical glow and gold piles across the flooded dungeon’s cells, then triggers a hidden poison
gas mechanism while looting them
2022-12-26 @ 00:38:55, @ 01:15:42.
Picks the final lock to free Jess’s character from a burning cell
2022-12-26 @ 03:53:00.
Frees the prisoner Murph, who immediately re-triggers a teleport trap
2022-12-26 @ 03:04:37–03:07:18.
Loots the Vonderbux family signet ring from an empty crypt in the catacombs
2023-01-30 @ 02:18:27.
Resists Strahd’s domination gaze alongside Xarthax during the boss fight
2023-02-12 @ 01:00:30.
Fails a save prying open Strahd’s coffin with a shield and turns to stone, restored by Xarthax’s Dispel
Magic 2023-02-12 @ 00:30:57–00:36:18.
Spots the riddle on the hourglass trap and disarms the golden chest’s trap
2023-03-12 @ 00:24:30–00:34:48.
Feeds Todd a Barkskin potion mid-fight and burns a Fate Point to keep Alumbra conscious after her
critical fumble between the two golems 2023-03-12 @ 01:17:30, @ 01:37:45.
Identifies the golems’ poison via Poison Lore and brews an antidote overnight, curing Wu and Alumbra
2023-03-12 @ 02:35:17–02:38:36.
Absent from the next two sessions; his potions are used remotely by the party as an NPC healing source
2023-03-18 @ 00:15:32.

Unresolved
The character’s name is never consistently stated. Candidates considered and rejected:

“Zendrick” — said once by Pat (DM), “That’s correct, Zendrick”
2022-12-18 @ 00:28:15; no second independent
line anywhere in the corpus uses it.
“Lobel” — said once by Pat while reading out a VTT token setting (“Lobel, you’re as a human”)
2022-12-26 @ 00:53:37; likely a token/display
name rather than a spoken in-fiction name, and not repeated elsewhere.
“Woo-Woo”/“Wubu Tang” — used in the mistform session, but this is a joking exchange (“My name is Woo
Woo”/“I’m with Wubu. Wubu Tang.”) 2023-02-12 @ 00:25:34,
@ 00:25:48, and “Woo-woo” is also the established nickname for
Jake’s monk character, confirmed by name in the chat log the same campaign
2022-12-18 @ 00:24:07-00:24:08 — too
ambiguous/joking to accept as this character’s name.
“Nadi”/“Nadia” — by far the most frequent, heard dozens of times, but it recurs across entirely
unrelated campaigns and characters spanning 2020 (“The Gang”) through 2025 (DungeonVice), addressed to
Ozan regardless of which character he’s playing — e.g.
2020-09-28, 2020-04-13,
2023-10-01, and the DungeonVice session 3 transcript. This
pattern strongly suggests “Nadi”/“Nadia” is an out-of-character nickname for Ozan himself (used
alongside “Ozan”/“Ozone”), not an in-fiction name specific to this Ravenloft alchemist.

pcs/ozone.title: Ozone
pcs/ozone.content:
Also heard as: Ozan's character, Mr. Vajidkas
Ozan’s bard-type character in the DungeonVice campaign, going by the disguised alias “Mr. Vajidkas” (“from
Kazakhstan”) during the dockworker con. Uses a disguise kit/hat of disguise, a net as signature weapon, an
oratory bardic performance (“Pirate’s Courage”), Glitter Dust, Knowledge (religion), and channels positive
energy to heal. Speaks Common and Goblin.
History
