Flirts his way into the confidence of the captured prisoner, Riggs’s Widow, learning about
Riggs, the Golden Ticket to the Devil, and the College of Turgeth Drug Pipeline
2025-03-31 @ 00:15:20-00:24:08.
Poses as “Mr. Vajidkas” to befriend drunk dockworker Dex, trading moonshine and cocaine for intel,
before Dex reveals himself as a lookout 2025-03-31 @ 00:56:49-01:05:14.
Casts Glitter Dust, blinding the warehouse guards; blinded, they miss their shots (one hits a wall, one
grazes an ally) and the party cuts them down on attacks of opportunity as they flail and flee
2025-03-31 @ 01:15:07-01:20:04.
Reminded of his forgotten “Whoop Whoop” whistle item 2025-03-31 @ 01:28:59.
Heals himself and the party with Channel Positive Energy and looted potions
2025-03-31 @ 03:03:51-03:06:27.
Torches the warehouse with a tossed cigarette as he and Nutty retreat
2025-03-31 @ 03:13:57-03:14:24.
Receives a Ring of Protection +1 from Nutty’s Arcane Combatant (DungeonVice)
2025-03-31 @ 03:19:55.

pcs/pat's-wizard-(dungeonvice).title: Pat's Wizard (DungeonVice)
pcs/pat's-wizard-(dungeonvice).content:
Pat’s character in the DungeonVice campaign: a wizard. Not to be confused with Pat’s Wizard from
JakeDM’s 2023 campaign — a different character in a different campaign. Pat was away for nearly all of
session 3, so little is known about this character yet.
History

Casts Mage Armor on Rich’s Monk (DungeonVice) before the mission, then is AFK/absent for nearly the
entire session, acting as lookout 2025-03-31 @ 00:48:40, @ 02:14:35.
Returns to find the party already leveled up without him; will level up a session behind the others
2025-03-31 @ 03:18:05, @ 03:18:18.

Unresolved
No proper name, race, or further build detail was given on mic in session 3, since Pat was absent for
almost the whole session. Jake (DM) and the other players address him exclusively as “Pat” throughout,
including his one in-character exclamation on returning (“Oh, son of a bitch”)
2025-03-31 @ 03:18:18, @ 03:18:34. Sessions 1–2 of this campaign, where the
character may have been introduced, are not yet transcribed.

pcs/pat's-wizard.title: Pat's Wizard
pcs/pat's-wizard.content:
Pat’s main-arc character: a tiefling with a prehensile tail, a wood-mage wizard who later also casts
spells described as sorcerous. Never named on mic across any of the five main-arc sessions.
History

Introduced as a tiefling wood mage/wizard; uses the Wand of Memory Lapse on Mary twice to erase
an awkward encounter at her door, and later again after Connor insults her; conjures a wooden stick and
throws it at an attacking goblin family, accidentally killing the goblin father when he falls off a
balcony 2023-09-12 @ 02:56:41, @ 03:06:06,
@ 03:24:07, @ 03:43:33.
Flies the heist’s loot chest to the bank roof and loots it into a bag of holding
2023-10-01 @ 02:42:00–03:57:41.
Casts the new spell Cicero/Sirocco, a furnace-hot blast that triggers the Dyson Dynamo’s citywide
firestorm; flies Ozan out of the blaze; sets up a refugee triage camp afterward
2023-10-15 @ 00:21:51, @ 01:30:03, @ 01:49:39.
Fails to buy the spell Skeleton Crew from a refugee wizard; scries on Cadillac for seven minutes; casts
Fly on the party’s boat and hands control to his familiar, a luck dragon named Randy; trips a magical
Alarm sneaking disguised into Lutathal 2023-10-24
@ 00:38:18, @ 00:49:09–00:54:54, @ 01:08:23, @ 01:38:37.
Casts the “Neuralizer” memory-lapse spell on a TIU investigator mid-interrogation; later
intimidates/bluffs a carpet shopkeeper out of a discarded firework carpet and Neuralizes him too, to
cover up admitting the carpet will be raced
2023-11-28 @ 00:46:48, @ 01:52:22–01:56:28.

Unresolved
Described as a wizard (wood-mage specialist) in sessions 1, 2, and 4, but as a “sorcerer” with an
improved familiar in session 5 — never explained on-mic whether this is a class change, multiclass, or
just loose terminology. His character name is never stated in any session; Jake (DM) and the other
players address him exclusively as “Pat” across all five sessions, including in clearly in-character
moments (e.g. casting the Wand of Memory Lapse, the “Neuralizer” interrogation scene)
2023-09-12,
2023-11-28.

pcs/raven.title: Raven
pcs/raven.content:
Also heard as: Donovan, Johnny, Jonathan
A human witch, roughly 50 years old and twice divorced, with a familiar zoog that prefers eating sentient
beings. Casts hexes (Misfortune, Cackle, Ear-Piercing Scream, Evil Eye), Cure Light Wounds, Fly, Remove
Curse, and Air Bubble. Dies partway through the campaign and rises as Strahd’s
vampire thrall under the name Donovan, ultimately betraying the party before being lost to the Astral
Plane.
History

Introduced as a human witch with a sentient-being-eating zoog familiar
2022-12-06 @ 00:46:55.
Casts Remove Curse on Irina with no effect
2022-12-06 @ 03:08:25.
Accidentally splashes Madame Eva with holy water, ending the tarot reading early
2022-12-06 @ 04:00:19.
Rejoins the party partway through the dinner session; casts Remove Curse to cure the familiar’s
cauldron-induced brain-craving 2022-12-18
@ 01:46:49, @ 02:08:49.
Pickpockets a chained bookkeeper for 333 gold undetected
2022-12-26 @ 04:22:30.
Flies down a 400+ foot shaft to scout the catacombs, then ferries party members down one at a time
2023-01-30 @ 01:54:00.
Splashes holy water on Sergei von Zarovich’s body, triggering a mind-link that reveals Strahd’s
murder of Sergei and Tatiana 2023-01-30 @ 04:00:19.
Chasing a lost familiar, crashes into the warded bars guarding Strahd’s coffin, is fatally drained, dies,
and rises on the spot as a chaotic-evil vampire thrall
2023-01-30 @ 04:56:54–05:19:31.
As “Donovan,” wins initiative and flees the party as mist through a gap near the ceiling, along with his
zoog 2023-02-12 @ 00:03:28–00:10:31.
Revealed to have secretly been serving Strahd the whole time, ambushing the party from a dark bedroom;
dominates Jake and summons a delayed pack of wolves
2023-03-18 @ 00:48:16 onward.
Dropped to 0 HP and turns to vampire gaseous/mist form; Jess scoops him into her handy haversack for
containment 2023-03-18
@ 02:04:54–02:06:49.
Flung into the Astral Plane when Todd (Nutty) destroys the haversack mid-fight; given two
hours to find a resting place or be destroyed forever — fate never resolved on-screen
2023-03-18 @ 02:30:46, @ 02:43:09.

Unresolved

The character’s real name is never cleanly stated — “Raven” is used before the vampirization, “Donovan”
afterward, and the DM calls her “Johnny”/“Jonathan” at least once, possibly a running joke rather than a
real name 2023-01-30 @ 03:39:55, @ 05:16:39.
Donovan’s fate after being flung into the Astral Plane is never shown or mentioned again in the recorded
sessions.

pcs/rich's-monk-(dungeonvice).title: Rich's Monk (DungeonVice)
pcs/rich's-monk-(dungeonvice).content:
Rich’s character in the DungeonVice campaign: a monk fighting with Crane Style, Stunning Strike, and
flurry of blows. Never named on mic in session 3. Carries the party’s shared platinum piece in his handy
haversack.
History

Mage-Armored by Pat’s Wizard (DungeonVice) before the mission; carries the party’s platinum piece
in his handy haversack 2025-03-31 @ 00:48:40, @ 00:51:08.
Punches open the warehouse door under fire to start the raid
2025-03-31 @ 01:08:22.
Sprints ahead alone toward a signal flare, runs past Fugly rather than stopping to fight, then
doubles back; Fugly follows him downstairs and nearly drops him with a 36-damage critical hit, before
Nutty arrives, flanks Fugly, and finishes him off — Rich then loots his Boots of Haste
2025-03-31 @ 01:37:48-02:49:34.
Activates the boots and turns ethereal, flies after the departing ship and spots The Boot himself,
unnoticed, ending the session mid-chase 2025-03-31 @ 02:58:23-03:02:43,
@ 03:09:40-03:10:13.

Unresolved
No proper name was given on mic for this character in session 3. Jake (DM) addresses Rich exclusively by
his real name throughout, including during his signature moments (the critical hit he takes, his
Boots of Haste chase) 2025-03-31 @ 01:55:23, @ 03:16:27. Sessions 1–2 of
this campaign, where the character may have been introduced, are not yet transcribed.

pcs/richard-findelberg.title: Richard Findelberg
pcs/richard-findelberg.content:
Rich’s android wizard/crafter/blaster sorcerer, immune to fatigue, exhaustion, and fear. Surname
“Findelberg” is given once, in session 5.
History

Introduced woken near a pile of bodies outside a snowy castle; no spellbook
2023-09-12 @ 03:13:10–03:14:15.
Repeatedly casts Lightning Bolt and Fireball during the vault brawl; casts Blind on Cadillac, who shrugs
it off with a successful save; wins a Broom of Flying on a roll-off meant for the absent Jess
2023-10-01 @ 00:54:01, @ 01:22:41, @ 03:28:22–03:36:35,
@ 04:27:03–04:27:29.
Casts Haste on the party; Dimension Doors the absent NPCs clear of the burning city; crafts his
Headband of Intellect up to +4, which comes with a haunted “eye” showing visions of the fire
2023-10-15 @ 00:27:11, @ 01:07:58, @ 02:03:00.
Confirms he still has his silver scrying mirror, lent to Pat to spy on Cadillac; crafts extra sleeves
of many garments overnight for the party
2023-10-24 @ 00:24:36, @ 00:56:19–01:00:01.
Absent from session 6; per the session’s recap, bartered into indentured “robot servant” service to
a rug shop by Frankie rather than pay for a carpet
2023-11-28 @ 00:12:38–00:13:23.

Unresolved
His character’s full name (“Richard Findelberg”) is only given once, in session 5 — earlier sessions use
only “Richard” or “Rich’s character.”

pcs/sarkhan-vol.title: Sarkhan Vol
pcs/sarkhan-vol.content:
Also heard as: Vol, Con, Khan
A human transmutation wizard, former combat mage for Hawthorne’s war effort who worships a dragon god and
keeps a fairy dragon familiar. Appears only in the interlude session DM’d by Pat; see
2023-10-08 and jakedm Unresolved for
this session’s disconnect from the rest of the campaign.
History

Teleports roughly 1,300 miles to Hawthorne in answer to Jace Gandolfini’s summons
2023-10-08 @ 01:03:49.
Shares an identical dream with Jace and accepts a Revelation Crystal from a skeleton child, waking with
a brand @ 01:56:37–01:58:19.
Uses his Revelation Crystal to dispel the cursed map’s illusion, revealing the route to the Tomb of
Horrors @ 02:01:41.
Buys and copies scrolls of Concealed Breath and Dispel Magic as backup against the Isle of Death’s
miasma @ 03:02:11–03:10:40.

Unresolved
His nickname is transcribed inconsistently as “Con,” “Khan,” “Kavík,” and “Kansvæin”; “Sarkhan Vol” is
used here on the strength of an explicit Magic: The Gathering reference at the table
2023-10-08 @ 02:04:11–02:04:26. No later session
returns to this character.

pcs/seabreeze.title: Seabreeze
pcs/seabreeze.content:
Also heard as: Rick, Nutty's Strix, Nutty's Druid
Nutty’s character: a Strix (“birdman”) fighter/archer. Named “Rick, aka Seabreeze” in session 2.
History

Introduced as a Strix fighter/archer 2023-09-12
@ 03:13:43.
Named “Rick, aka Seabreeze”; dogfights and shoots down an enemy druid NPC who wild-shaped into a crow
(the “Druid” is the enemy, not Seabreeze’s own class) 2023-10-01
@ 03:06:08, @ 03:31:06.
Flies up and shoots dead the doppelganger carrying the Dyson Dynamo
2023-10-15 @ 00:36:05.
Signs into Lutathal under the joke alias “Bertha” 2023-10-24
@ 03:29:18.
Not listed in the session 6 party.

Unresolved
None outstanding — the apparent “Druid” discrepancy in session 2 was an enemy NPC druid (killed by
Seabreeze mid-dogfight), not Seabreeze’s own class.

pcs/tick-tick.title: Tick-Tick
pcs/tick-tick.content:
Also heard as: Jake's druid, Paladin of Pelor, Jake Bins, Shake Fins
Jake’s Arc I character: an elf druid who became the cursed, compelled bearer of the Apocalypse Box,
died, and was reborn a Paladin of Pelor. Likely (though not explicitly confirmed) the same character as
the unnamed divine shapeshifter Jake plays starting 2020-01-20
— the name “Tick-Tick” only appears starting the Apocalypse Box arc.
History

As an unnamed divine caster, shapeshifts into a bird/falcon and carries an immovable rod
2020-01-20 @ 01:56:05.
Shapechanged into falcon/bat forms exploring Spider Heaven with an Allosaurus companion
2020-03-16 @ 00:34:16.
Fails a DC 30 will save on the newly-appeared Apocalypse Box and is magically compelled to seize
and guard it by any means, including violence against friends
2020-03-16 @ 00:22:04.
Flees with the box to the ship; opens it under the Apocalypse Box’s curse, risking Shoggoth summons
each day 2020-03-16 @ 00:40:06.
Named “Tick-Tick” for the first time; the party debates killing him to stop the box’s eventual
destruction of the plane 2020-03-24 @ 00:30:49.
Loses 40%+ of his blood volume bleeding the ship’s engine, goes into cardiac arrest, and is later killed
by the demon possessing Nutty while unconscious
2020-03-24 @ 00:58:36, @ 02:22:31.
Dies and, with his final breath, communes with Pelor; his body dissolves and reforms as an armored
Paladin of Pelor wielding a golden scythe, free of the Apocalypse Box’s curse
2020-03-24 @ 02:38:22.
As the new Paladin, banishes the demon possessing Nutty with his holy symbol
2020-03-24 @ 02:42:10.
Heals Nutty with Lay on Hands after his soul is restored to his body
2020-03-25 @ 00:20:28 (approx., following soul restoration).
Lands a critical smite on the soul-sucking demon in the puzzle room
2020-03-25 @ 01:23:56.
Grappled, dragged into the Ethereal Plane by a demon, and strength-drained to 0 and unconscious
2020-04-06 @ 01:31:42–01:59:08.
Back and active by the next session; gets forcibly thrown out of a knighting ceremony over a joke and
challenged to a duel to the death 2020-04-13 @ 01:43:28.
Fires a smiting arrow into the glabrezu demon during the temple fight
2020-04-13 @ 03:16:05.

Unresolved
The mechanism by which the party recovered Tick-Tick from the Ethereal Plane between sessions is never
shown on-screen. His duel to the death, scheduled for the morning after
2020-04-13, is interrupted by the demon fight and never
revisited in the recorded sessions.

pcs/todd-stone.title: Todd Stone
pcs/todd-stone.content:
Also heard as: Todd, Tad
A human fighter who fights with two spike shields, carries the party’s torches, and has no darkvision.
The most consistently-named and stable PC across the whole Ravenloft campaign; AC climbs to 24+ (26
fighting defensively, higher still with buffs) by the later sessions.
History

Introduced carrying two spike shields at the roadside inn
2022-12-06 @ 00:16:20.
Learns from Madame Eva’s tarot vision that he does not die to a vampire, but chokes on a sausage
decades later 2022-12-06 @ 03:45:11.
Bumps a suit of armor with someone breathing inside it, interrupting Strahd’s organ music
2022-12-18 @ 00:31:45.
Sets the Strahd decoy mannequin on fire, then critically fumbles a thrown shield into his own face and
stuns himself 2022-12-18 @ 00:53:45, @ 01:29:07.
Falls through a trap door into the flooded lower dungeon and finds a gold-filled treasure chest
2022-12-18 @ 02:22:33–02:31:28.
Trapped at the bottom of a hundred-foot funnel shaft with Ozan’s character, across from gold-filled
cells 2022-12-26 @ 00:34:37.
Ignites a poison gas trap by throwing a lit torch into it to test flammability, starting a fire that
burns for the rest of the session
2022-12-26 @ 01:17:44–01:18:21.
Spends many rounds breaking down a reinforced door to free the prisoner Murph
2022-12-26 @ 02:58:23–03:03:16.
Tanks at the top of a stairwell against two golems, dropping a looted chest mid-flight to survive
2023-03-12 @ 00:59:51–01:00:50.
Trying to help free Donovan’s mist form from a handy haversack, destroys the haversack
instead, tearing open a gate to the Astral Plane
2023-03-18 @ 00:21:03–00:24:21
(approximate).
Finds a previously-rescued prisoner dead, eyes removed, and presses on alone toward a tower with a
pulsing red glass “heart” as the session ends
2023-03-18 @ end of session.
Continues exploring the upper dungeon alone while the rest of the party rests at low HP, avoiding a
spiderweb-filled room and fixating on the pulsating red light
2023-03-18 @ 00:02:46–00:03:14.

Unresolved
Todd’s class/build is mostly inferred from play (shields, Strength, tanking) rather than ever stated
outright on-mic 2023-03-12.

pcs/xarthax.title: Xarthax
pcs/xarthax.content:
Also heard as: Zyrtax, Zarthax, Zarafax, Czarthax, Jacques (session 3 mishearing)
An android arcane caster — doesn’t eat, doesn’t sleep, immune to necrotic damage, fear, aging, and
mind-affecting effects (having no flesh or mind to affect in the usual sense). Casts Mage Armor, Shield,
Shocking Grasp, Mirror Image, Dispel Magic, Fly, Fireball, and Magic Missile, among others. Carries gloves
of reconnaissance that let him see five feet through solid material.
History

Casts Fly to rejoin the party in the flooded dungeon
2022-12-18 @ 02:35:40.
Fireball wipes most of a ten-skeleton ambush in the rotting cell corridor
2022-12-18 @ 01:19:21–01:22:17.
Identifies the Tome of Strahd via Knowledge (History)
2022-12-18 @ 02:12:35.
Flies into the burning gas-trap room to rescue party members
2022-12-26 @ 01:37:34–01:48:02.
Identifies Jake’s shapeshifting sword as the Sun Sword via Spellcraft
2023-01-30 @ 04:10:16.
Resists Strahd’s domination gaze and opens the boss fight with a fireball
2023-02-12 @ 01:00:30, @ 01:05:52.
Restores Woo from petrification with Dispel Magic after Woo fails a save prying
open Strahd’s coffin 2023-02-12 @ 00:34:21–00:36:18.
Blasts open a DC 40 locked door with a scroll of Knock (rolling 43) right as the room’s two iron golems
animate 2023-03-12 @ 00:44:19.
Finishes off the second iron golem with Magic Missile
2023-03-12 @ 02:29:01.
Tanks the servants’-dining-hall ghost ambush almost single-handedly, being immune to the ghosts’ aging
and fear/mind effects — the table later concludes this immunity was the only thing stopping a total
party wipe 2023-03-18,
2023-03-18 @ 00:56:44–00:57:14.
Weighs 4th-level wizard spell picks (Stoneskin, Dimension Door, Ball Lightning, Permanency) on leveling
up to 7th 2023-03-18 @ 00:40:48–01:04:00.

Unresolved
Xarthax’s proper name is never stated on mic in several sessions, and session 1 instead describes “Rich’s
character” as an unnamed drow bard carrying the Aegis of Recovery, with a separate absent “Jeff’s
character” as a mage-type carrying the Scabbard of Keen Edges. Whether Xarthax (who first appears by name
in session 2) is meant to be a continuation of either of those session-1 characters, or an unconnected
replacement, is never addressed in the transcripts
2022-12-06.

places/acatlalco.title: Acatlalco
places/acatlalco.content:
A mountain range/region within the Kingdom of Squiyles (4885 era) from which trolls begin pouring out
in large, slow-moving droves, straining the kingdom during its war with Binneth.
History

Trolls are sighted moving out of the Acatlalco mountain ranges in Squiyles, reported independently by
trappers and hunters in both Totezatlan and Somic; the King of Squiyles makes no public statement,
and foothill farmers begin independent evacuation plans 2019-06-10.
Continues to feed the troll migration into the wider Troll Mountains through and after the war
2019-10-07.

Unresolved
A region/city called “Acatlalco” also appears as part of Godoy’s geography in the JakeDM campaign
(2023 real-world / unspecified far-future in-world date): “Godoy City, Acatlalco, Western Territories.”
The two uses of the name are centuries (at least) apart in-world and on vastly different scales (a
mountain range vs. a city’s administrative region) — recorded as a naming echo only, not a confirmed
link. See Godoy’s Unresolved section.

places/balnaskor-mountains.title: Balnaskor Mountains
places/balnaskor-mountains.content:
Also heard as: Balneskor, Balneskor Mountains
A snowy mountain range home to sparse snow-dwelling orc clans, a family-run goblin inn, and rumors of a
mysterious fog-shrouded town. The Gazette spells the range both “Balnaskor” and “Balneskor” across the
same pair of issues.
History

A wealthy goblin noble, ‘Narfuuuk’, places a 10,000 gold piece bounty after his nephew is kidnapped
from the family’s inn here by a group of adventurers seen leading him away in manacles, suspected
(unconfirmed) of operating as slavers 2022-12-18, 2022-12-26.
Timothy Mantooth, Rex Sauvage’s successor as the Gazette’s field reporter, dispatches from the
snowy Balnaskor range, gathering stories from local orc clans — including rumors of “a mysterious
mountain town enveloped in an inescapable fog” 2022-12-18.

places/beisfjord.title: Beisfjord
places/beisfjord.content:
A city in the Kingdom of Binneth where captured orc intelligence is delivered.
History

Binneth’s Royal-Elites return here to present a captured orc scout and his sending stone to Captain
Vakrum, the first direct evidence of the orcish invasion reaching Binneth soil
2019-04-29.
The lone surviving scout mutilated by Gorthak’s forces makes it back to Beisfjord carrying
Gorthak’s demand for Zakmed’s return before dying of an untreated wound infection
2019-06-10.

places/bostur.title: Bostur
places/bostur.content:
Also heard as: Bostur City
A city in the Kingdom of Squiyles, sacked by the Nayesche Orc tribe in the attack that kicks off the
Binneth–Squiyles-era orcish incursion — the event the press dubs “Bloody Tuesday.”
History

City Hall is razed and Duke Harrington is beheaded, his head paraded through the streets, during the
Nayesche attack dubbed “Bloody Tuesday”; plans begin for an orcish “conquest-hall” to replace City
Hall 2019-04-09.
Gorthak (credited here under the spellings “Garthok”/“Gorthuk”) is interviewed on-site, feasting
on the remains of locals and proclaiming dominance over the land 2019-04-09.

places/bringska.title: Bringska
places/bringska.content:
A small town in the Kingdom of Hawkthorne, site of a bizarre reality rift in its town square.
History

A rip in reality — a strange, colorful “wall” — opens in the town square. People who jump through
gain random effects: telekinesis, pockets full of jewels, hair loss, uncontrollable hysterical
laughter; the last person to enter is pulled through the ground screaming and never seen again.
Authorities seal the wall in stone 2019-06-24.

places/cacoal.title: Cacoal
places/cacoal.content:
A country whose capital is Ezaso City, fully overrun by doppelgangers partway through the
Binneth–Squiyles war and self-declared the “Changeling Nation.”
History

Established as the country containing the capital city Ezaso 2019-04-01.
Reported fully overrun, overtaken, and controlled by doppelgangers; its leaders declare it a
self-recognized nation and close it to outside entry. Former resident Gerard Twombly objects
publicly; King Stroth makes no statement 2019-07-15. See The Changeling Nation.

Unresolved
The 2019-04-01 issue places Cacoal/Ezaso under discussion alongside the Kingdom of Binneth’s royal
astronomer, while the 2019-04-09 and later issues place Conopimalis (the Gazette’s own home city) and
Ezaso firmly under the Kingdom of Squiyles — see Conopimalis (Erepec)‘s Unresolved note on this
same contradiction.

places/castle-ravenloft.title: Castle Ravenloft
places/castle-ravenloft.content:
Strahd von Zarovich’s castle, perched on cliffs overlooking Village of Barovia. The party enters
once, for a dinner invitation, and never leaves again for the rest of the recorded campaign — all six
subsequent sessions take place somewhere inside it.
Summary
Twin guardhouses and a 50-foot precipice guard a drawbridge; the massive main doors open on their own as
organ music drifts out. Inside, the castle is riddled with illusions, traps, and the preserved history of
Strahd’s family: a dining hall, a secret puppet room, a rotting cell corridor, a cauldron room, Strahd’s
personal chamber, a flooded lower dungeon, a spire-top prison cell, catacombs full of family crypts,
Strahd’s own coffin room, a golem-guarded puzzle chamber, and a tower topped with a pulsing red glass
“heart” that is never reached in the recorded sessions.
History

The party disembarks from a mysterious black carriage into the castle’s stormy courtyard; the doors
open on their own as the session ends
2022-12-06 @ 04:16:54–04:34:13.
Dinner with Strahd turns into a castle-wide lockdown after a thrown dinner roll;
the party finds a decoy mannequin, fights skeletons, finds the Tome of Strahd, and falls into a
flooded dungeon level 2022-12-18.
A poison-gas trap in the flooded basement is set ablaze and burns for most of a session; the party meets
Bartholomew and claims the Sun Sword’s blade (then unidentified) from the fire
2022-12-26.
A ghost ambush carries the party to a spire-top prison; below, the catacombs yield the deaths of
Sasha Ivliskova and Petrina Velikovna, and Donnie’s character is turned into a vampire
thrall near Strahd’s coffin 2023-01-30.
Strahd’s coffin is found empty, and the party is teleported into a brutal boss fight with Strahd himself
in his audience chamber 2023-02-12.
A riddle-trapped gargoyle room animates two iron golems, nearly killing Alumbra
2023-03-12.
Donovan is revealed as a traitor, dropped to 0 HP and contained in a haversack, then
accidentally flung into the Astral Plane when Todd destroys it; a servants’ dining hall ambush by ~400
ghosts nearly wipes the party
2023-03-18 @ 02:04:54, @ 02:30:46.
The party’s exploration halts mid-dungeon, near a tower with a pulsing red glass “heart,” when the
session’s battle map breaks — the last recorded session of the campaign
2023-03-18.

Unresolved
The castle is never fully mapped or cleared in the recorded sessions; the tower with the red glass heart
remains unexplored.

places/conopimalis-(erepec).title: Conopimalis (Erepec)
places/conopimalis-(erepec).content:
Also heard as: Conopimalis
The city housing Rugby’s Roaming Gazette’s original headquarters, in the region of Erepec. Its
kingdom allegiance is contradicted across the Gazette’s own early issues.
History

The 2019-04-01 issue’s masthead places Conopimalis, Erepec, in the Kingdom of Binneth
2019-04-01.
Every subsequent issue’s masthead (2019-04-09 onward) places Conopimalis, Erepec, in the Kingdom of
Squiyles instead 2019-04-09.
Serves as the Gazette’s base of operations until the fall of Squiyles, after which the paper
relocates to Stogath 2019-10-07.

Unresolved
The Gazette’s own masthead contradicts itself on which kingdom Conopimalis/Erepec belongs to: Binneth
in the first issue, Squiyles in every issue after. Both are recorded here rather than silently picking
one.

places/council-chambers-(turgeth).title: Council Chambers (Turgeth)
places/council-chambers-(turgeth).content:
Regal domed hall in Turgeth where the Council’s seven members work; records kept by Loren Fenn.
Adjoins The Holding Cells (Turgeth).
History

The party teleports in and is logged by Loren Fenn before being cleared to interrogate the prisoner
2025-03-31 @ 00:11:35-00:14:20.

places/dockside-warehouse-(turgeth).title: Dockside Warehouse (Turgeth)
places/dockside-warehouse-(turgeth).content:
Also heard as: the west side warehouse
The Boot’s dockside shipping and drug operation on Turgeth’s west side.
History

The party teleports in to raid it 2025-03-31 @ 00:42:21.
Site of the full firefight against Dex and the warehouse guards, including Fugly (nicknamed
“the captain” mid-fight — see The Guard Captain) 2025-03-31
@ 01:05:14-02:48:42.
Burned down by Ozone as the party retreats 2025-03-31 @ 03:13:57-03:14:24.

places/drang-city.title: Drang City
places/drang-city.content:
A city in Ingenia, Kingdom of Hawkthorne, whose Town Square hosts two shops advertised repeatedly in
the Gazette’s later, post-war issues.
History

Blanchet’s Botany (carnivorous plants, bonsai treefolk pets, plant-derived toxins) and Dusk & Willow
(a magical superstore: wands, rods, tomes, onsite spell creation, magical tattoos) both operate out
of Town Square, Drang City 2022-12-18, 2022-12-26.

places/eastern-territories.title: Eastern Territories
places/eastern-territories.content:
A sovereign region declared by former Squiylian citizens alongside the Western Territories in the
immediate aftermath of Squiyles’ collapse.
History

Declares itself sovereign, post-war, alongside the Western Territories; shown on the Gazette’s
continental map alongside the Orc Lands, Troll Mountains, the Changelings’ territory, the Howling
Gulf, and Binneth 2019-10-07.

places/ezaso-city.title: Ezaso City
places/ezaso-city.content:
Also heard as: Ezaso
Capital city of Cacoal, within the Kingdom of Squiyles. Site of a doppelganger infiltration
panic, a dangerous orc-masked killer, and multiple Merchants Square shops advertised in the Gazette.
History

Hosts the “Astronomy Summit” where attendees puzzle over stars vanishing from the sky
2019-04-01.
Captain Tartan of the Ezaso City Guard first warns of doppelganger infiltration (“Trust No-one”),
then a week later publicly walks the claim back as an “over exaggerated” rumor caused by “some kind
of flu,” backed by the king, who threatens to jail anyone who says “doppelganger” again
2019-04-01, 2019-04-09.
Street children are killed in a market by a six-foot, blue-skinned orcish man in a carved wooden
mask who reportedly vomits swarms of spiders and howls until victims’ ears bleed — speculated
(unconfirmed) to be a member of Gorthak’s army 2019-04-22.
Merchants Square hosts recurring advertisers: Exotic Animal Companion Sales, Ziff and Zoffs (magical
pranks), The Arcane Archer (spell-infused arrows), and the Moonwind Concert Hall, which hosts Bardic
Illusionist Feyman Allbright 2019-04-09, 2019-04-15. Thogs Exotic Meats also
trades in Ezaso, paying top dollar for dragon meat 2019-04-15.

Unresolved
Whether Cacoal (and therefore Ezaso) was within the Kingdom of Squiyles or the Kingdom of Binneth is
itself disputed across issues — see Conopimalis (Erepec)‘s Unresolved section.

places/godoy.title: Godoy
places/godoy.content:
A multicultural, changeling-populated city near the Troll Mountains, destroyed in episode 4 when the
Dyson Dynamo mirrored the party’s own fire spell across the whole city — roughly 90% mortality. An
inner Capitol district survived under a magical “blue dome.”
History

Site of the doppelganger caravan ambush that triggers the Dynamo’s citywide firestorm
2023-10-15 @ 00:56:37–01:42:41.
Confirmed roughly 90% mortality; only the party and the capital’s defenders under the blue dome survive
@ 01:42:41–01:42:50, @ 02:06:44–02:06:49.
The party watches it burn from the walls the morning after, then flees with the refugee column toward
Lutathal 2023-10-24 @ 00:12:40–00:29:12.
Rugby’s Roaming Gazette, dated DEC 19 4885 (before the destruction, which it never anticipates),
gives it a fuller geography — “Godoy City, Acatlalco, Western Territories” — and reports a critical
guard shortage caused by an overly strict vetting process, with Captain Cadillac Huggins (see
Cadillac) and Captain Darian Steele named as the city’s dedicated protectors. Local businesses
“Sycophancy Scrolls” and “Ram & The Fence,” both in the Town Square, advertise in the same issue
2023-09-24.

Unresolved
May be the same city as Lidurithal (episodes 1–2) — both sit near the Troll Mountains and both center
on the same bank — but no session states this explicitly.
The Gazette’s “Acatlalco” region name for Godoy echoes the “Acatlalco mountain ranges in Squiyles”
named in the 2019-06-10 issue, centuries (at least) earlier in-world and on a vastly different scale (a
mountain range vs. a city’s administrative region). Recorded as a naming echo only — not asserted to be
the same place. See Acatlalco.

places/hawthorne-college.title: Hawthorne College
places/hawthorne-college.content:
Also heard as: Hawkthorne, Hawthorne College of Enchantment
One of two top-ranked arcane schools in the world (tied with Beneth), specializing in enchantment magic,
located in the port town of Crist/Stornes. Appears only in the Pat-DM’d interlude session; see
2023-10-08 and jakedm Unresolved.
History

Alma mater and current workplace of Jace Gandolfini and Sarkhan Vol; tied with Beneth as the
top-ranked arcane college, specializing in enchantment, located in the port town of Crist/Stornes
2023-10-08 @ 00:35:02–00:35:46, @ 00:44:02.
Hosts a faculty meeting covering budget, the Elven Academy exchange, and a Changeling War update
@ 01:12:45.
Its concealed crafting workshop, password-locked in Celestial, is where Jace and Sarkhan prepare
bottles of air for the Isle of Death expedition @ 02:35:45–03:10:40.

places/holsoy.title: Holsoy
places/holsoy.content:
A town whose Church of St. Cuthbert burns down in what the Gazette frames as part of a pattern of
dragon attacks targeting that church’s holdings.
History

The Church of St. Cuthbert in Holsoy burns to the ground; exotic-monster expert Corbin Strange
speculates dragons may be exacting multi-generational revenge for forgotten grievances against the
church, noting it’s unusual for normally-solitary dragons to coordinate like this
2019-06-10.

places/howling-gulf.title: Howling Gulf
places/howling-gulf.content:
Also heard as: the gulf
The gulf between Binneth and Squiyles where the naval war between the two kingdoms is fought, and
later the site of a strange magical tunnel left behind by the war.
History

Site of the naval standoff between Binneth and Squiyles, as both kingdoms mass warships; a single
shot could trigger all-out war 2019-06-10.
Binneth’s fire-breathing secret-weapon ships destroy nearly half of Squiyles’ navy in a night battle
here 2019-06-17.
Two “Magical Death Tornadoes” — confirmed magical waterspouts of unknown origin, growing to roughly
300 feet tall — are spotted spiraling in the center of the gulf 2019-07-15.
Binneth lifts its trade blockade into the gulf after the war, striking new trade deals with former
Squiylian partners 2019-10-07.
A strange, calm, non-spinning hole/tunnel — a circular waterfall pouring endlessly into an abyss,
radiating a magical aura — appears where a whirlpool once was; a fisherman and his companion Paulie
report hearing what might be a deep growl from within 2019-10-07.

places/howling-hooters.title: Howling Hooters
places/howling-hooters.content:
A bar/inn in Lidurithal, the party’s base for the bank job and Mary’s residence.
History

The party’s contact point; Mary’s room is upstairs
2023-09-12 @ 02:18:49–02:46:26.
Four city guards raid the bar searching for Mary and are talked out of finding anyone @ 03:27:48–03:45:01.

places/isle-of-death.title: Isle of Death
places/isle-of-death.content:
Also heard as: Deeth, Death Isles
A region permanently shrouded in a deadly, constitution-draining Miasmic Cloud, once home to prestigious
necromantic schools, now abandoned. The Tomb of Horrors lies at its center. Appears only in the Pat-DM’d
interlude session; see 2023-10-08 and
jakedm Unresolved.
History

Described as once home to prestigious necromantic schools, abandoned after the miasma spread
2023-10-08 @ 00:31:05.
Confirmed via the dispelled Tomb of Horrors map to hold the Tomb at its center
2023-10-08 @ 02:01:41–02:09:52.
Prompts Jace Gandolfini and Sarkhan Vol to craft/buy bottles of air and a scroll of Concealed
Breath to survive its miasma @ 02:35:45–03:10:40.
Rugby’s Roaming Gazette describes an “Isle of Death” (a locals’ nickname) east of Sawyen, before the
“Monstrous nation of Suenth” — home to a skeletal, skinless flying horror and to monsters and
dinosaurs, witnessed by fisherman Than’ Targuhn 2019-07-15. The very next issue describes
a miasmic “death cloud” spreading from the shores of Sawyen and Suenth 2020-04-13.

Unresolved
No later session revisits the Isle of Death or the Tomb of Horrors expedition.
The Gazette’s “Isle of Death” (2019-07-15, in-world MAY 8 4885) shares this page’s name, its
monster-haunted reputation, and a miasma-adjacent region (the “death cloud” of the very next issue) —
but the two are never confirmed on-mic or in print to be the same island, and a huge span of in-world
time separates the Gazette’s 4885 setting from the JakeDM campaign. Flagged as a possible echo, not
asserted as the same place.

places/isle-of-torta.title: Isle of Torta
places/isle-of-torta.content:
Also heard as: Torta, Island of Torta
A remote island, long an area of contention between local officials and criminal organizations, where
a captive dragon escapes and from which an entire chain of dragon attacks appears to originate.
History

A blue dragon attacks the island, vaporizing onlookers; the attack is described as moving inland
from Torta toward populated cities 2019-04-01.
A dragon that had earlier escaped from Torta blasts a hole in King Stroth’s castle in Squiyles with a
lightning bolt, freeing a second captive dragon and devastating the castle
2019-04-09.
Thieves who stole a Church of St. Cuthbert vessel from Thorhofn City are tracked to Torta — “the
same island where the dragon attacks seem to have started” — where their burned ship is found
scuttled near shore 2019-06-10.

places/kafka.title: Kafka
places/kafka.content:
An agricultural hub in the Kingdom of Squiyles and one of the kingdom’s largest potato exporters,
overrun and enslaved by Gorthak’s orcish army.
History

Falls to Gorthak’s army; war-time strategist Martin Graybeard notes Kafka had no royal protection
presence, recommending nearby families evacuate or prepare for attack
2019-04-15.
Its potato trade resumes under new agreements after Binneth lifts its post-war trade blockade into
the Howling Gulf 2019-10-07.

places/kingdom-of-binneth.title: Kingdom of Binneth
places/kingdom-of-binneth.content:
A kingdom ruled by King Tygard, locked in a long land dispute and eventually open war with the
Kingdom of Squiyles. Emerges from the war as one of the world’s rising great powers, having lost
very little military strength while Squiyles collapsed entirely.
History

King Tygard meets King Stroth of Squiyles for the kingdoms’ annual alliance/trade negotiations;
Stroth loses his temper and dangles Tygard out a third-story window, and both parties leave hurling
threats of war 2019-04-15.
Binneth’s Royal-Elites capture an orc scout on Binneth soil — the first sign of the orcish invasion
(previously confined to Squiyles) reaching Binneth land — and recover a magical sending stone from
him; they return him to Beisfjord to present to Captain Vakrum 2019-04-29.
Gorthak’s forces wipe out an entire Binneth scouting party, sparing and mutilating one scout to
carry a demand back to Beisfjord for the return of the orc prisoner Zakmed; the Binneth king issues no
public statement 2019-06-10.
Zakmed — confirmed via confiscated sending stones to be Gorthak’s son — escapes Binneth custody; the
crown offers a reward for his re-capture 2019-06-17.
Reportedly hires seafaring mercenaries and fields a “secret weapon” fleet of fire-breathing ships,
which destroys nearly half of Squiyles’ navy in a night battle in the Howling Gulf
2019-06-10, 2019-06-17.
Post-war, claims new territory north of its border without further conflict, lifts its trade
blockade into the Howling Gulf, and strikes new trade deals (including the potato markets) with
former Squiylian trading partners; the Gazette’s economists call Binneth a rising world power
2019-10-07.
Part of eastern Binneth is later swallowed by the spreading miasmic death cloud emanating from
Sawyen and Suenth 2020-04-13.
Royal Astronomer Hammond Hardle observes the last visible star go dark from Binneth’s royal
observatory moments before evacuating through a Feywild gate — part of the “Day Zero” anomaly (see
timeline) 2019-05-12.

Unresolved
The 2019-05-12 issue, dated APRIL 17 4900 rather than 4885, describes the Material Plane itself
apparently ceasing to exist and Binneth’s royal observatory evacuating to the Feywild. The very next
issue in sequence reverts to 4885 and continues the ongoing war as if nothing happened — the paper never
references the 4900 events again. Treated as a flagged paradox/alternate-future branch, not a confirmed
part of Binneth’s history. See timeline.

places/kingdom-of-hawkthorne.title: Kingdom of Hawkthorne
places/kingdom-of-hawkthorne.content:
A kingdom to the north of Squiyles, later described by the Gazette as a
“powerful goblin kingdom.” Home to Novaexum City, Bringska, Veset, and Drang City.
History

Hosts the Hawkthorne Royal Gala, attended by field correspondent Rex Sauvage, where his carriage
driver attacks him with an enchanted, mind-dominating glass eye 2019-04-22.
Grandmaster Wizard Kirby’s catastrophic public immortality-spell demonstration takes place at the
Novaexum Lecture Hall in Novaexum City, Sacium, Hawkthorne 2019-04-01,
2019-06-24.
A strange rainbow-colored rift opens in the town square of Bringska, granting (and cursing)
random powers to townsfolk who jump through it, before being sealed in stone by authorities
2019-06-24.
Eastern Hawkthorne is swallowed by the spreading miasmic death cloud originating from Sawyen and
Suenth 2020-04-13.
Described by the Gazette as a “powerful goblin kingdom” expected to send representatives to the
post-war changeling peace summit 2022-12-18.
Home to Drang City (Ingenia) and Veset (Lausia), both named in Gazette advertisements
2019-07-15, 2022-12-18, 2022-12-26.

places/kingdom-of-squiyles.title: Kingdom of Squiyles
places/kingdom-of-squiyles.content:
Also heard as: Squiles
A kingdom ruled by King Stroth, publisher-city Conopimalis’s home nation and
Rugby’s Roaming Gazette’s original base. Fights a long war on two fronts — orcs from the east under
Gorthak, trolls pouring out of the Acatlalco mountains — loses that war, and is ultimately
overrun and ruled by changelings. “Squiles” is included here defensively as a
plausible Whisper-mangled spelling, though it has not been confirmed to appear in any transcript.
History

Long-running land dispute with the Nayesche Orc tribe escalates into open war: the Nayesche sack
Bostur City on “Bloody Tuesday,” beheading Duke Harrington 2019-04-09. See Bostur.
A dragon escapes containment at the Isle of Torta and blasts a hole in King Stroth’s
castle, freeing a second captive dragon; over half the castle is destroyed and 80% of the royal army
is lost in the ensuing chaos 2019-04-09.
King Stroth declares the kingdom’s first military draft in 90 years, the first since the War of the
Falling Moon under his grandfather; draft-dodging is rumored to carry severe punishment
2019-04-22.
Kafka, a major agricultural/potato-exporting hub, falls to Gorthak’s orcish army
2019-04-15.
Trolls begin pouring out of the Acatlalco mountain ranges in large, slow-moving droves, reported
independently by trappers in Totezatlan and Somic; King Stroth makes no public statement
2019-06-10.
Open naval war breaks out with Binneth in the Howling Gulf; Squiyles fields a
Wizard Special Forces air-naval unit under Captain Hoolihan, but Binneth’s “fire-breathing ship”
secret weapon destroys nearly half the Squiylian fleet 2019-06-10, 2019-06-17,
2019-06-24.
Mass civil unrest: citizens riot for peace with Gorthak, refugees fleeing north into Hawkthorne are
turned away at the border, and a separatist uprising (pushing for a union of self-governing countries
free of King Stroth) sees its leaders arrested for treason 2019-06-17.
Trolls and orcs appear to be acting in loose coordination to divide contested land, ravaging farms in
central Squiyles while orcs hold the east; food supply collapses kingdom-wide as most able-bodied men
are drafted 2019-06-17, 2019-06-24.
The entire country of Cacoal, part of Squiyles’ holdings, is overrun by doppelgangers and
self-declares the “Changeling Nation”; King Stroth makes no statement 2019-07-15.
The kingdom falls entirely: by JUNE 1 4885, Squiyles has collapsed, its territory is being redivided by
the Eastern and Western Territories’ squabbling noble militias, changelings have taken over the
majority of its former land, and Rugby’s Gazette is forced to relocate its headquarters to
Stogath 2019-10-07.
Post-collapse, the changeling government hosts an international peace summit in the former Squiylian
capital, which ends in chaos when changeling delegates are revealed to have infiltrated the
conference disguised as other nations’ diplomats 2022-12-18, 2022-12-26. See
The Changeling Nation.

Unresolved
Whisper transcription elsewhere in this wiki has not been confirmed to use the spelling “Squiles” for
this kingdom; the alias is recorded defensively per the Gazette merge’s own instructions, not because it
has been observed in a transcript.

places/kingdom-of-turgyth.title: Kingdom of Turgyth
places/kingdom-of-turgyth.content:
Also heard as: Turgythe
A kingdom whose capital region includes Kuria (home to Pores) and which, under the Science and Alchemy
research act of 4870, funds the world’s first space program.
History

Rex Sauvage, fighting off a band of harpies while flying on his griffin Sterling, is en route “toward
the kingdom of Turgyth” at the request of his friend King Fashim Thoronor 2019-04-09.
Balthezar’s Bazaar, a traveling carnival of curiosities, sets up in Pores, Kuria, Kingdom of Turgyth,
every weekend in June 2019-10-07.
Announces the world’s first space program — exploring “the space between the world… and the
heavens occupied by the gods themselves” — funded by the royal treasury and led by Dr. Joanne
Hingbrant 2019-06-24.
Representatives of “Turgythe” are requested to attend the post-war changeling peace summit in former
Squiyles 2022-12-18.

Unresolved
See Turgeth (the DungeonVice-campaign city, 2025, home to the College of Turgeth) for a
name-root echo flagged on that page — a city vs. a kingdom, and centuries apart in-world, so not
asserted to be the same place.

places/laudir.title: Laudir
places/laudir.content:
A peninsula city in the Kingdom of Squiyles, starting point for the kingdom’s annual airship race.
History

Hosts the annual airship race: racers depart Laudir heading west off the peninsula, over the skies
of Victrum and the surrounding islands, finishing at Tredexum. Local air captain Reginald Woolrick
is among the competitors; foul play was suspected but unproven in the previous year’s race
2019-04-15.

places/lidurithal.title: Lidurithal
places/lidurithal.content:
Also heard as: Lidurithol
A sprawling city near the Troll Mountains with a dwarvenish, vaguely feudal-Japanese architectural
feel (sliding doors, high porches). Site of the bank job in episodes 1–2.
History

The party arrives via Mitch Copperhead’s drop-off; established as near the Troll Mountains with
dwarven/feudal-Japanese architecture 2023-09-12
@ 02:33:04, @ 02:33:25.
Home to the Howling Hooters and the unnamed bank targeted by the heist @ 02:18:49, @ 03:01:14.

Unresolved
May be the same city as Godoy (episode 4) — both sit near the Troll Mountains and both center on the
same bank — but no session states this explicitly; the name simply changes between episodes 1–2 and
episode 4.

places/lutathal.title: Lutathal
places/lutathal.content:
Also heard as: Luterol, Laduriel, Liduriel, Kalooza
A city built into a mountain face in a half-oval shape with a waterfall through the wall, multicultural
and class-divided, home to the annual Magic Carpet Race (called the Rug Mandela in episode 6). Reached by
the party roughly twelve hours’ flight (or 2.5 days’ march) from Godoy.
History

Chosen as the party’s refugee destination over Ukendafar and Olingad; reached ahead of the refugee
column via flight; built in a half-oval against a mountain wall with a waterfall down it
2023-10-24 @ 00:26:13–01:17:11, @ 01:21:36.
Gate guards share a sigil with Cadillac’s mage group, tying his faction to the city @ 01:25:59.
The party registers for the Magic Carpet Race (ticket #7, 50,000 gp prize) and falls out with carpet
sponsor Greg @ 02:28:58–02:53:46.
As “Liduriel”/“Kalooza”: the rug-shop/Greg conflict continues directly from the prior session; the
party learns the race (now called the Rug Mandela, 20,000 gold winner-take-all) starts the next morning
2023-11-28 @ 00:12:38, @ 02:06:28,
@ 01:33:40.

Unresolved
The city’s name changes between “Lutathal” (episode 5) and “Liduriel”/“Kalooza” (episode 6), and the
race’s name and prize amount also change (Magic Carpet Race/50,000 gp vs. Rug Mandela/20,000 gp); no
session explicitly confirms these are the same event, though the carried-over Greg/rug-shop conflict
strongly implies the same city.
A third variant appears in Rugby’s Roaming Gazette: the “Rugmandella” race, grand prize a magic carpet
also called the “Rugmandella” (made by Carpet Baggers Industries), starting in Lauvog, Western
Territories, rather than Lutathal/Liduriel/Kalooza 2023-09-24. One more data point in the
naming inconsistency, not a resolution.

places/mccathlyre.title: McCathlyre
places/mccathlyre.content:
A kingdom or region whose southern waters became The Free Islands after pirate Captain Jamal
claimed the sparsely-inhabited chain south of it.
History

The Free Islands/Free Isles are described as “the sparsely inhabited island chain south of
McCathlyre” 2019-04-29.
Representatives of McCathlyre are requested to attend the post-war changeling peace summit in
former Squiyles 2022-12-18.

places/meschen.title: Meschen
places/meschen.content:
A small, isolated mountain village near Suenth and Sawyen, destroyed by the miasmic death
cloud after its people refused to believe the threat existed or evacuate.
History

Discovered by an evacuation party during the Suenth/Sawyen island evacuations; its culture is deeply
tied to the mountain and the villagers had only ever met one other group of outsiders before. Unable
to explain the miasma threat in terms they understood, the rescue party leaves them behind — gifted
with food and goods from the village — rather than forcibly abduct them
2020-04-13.

places/neo.title: Neo
places/neo.content:
Also heard as: NIO
A small, populous river town on Nutty’s home continent, in a country given variously as “Gaethier,”
“Manhee,” “Mannhai,” or “Man High” across sessions — likely all the same mishearing. Heavily
Asian-inspired, with many catfolk residents. Home to Star Iron Works, a custom dwarven blacksmith, a
bait-and-tackle shop, a general store, and a Church of St. Cuthbert branch.
History

Donnie and Jake fly here on a magic broom and find an enchantress willing to bind an air elemental to
the ship 2020-01-20 @ 02:04:40–02:19:25.
The party returns to shop and is nearly exposed as harboring Mori Yoshinari, wanted by the Church of
St. Cuthbert 2020-01-28 @ 00:52:22–01:15:30.

Unresolved
The spelling of the surrounding country’s name is never pinned down in the transcripts.

places/novaexum-city.title: Novaexum City
places/novaexum-city.content:
Also heard as: Novaexum
A city in Sacium, Kingdom of Hawkthorne, home to the Novaexum Lecture Hall.
History

Grand/Grandmaster Wizard Kirby announces an “Immortality Lecture” at the Novaexum Lecture Hall for
May 1st 2019-04-01.
Days later, Kirby’s public demonstration of a theoretical immortality spell-stacking technique
catastrophically fails at the same lecture hall: his focusing mirrors and astral lenses shatter,
duplicate versions of himself tear through the crowd, and he is never seen again
2019-06-24.

places/orc-lands.title: Orc Lands
places/orc-lands.content:
The territory claimed and unified by Gorthak after he united all the orc clans into a single
horde, formerly disputed border land claimed from the Kingdom of Squiyles.
History

Proclaimed on the Sunday Gorthak is named ruler of all orc clans, with tribal celebrations heard
from all who venture near 2019-04-29.
Shown on the Gazette’s post-war continental map as its own territory, alongside the Western and
Eastern Territories, the Troll Mountains, the Changelings’ territory, the Howling Gulf, and Binneth
2019-10-07.
Partly swallowed by the spreading miasmic death cloud originating from Sawyen and Suenth
2020-04-13.
Rex Sauvage is reported “tragically killed while on a field report in the orc lands,” per his
successor Timothy Mantooth 2022-12-18. See Rex Sauvage.

places/paengju.title: Paengju
places/paengju.content:
A massive rainforest island containing many undiscovered species of plants, insects, fungi, animals,
and magical beasts — including, per a single secondhand account, a psychic parasitic plant.
History

In-house botanist Gerome Kudzu Wünderberry is interviewed about reports of a psychic, parasitic plant
that enslaves hosts to help it propagate; a single escapee claims to have tended it for 12 years
before a lightning strike freed him. Research expeditions are being planned
2019-06-17.

Unresolved
The psychic-plant story rests on one secondhand, unverified account; the Gazette itself frames it as
rumor pending expedition confirmation.

places/sawyen.title: Sawyen
places/sawyen.content:
A country or region bordering the monstrous nation of Suenth and the monster-haunted
Isle of Death, and later ground zero (with Suenth) for the spreading miasmic death cloud.
History

The Isle of Death lies just east of Sawyen, before reaching Suenth; a popular fishing spot for rare
large monstrous fish despite the dinosaurs and monsters known to roam the isle
2019-07-15.
The miasmic “death cloud” — a green cloud of deathly energy — begins emanating from the shores of
Sawyen and Suenth, eventually swallowing parts of Binneth, the Orc Lands, and Hawkthorne
2020-04-13.

places/somic-city.title: Somic City
places/somic-city.content:
Also heard as: Somic
A city in the Kingdom of Squiyles, home to the Elf Quarter and a shop district advertised repeatedly
in the Gazette.
History

Home to Grimwald’s magic tattoo parlor and “Attaché,” a clothing shop in the Elf Quarter selling a
“Pea-coat of many things” 2019-04-01.
Officer Ganstad of the Somic City Guard takes tips on wanted criminal George Cephalus
2019-04-09.
Trappers and hunters in Somic independently report trolls pouring out of the Acatlalco mountains
2019-06-10.

places/stogath.title: Stogath
places/stogath.content:
Also heard as: Stogath Isle, Isle of Stogath, City of Stogath
An island in the Western Territories, formerly under Squiylian rule, that becomes Rugby’s Roaming
Gazette’s new headquarters after the fall of Squiyles and the destruction of
its old offices in Conopimalis. Remains the Gazette’s base of operations
through every surviving post-war issue.
History

The Gazette relocates its headquarters here after its half-destroyed Conopimalis office becomes
untenable amid Squiyles’ collapse; the new mailing address given is “Rugby’s Roaming Gazette, City
of Stogath, Isle of Stogath, Western Territories” 2019-10-07.
Remains the publication’s listed base through the JULY 4 4885 (2020-04-13), JUNE 7 4885
(2022-12-18/2022-12-26), and DEC 19 4885 (2023-09-24) issues 2020-04-13,
2022-12-18, 2022-12-26, 2023-09-24.

places/suenth.title: Suenth
places/suenth.content:
A “monstrous nation” bordering Sawyen and the Isle of Death, later the other source point (with
Sawyen) of the spreading miasmic death cloud.
History

Described as the “Monstrous nation of Suenth,” reached just past the Isle of Death east of Sawyen
2019-07-15.
The miasmic death cloud begins emanating from the shores of Suenth and Sawyen together
2020-04-13.
Small islands surrounding Suenth and Sawyen are evacuated ahead of the cloud; the isolated mountain
village of Meschen refuses to evacuate and is left to its fate 2020-04-13.

places/the-free-islands.title: The Free Islands
places/the-free-islands.content:
Also heard as: The Free Isles
A sparsely inhabited island chain south of McCathlyre, claimed by pirate Captain Jamal and declared
an open pirate haven.
History

Captain Jamal claims the chain, dubbing it “The Free Islands”/“The Free Isles,” and invites pirates
to settle and defend it; previously undeveloped and lightly taxed kingdom territory, home to a few
native tribes 2019-04-29.
Career-deckhand Merl Sedgwick plans to join Jamal there 2019-04-29.
Captain Jamal advertises recruitment directly in the Gazette: “JOIN THE RANKS — THE FREE ISLES”
2019-04-29.

places/the-holding-cells-(turgeth).title: The Holding Cells (Turgeth)
places/the-holding-cells-(turgeth).content:
Prison in Turgeth holding the city’s worst criminals, including Riggs’s Widow.
History

Ozone flirts information out of Riggs’s Widow here 2025-03-31 @ 00:14:45.

places/the-inspectors'-office.title: The Inspectors' Office
places/the-inspectors'-office.content:
Also heard as: the office, HQ
The inspectors’ headquarters in Turgeth, where Jerry operates the teleporter.
History

The party regroups here after the prisoner’s capture, choosing between the boot and the aqueducts job
2025-03-31 @ 00:00:00.

places/the-nexus.title: The Nexus
places/the-nexus.content:
A planar prison for powerful evil beings, conceptually similar to Carceri but run by a separate authority.
Cannot be left by plane shift — the only way out is forward, through a chain of gem-keyed portals. The
party is trapped here at the end of the recorded sessions.
History

The party steps through a one-way portal from the cult complex and arrives on a frozen, blizzard-swept
mountaintop within the Nexus 2021-10-19 @ 03:08:00.
Identified via a knowledge check, boosted by ambient knowledge the party seems to absorb just from being
there 2021-11-02 @ 00:18:18–00:19:54.
Confirmed the party cannot plane shift or backtrack out; they must advance through a chain of
gem-keyed portals, tracked by the Locate Portal Sextant
2021-11-02 @ 02:03:53–02:30:02.
An angelic-inscribed circle near the arrival portal names several other regions of (or connected to) the
Nexus: floating islands, a sunken location, a mountain range, “the scorch,” an ocean of storms, “the
twisting,” a jungle of secrets, “the empty quarter,” and ivory walls
2021-11-02 @ 02:33:53.

Unresolved
The campaign’s recorded sessions end with the party still trapped in the Nexus, resting before pushing
toward a suspected fiery plane next.

places/the-ship.title: The Ship
places/the-ship.content:
Also heard as: the planeshifting ship, the elemental airship
The party’s vessel through most of Arc I: originally The Mage’s trapped, blood-draining planeshifting
ship, stolen by the party, later enchanted to fly via a permanently bound air elemental, Pop Jack.
History

Originally the mage’s trapped vessel, drains blood to power its plane-shift crystal and fuel his
immortality 2020-01-20 @ 00:17:25.
The party refuels its empty blood reservoir with a captured intruder, killing him in the process
2020-01-20 @ 01:33:24–01:43:35.
Permanently enchanted to fly via a bound air elemental (Pop Jack) for 100,000 gold
2020-01-20 @ 02:18:13–02:44:38.
Its planar crystal activates on its own overnight, dragging the ship into the first layer of the Abyss
2020-01-28 @ 03:40:30–03:45:48.
Refueled with drow blood after an ambush in Hell
2020-03-25 @ 00:55:49.
Jumped out of Hell via the sextant’s reset settings, landing the party in the Feywild instead of home
2020-03-25 @ 02:31:40–02:36:13.
By this point kept permanently parked thirty feet up “to dodge time wizards”
2020-04-13 @ 01:01:11.

places/thorhofn-city.title: Thorhofn City
places/thorhofn-city.content:
Also heard as: Thorhofn
A city in the Kingdom of Binneth, site of a 700-year-old pilgrimage cathedral, a wave of mysterious
abductions, and the theft of a Church of St. Cuthbert vessel.
History

Tadmenroe Cathedral, a 700-year-old pilgrimage site, is burned down by three dragons (red, blue, and
green) in the early morning; no one is hurt because the building was under renovation. Head cleric
Morin Claust mourns the loss 2019-04-22.
The Wares District is home to “Shoot and Lute” (family-run since 4867) and “Daniels
Extra-Dimensional Delights” 2019-04-22.
A wave of abductions is reported daily in the city, carried out by cloth-masked figures near the city
gates; Captain of the Watch Shamus Greerson comments, and a witness who spoke to the Gazette herself
later goes missing 2019-04-29.
The Redlight District hosts “Buscy Bards,” advertising the elf entertainer Aaliyah
2019-04-29.
A Church of St. Cuthbert vessel is stolen from the docks while paladin Worick Dragon-bane naps aboard
it and is blinded by the thieves; the ship is chased to the Isle of Torta and found scuttled and
burned, with a surviving watchman identifying one thief as a samurai 2019-06-10.
The scout mutilated by Gorthak’s forces, carrying the demand for Zakmed’s return, dies here after
collapsing from an untreated infection 2019-06-10.

places/troll-mountains.title: Troll Mountains
places/troll-mountains.content:
A mountain range from which trolls, previously confined to the Acatlalco mountain tunnels, spread out
across the continent in the aftermath of the Binneth–Squiyles war.
History

Shown on the Gazette’s post-war continental map as a named region separate from, but adjacent to,
the Acatlalco range where the troll migration began 2019-10-07.
Trolls, previously confined to mountain tunnels, spread throughout the range, bringing increased
sightings of other dangerous beasts 2019-10-07, 2022-12-18,
2022-12-26.
By late 4885, alchemists announce a troll-DNA-altering compound (transmitted via troll copulation)
meant to end the trolls’ regenerative advantage and “civilize” the mountains
2023-09-24.

Unresolved
Named Troll Mountains near Godoy in the Godoy page’s geography (JakeDM campaign, 2023) may echo
this same mountain range by name only; see Godoy’s Unresolved section — not asserted to be the
same range given the vast gap in in-world time between the Gazette’s 4885 setting and JakeDM’s.

places/turgeth.title: Turgeth
places/turgeth.content:
The city the DungeonVice party works as inspectors for, governed by a Council of seven members who keep
meticulous, timestamped records of all visitors. Home to The Inspectors’ Office, the
Council Chambers (Turgeth), and a branch of the College of Turgeth. Its drug trade was run by
Riggs and is now run by The Boot.
History

Established as governed by a Council of seven, with records kept by Loren Fenn
2025-03-31 @ 00:11:58.
The city’s teleporter network can’t reach every location — only direct hubs like headquarters and the
Council/church are reachable, and everyone can tell where a teleport originated
2025-03-31 @ 00:11:02.
Has its own sports culture: “mages and bases,” dragons and footy, handball, and ping pong (the
most-watched and bet-on sport, played by ungifted “normies”)
2025-03-31 @ 00:34:05-00:34:57.

Unresolved
Rugby’s Roaming Gazette, centuries (at least) earlier in-world, describes a whole “Kingdom of Turgyth”
(also spelled “Turgythe”) — home to Pores/Kuria and the site of a space-program announcement — see
Kingdom of Turgyth. The name-root echo (Turgeth/Turgyth) is noted here without asserting any
connection: different campaigns, a vast time gap, and a city-vs-kingdom scale mismatch all argue
against treating them as the same place.

places/village-of-barovia.title: Village of Barovia
places/village-of-barovia.content:
A fog-bound, vampire-terrorized town at the foot of Castle Ravenloft: shuttered shops, claw-scarred
walls, a church, Bildrith’s Mercantile, and the Blood of the Vine tavern. Reached through magical mists
that trap anyone without a gypsy guide and their special candles/lanterns.
History

The party arrives after forcing a goblin guide through the mists, finding a dead villager with a forged
letter on the way 2022-12-06 @ 02:09:38, @ 01:58:10.
The village’s sole remaining priest maintains the church’s holy wards through constant prayer and gives
the party a map to Castle Ravenloft 2022-12-06 @ 02:18:39.
The party meets Ismark Indirovich and Irina Indirovich at the Indirovich estate, and is ordered
off the property 2022-12-06 @ 02:32:48–03:07:21.
The party shelters overnight in the village church, watching harmless ghosts march toward the castle at
midnight 2022-12-06 @ 03:24:44.
At a nearby gypsy encampment, Madame Eva gives the party a tarot reading
2022-12-06 @ 03:44:15–03:52:28.

Unresolved
The party never returns to the village after departing for Castle Ravenloft; its fate, and that of
Ismark and Irina, is never followed up on.

places/western-territories.title: Western Territories
places/western-territories.content:
A sovereign region declared by former Squiylian citizens after the fall of Kingdom of Squiyles,
with no central government — “a wild-west style of living,” per the Gazette. Becomes Rugby’s Roaming
Gazette’s new home via Stogath.
History

Declares itself sovereign in the war’s immediate aftermath, alongside the Eastern Territories;
various wealthy families’ militias impose conflicting local laws in the absence of a central
government 2019-10-07.
Home to Stogath, the Gazette’s relocated headquarters 2019-10-07.
Hosts “Lee’s Impending Doom Solutions,” a miasmic-cloud fallout shelter business, among its
advertisers (located in Yosari, Kaku, Kingdom of Gaithiyre — a neighboring kingdom, not the
Territories themselves) 2020-04-13.
By DEC 19 4885, the Death-Defying “Rugmandella” magic carpet race starts from Lauvog, in the Western
Territories 2023-09-24. See Win the Magic Carpet Race.
Godoy, “a city celebrated for its serenity” in the Acatlalco region of the Western Territories,
suffers a guard shortage from an overly strict vetting process 2023-09-24. See
Godoy.

quests/aqueducts-assignment.title: Aqueducts Assignment
quests/aqueducts-assignment.content:
A Council job offered by Volto, concerning funding from “Captain Lieutenant Squats.” Passed over by
the party in favor of the Hunt for the Boot.
History

Offered at the top of the session; the party chose to chase the boot instead
2025-03-31 @ 00:07:25-00:07:44.

quests/college-of-turgeth-drug-pipeline.title: College of Turgeth Drug Pipeline
quests/college-of-turgeth-drug-pipeline.content:
Investigate the College of Turgeth’s secret role as the true supplier of the drug Maka, worth
~75,000 gp/week.
History

Revealed by Riggs’s Widow during her interrogation; not yet investigated directly by the party
2025-03-31 @ 00:24:08-00:24:19.

quests/cover-up-godoy's-destruction.title: Cover Up Godoy's Destruction
quests/cover-up-godoy's-destruction.content:
After accidentally leveling Godoy (roughly 90% mortality) with their own fire magic amplified by the
Dyson Dynamo, the party debates how to avoid being blamed.
History

Connor proposes blaming an unknown natural disaster/meteor; the party sets up a refugee triage camp
partly to avoid suspicion 2023-10-15 @ 01:39:56, @ 01:49:39.
The party confirms nobody outside their group seems to know who was responsible yet, though “technically
legendary” per an in-game check 2023-10-24 @ 00:18:17.

Unresolved
No session confirms whether the cover-up ultimately succeeds; the TIU’s suspicion of the party by
episode 6 is tied to the Dyson Dynamo, not explicitly to Godoy’s destruction.

quests/defeat-strahd.title: Defeat Strahd
quests/defeat-strahd.content:
Kill Strahd von Zarovich — tied explicitly to both saving Barovia and escaping the magical mists
trapping visitors in his domain.
History

Stated as the party’s goal early in the dungeon crawl: “we got to kill him twice” to both save the town
and escape 2022-12-18 @ 00:59:48–01:00:10.
The party fights Strahd directly in his audience chamber after being teleported in front of him; he
dominates much of the party before escaping as mist
2023-02-12 @ 00:58:14–02:23:45.

Status
Open — Strahd is never defeated, or even fought to a finish, in the recorded sessions. The campaign’s last
session ends with him still alive.

quests/escape-castle-ravenloft.title: Escape Castle Ravenloft
quests/escape-castle-ravenloft.content:
Find a way out of Castle Ravenloft after the party becomes trapped deep inside it following the dinner
invitation ambush.
History

Raised as a concern after Strahd’s dinner invitation turns into a castle-wide lockdown
2022-12-18.
Still unresolved as the party pushes deeper into the castle’s upper dungeon, chasing a pulsating red
light toward an unexplored tower 2023-03-18
@ 00:03:14–00:22:21.

Status
Open — this is the last recorded session of the campaign; the party never leaves the castle on-screen.

quests/escape-the-abyss-and-hell.title: Escape the Abyss and Hell
quests/escape-the-abyss-and-hell.content:
After the ship’s planar crystal drags the party into the Abyss, they spend several sessions trapped there
before finally escaping back out — though not quite to where they meant to go.
History

The ship is dragged into the first layer of the Abyss when its planar crystal activates unprompted
2020-01-28 @ 03:45:48.
The party survives the Apocalypse Box crisis and a demon-nutty attack while still trapped there
2020-03-24.
The party fights free of a side dungeon, refuels the ship with drow blood, and pilots an interplanar
jump out 2020-03-25 @ 02:31:40–02:36:13.
The jump lands the party in the Feywild/First World, not the Material Plane as intended
2020-03-25 @ 02:40:38.

Status
Completed — the party is out of Hell/the Abyss, though stranded in the Feywild instead of home.

quests/escape-the-mists.title: Escape the Mists
quests/escape-the-mists.content:
Escape the magical mists trapping visitors in Barovia — tied explicitly to killing
Strahd von Zarovich.
History

Only gypsies with special candles/lanterns are confirmed able to pass safely through the mists; it’s
unresolved whether Strahd himself can leave
2022-12-06 @ 01:10:22.
Framed by the party as requiring Strahd’s death (“you got to kill him twice”)
2022-12-18 @ 01:00:01–01:00:10.

Status
Open — never resolved; the party never leaves Barovia or Castle Ravenloft in the recorded sessions.

quests/escape-the-nexus.title: Escape the Nexus
quests/escape-the-nexus.content:
The party’s goal after learning they’re trapped in The Nexus, a planar prison they cannot leave by
plane shift — only by advancing forward through a chain of gem-keyed portals tracked by the
Locate Portal Sextant.
History

The party confirms they cannot plane shift or backtrack out of the Nexus
2021-11-02 @ 02:03:53.
A new red gem is recovered, suspected to key a fiery plane as the next destination
2021-11-02 @ 02:03:16–02:19:12.

Status
Open — this is the last recorded session; the party rests before pushing onward, with the outcome
unknown.

quests/find-the-sun-sword's-hilt.title: Find the Sun Sword's Hilt
quests/find-the-sun-sword's-hilt.content:
Recover the missing hilt of the Sun Sword, needed to restore the weapon’s full power against
Strahd von Zarovich.
History

A Spellcraft check identifies the sword Jake has been carrying as the Sun Sword’s blade, and confirms
its hilt was separated long ago and never recovered
2023-01-30 @ 04:10:16.
Still referenced as missing by the end of the recorded campaign
2023-03-18 @ 00:44:03.

Status
Open — the hilt is never found in any recorded session.

quests/find-the-tomb-of-horrors.title: Find the Tomb of Horrors
quests/find-the-tomb-of-horrors.content:
Jace Gandolfini and Sarkhan Vol set out to find the legendary Tomb of Horrors on the
Isle of Death, hoping to recover a demi-lich’s unrecovered hoard, including a Ring of Three Wishes.
Appears only in the Pat-DM’d interlude session; see jakedm Unresolved.
History

Jace discovers a field report and map pointing to the Tomb
2023-10-08 @ 00:56:17.
The map’s illusion is dispelled, confirming the Tomb lies at the center of the Isle of Death
@ 02:01:41–02:03:05.
The pair prepare bottles of air and a scroll of Concealed Breath and ready to depart; the session ends
before they leave Hawthorne @ 03:07:42.

Unresolved
No later session picks this quest back up.

quests/find-the-tool-of-evil.title: Find the Tool of Evil
quests/find-the-tool-of-evil.content:
Madame Eva’s tarot prophecy of “a tool of evil” protected by darkness, needed against
Strahd von Zarovich.
History

Prophesied during the party’s tarot reading at the gypsy encampment
2022-12-06 @ 03:49:01.
A shapeshifting magic sword is claimed from a basement fire trap and later identified as the
Sun Sword’s blade — a plausible but never-confirmed match for the prophecy
2022-12-26 @ 03:58:28,
2023-01-30 @ 04:10:16.

Status
Open/unconfirmed — the party never explicitly ties the Sun Sword to Madame Eva’s prophecy on-screen.

quests/hunt-for-the-boot.title: Hunt for the Boot
quests/hunt-for-the-boot.content:
Track down and deal with The Boot, the troll crime lord who took over Turgeth’s drug trade after
Riggs.
History

Chosen by the party over the Aqueducts Assignment as their priority
2025-03-31 @ 00:07:25-00:11:58.
The party raids a dockside warehouse tied to the Boot, killing Fugly (nicknamed “the captain”
mid-fight — see The Guard Captain), while the Boot’s ship pulls away from the dock with him aboard
2025-03-31 @ 00:43:30-03:10:13.
Session ends mid-chase with Rich’s Monk (DungeonVice), hasted and ethereal since @ 02:58:23-03:02:43,
flying after the departing ship and spotting the Boot, unseen by him — whether he’s caught is unresolved
2025-03-31 @ 03:09:40-03:17:16.

quests/kidnap-littlepen.title: Kidnap Littlepen
quests/kidnap-littlepen.content:
A one-shot heist job (DM’d by Ozan): infiltrate a mansion banquet and kidnap the goblin
Littlepen, a guest of the Aspis Corporation.
History

The party infiltrates the banquet under disguise
2020-09-28 @ 00:00:34.
Littlepen is sickened by poisoned soup, beaten unconscious under cover of darkness, and carried out
2020-09-28 @ 01:26:38–02:20:27.
The party escapes a jungle pursuit and secures Littlepen aboard their getaway boat
2020-09-28 @ 03:19:14.

Status
Completed — though no one in the party remembers the agreed payment for the job
2020-09-28 @ 03:22:57.

quests/raising-the-god-baby.title: Raising the God-Baby
quests/raising-the-god-baby.content:
Also heard as: the newborn god
A baby found inside a giant pearl in a flooded shrine, confirmed by detect magic to radiate overwhelming
divine power, with a blank holy-symbol pendant that clasped itself onto him unprompted — signs to the
party that the child is an unclaimed, brand-new god.
History

The baby’s pendant floats up out of the silt on its own and clasps itself around his neck
2020-04-13 @ 00:41:00.
Ozan’s detect magic confirms overwhelming divine power
2020-04-13 @ 00:53:27.
The party debates selling, eating, or waiting out the baby’s childhood before deciding to raise him
themselves as the founder of their own religion
2020-04-13 @ 00:49:08–00:53:49.

Status
Open — the baby’s upbringing and the religion the party plans to found around him are unresolved at the
end of the recorded sessions.

quests/recover-the-tome-of-strahd.title: Recover the Tome of Strahd
quests/recover-the-tome-of-strahd.content:
Recover the party’s stolen copy of the Tome of Strahd.
History

The Tome of Strahd is taken from the party when an earlier, less lethal group of ghosts captures and
ages them rather than killing them
2023-03-18 @ 00:34:16–00:35:05.

Status
Open — never recovered in the recorded sessions.

quests/rescue-donovan.title: Rescue Donovan
quests/rescue-donovan.content:
Free Donovan (Donnie’s character) from his vampire thrall-hood under Strahd von Zarovich,
or otherwise contain him until Strahd’s death.
History

Donovan dies and rises as a chaotic-evil vampire thrall near Strahd’s coffin; the party discusses needing
Cure Vampirism, Resurrection, or Strahd’s death to free him
2023-01-30 @ 05:19:31–05:28:46.
Donovan flees the party as mist rather than being rescued or recaptured
2023-02-12 @ 00:03:28–00:10:31.
Revealed to have secretly turned traitor and been serving Strahd all along; the party fights and defeats
him 2023-03-18 @ 00:48:16 onward.
The party’s attempt to contain his vampire-mist form in a handy haversack backfires when
Todd destroys the haversack, flinging Donovan into the Astral Plane with two hours to
find a resting place or be destroyed forever
2023-03-18.

Status
Failed — Donovan is lost to the Astral Plane and never recovered or mentioned again in the recorded
sessions.

quests/rescue-the-burgomaster's-family.title: Rescue the Burgomaster's Family
quests/rescue-the-burgomaster's-family.content:
Investigate Kolyan Indirovich’s disappearance and his adopted daughter Irina’s
vampiric bite.
History

Started when the party receives Kolyan’s plea for help
2022-12-06 @ 01:08:17.
Complicated by forged letters and the discovery that Irina is already twice-bitten and turning
2022-12-06 @ 02:58:06.
The family orders the party off the property after they try to restrain Irina for everyone’s safety
2022-12-06 @ 03:07:21.

Status
Abandoned — the party is ordered away and never returns to the village or the Indirovich family in any
later recorded session.

quests/retrieve-the-golden-ticket.title: Retrieve the Golden Ticket
quests/retrieve-the-golden-ticket.content:
Riggs’s Widow’s plan to use a hidden golden ticket to confront the
devil holding Riggs’s soul and reunite with him.
History

Revealed by Riggs’s Widow during her interrogation; the ticket itself was not retrieved this session
2025-03-31 @ 00:19:45-00:20:31.

quests/rob-the-bank-for-mitch-copperhead.filePath: quests/Rob the Bank for Mitch Copperhead.md
quests/rob-the-bank-for-mitch-copperhead.title: Rob the Bank for Mitch Copperhead
quests/rob-the-bank-for-mitch-copperhead.content:
Mitch Copperhead hires the party to rob the bank vault in Lidurithal and kill Cadillac on
sight.
History

Hired and briefed; fee negotiated to 8,000 gold
2023-09-12 @ 02:12:06–02:17:57.
The bank is robbed and the Dyson Dynamo recovered, but Cadillac escapes alive under cover of his
own wizard’s Darkness spell 2023-10-01 @ 04:12:40.
Copperhead himself, revealed as a doppelganger, is killed in his own ambush of the party
2023-10-15 @ 00:36:05.

quests/win-the-magic-carpet-race.title: Win the Magic Carpet Race
quests/win-the-magic-carpet-race.content:
Also heard as: the Rug Mandela
The party registers for Lutathal’s annual flying-carpet death race (called the Rug Mandela in
episode 6) without owning a carpet, and schemes to get one in time.
History

Registers for ticket #7 with a shot at a 50,000 gp prize, later settling on the team name “Scorching
Rays” 2023-10-24 @ 02:52:47–02:53:46, @ 02:57:55–02:57:58.
Sponsorship negotiations with carpet-maker Greg collapse @ 02:28:58–03:18:00.
Learns the race (now 20,000 gold winner-take-all) starts the next morning with no carpet in hand; plans
a bait-and-switch — acquire any flying carpet, disguise it, and swap it for a real racer’s
2023-11-28 @ 02:06:28, @ 01:33:40–01:36:58.
Pat bluffs/intimidates a shopkeeper out of a discarded firework carpet and test-flies it with a janky
but functional result (half the carpet holds weight, the other half sags)
@ 01:50:53–01:56:28, @ 02:00:56–02:02:32.

Unresolved
The race itself has not been run as of the last recorded session, which ends on an unrelated cliffhanger
(a demon rising through the city).
Rugby’s Roaming Gazette adds a third naming variant for this same race-and-prize concept: the
“Rugmandella” Race, grand prize a carpet also called the “Rugmandella” (made by Carpet Baggers
Industries), starting in Lauvog, Western Territories — on top of the “Magic Carpet Race”/Lutathal
(episode 5) and “Rug Mandela”/Liduriel/Kalooza (episode 6) variants 2023-09-24. Another
data point in the shifting names, not a resolution.

quotes.title: Best Quotes
quotes.content:
Quotes
The Gang (2019–2021)

“Beyond these doors lies the test of the Pharaoh. Turn now from this doom of power and evil from a
heartless man.” — Pat, reading the door inscription 2019-10-15 @ 00:17:51
“I suppose I can tell you I’m the Dread Pirate Bobber. Fishmen of the high seas.” — Rich, to Andrew
2019-10-15 @ 01:14:26
“We beat D&D, Molly. We did it.” — Jake (OOC) 2019-10-15 @ 02:27:37
“It’s like you move forward. And it’s like, no. You feel pushback. And then you inflict pain. And it’s
like screaming in pain.” — Pat, narrating elemental control 2020-01-20 @ 02:52:14
“I feel like this ship is, if it’s not already made us slide into the evil bracket, it’s pretty
