world/index.title: World Overview
world/index.content:
An orientation to the world as reported by Rugby’s Roaming Gazette, 15 surviving issues spanning
in-world APRIL 1 4885 to DEC 19 4885 (plus one flagged anomaly dated 4900 — see
timeline). This predates every recorded session; treat it as deep, mostly unconnected
backstory rather than as the world the recorded campaigns take place in, except where a page
explicitly cross-references the two (see “Open cross-references” below).
The two kingdoms and their war
The central storyline across the early issues is the war between Binneth
and Squiyles, complicated by a simultaneous orcish invasion from the
east and a troll migration out of the Acatlalco mountains.

Squiyles, ruled by King Stroth, is squeezed on three sides: Gorthak’s united
orc horde conquers its eastern cities (Bostur, Kafka), trolls
ravage its farmland, and Binneth’s secret-weapon fire-breathing navy guts its fleet in the
Howling Gulf. Internal collapse (famine, riots, a failed separatist uprising)
finishes the job.
Binneth, ruled by King Tygard, loses relatively little and emerges from the
war as a rising great power, claiming new territory and new trade deals.
The war’s outcome: Squiyles falls entirely. Changelings —
doppelgangers who first seized the country of Cacoal mid-war — take over the
majority of its former territory, ruling “with an iron fist.” Rugby’s Roaming Gazette, headquartered
in Squiyles’ Conopimalis throughout the war, is forced to relocate its offices to
Stogath in the Western Territories, where it remains for the rest of its surviving
run.

The orc unification
Gorthak (spelled “Garthok”/“Gorthuk”/“Gorthok” at different points — the Gazette
itself flags these as the same figure) rises from a tribal leader to ruler of every orc clan, uniting
them into a single horde that conquers Squiylian territory, clashes with Binneth, and outlasts the war
itself — the Orc Lands remain an established nation years later, when a new generation of Gazette
reporters still dispatches from their territory. His son Zakmed’s capture, and escape,
from Binneth custody is one of the war’s recurring subplots.
The Feywild/Day-Zero anomaly
One issue — 2019-05-12, dated APRIL 17 4900 rather than 4885 — describes “The Agency”
investigating a multiverse-altering event called “Day Zero,” the apparent end of the Material Plane,
and a mass evacuation to the Feywild. The very next issue in publication order reverts to 4885 and
resumes the ongoing war coverage as if nothing happened; the Gazette never mentions any of it again.
Treated here as a flagged, unexplained oddity — not a confirmed part of the main timeline. See
timeline, factions/The Agency, npcs/Dr. E Brown.
Ongoing crises as of the last issue (2023-09-24, in-world DEC 19 4885)

Troll migration and the new “vaccine.” Trolls have spread from the Acatlalco tunnels through the
wider Troll Mountains; alchemists have just announced a compound
(transmitted via troll copulation) meant to strip trolls of their regenerative edge.
The changeling peace-summit scandal. The Changeling Nation’s international peace conference,
meant to secure its legitimacy, collapsed when its own delegates were caught impersonating other
nations’ diplomats — leaving relations between empires strained and uncertain.
Godoy’s guard shortage. The city of Godoy (Acatlalco, Western Territories) is short-staffed after
an overly strict guard-vetting process, leaning on Captain Cadillac Huggins and Captain Darian
Steele — see the next section.

Open cross-references worth knowing about
A handful of pages carry Unresolved notes connecting Gazette content to the recorded campaigns —
flagged as naming echoes or dramatic irony, never as confirmed identity, given the vast and
unreconciled gap in in-world time:

Cadillac / Godoy — the Gazette’s hero cop “Captain Cadillac Huggins” is almost
certainly the JakeDM campaign’s doppelganger crime boss Cadillac, whom the paper has no idea is
either a doppelganger or a crime boss.
Acatlalco / Godoy — a mountain-range name echoed centuries later as a city’s
administrative region.
places/Isle of Death — a monster-haunted island of the same name and reputation appears in both
the Gazette and the JakeDM campaign.
Turgeth / places/Kingdom of Turgyth — a kingdom and a much-later city share a name
root.
the-gang / npcs/Dr. Boom — a 2019-04-22 reader submission reads like an in-world
account of a party of adventurers’ pre-recording exploits, never confirmed as The Gang.
Lutathal / quests/Win the Magic Carpet Race — a third name variant for the same
carpet-race concept.

world/timeline.title: World Timeline
world/timeline.content:
The in-world calendar as reconstructed from Rugby’s Roaming Gazette’s 15 surviving issues, in in-world
date order (not publication order — the two diverge, see below). Recorded sessions are placed on this
calendar only where the Gazette gives real traction; otherwise an issue is simply listed on the
calendar alone.
A note on order: the issues are not published in strict in-world chronological order, and one issue
is a flagged anomaly. Publication order (by filename/real-world date) runs 2019-04-01, 04-09, 04-15,
04-22, 04-29, 05-12, 06-10, 06-17, 06-24, 07-15, 10-07, 2020-04-13, 2022-12-18, 2022-12-26,
2023-09-24. Every issue except the 05-12 one runs APRIL 1 4885 → DEC 19 4885 in sequence. The 05-12
issue alone is dated APRIL 17 4900 — fifteen years later — and the issue immediately after it
(06-10) reverts to APRIL 24 4885 and continues the ongoing war as if nothing happened. The paper never
references the 4900 events again. It is placed below by its stated date, flagged prominently, rather
than folded silently into the main sequence.
4885


APRIL 1 4885 — 2019-04-01. Published in Conopimalis, Erepec, Kingdom of Binneth
(contradicted by every later issue’s masthead — see places/Conopimalis (Erepec)). Stars vanishing
from the sky; a blue dragon attacks the Isle of Torta; doppelganger infiltration panic begins in
Ezaso City; Rex Sauvage’s first field report.


APRIL 6 4885 — 2019-04-09. Bostur falls to the Nayesche orc tribe under Gorthak
(“Bloody Tuesday”); two dragons escape Torta and devastate Stroth Castle; Captain Tartan walks back
the doppelganger panic.


APRIL 10 4885 — 2019-04-15. The annual Squiyles airship race convenes at Laudir; King
Stroth nearly throws King Tygard out a window; Kafka falls to Gorthak’s army.


APRIL 12 4885 — 2019-04-22. Three dragons burn Tadmenroe Cathedral in Thorhofn; King
Stroth declares Squiyles’ first draft in 90 years; a masked orcish killer murders children in Ezaso;
reader submission from “Dr. Boom” (see the-gang Unresolved).


APRIL 15 4885 — 2019-04-29. Captain Jamal claims the Free Islands; Gorthak is
proclaimed ruler of all orc clans; Binneth captures its first orc scout.


APRIL 17 4900 — FLAGGED ANOMALY, see note above — 2019-05-12. “The Agency” and Dr. E
Brown investigate “Day Zero”; the Material Plane apparently ceases to exist; mass evacuation to the
Feywild, Shadowfell, and Ethereal plane. Never referenced again by the paper.


APRIL 24 4885 — 2019-06-10. (Resumes the 4885 sequence immediately after the 4900
anomaly, as if it hadn’t happened.) St. Cuthbert’s church burns in Holsoy; trolls sighted leaving
Acatlalco; naval standoff in the Howling Gulf; Rex Sauvage reported missing; Gorthak demands the
return of his son Zakmed.


APRIL 28 4885 — 2019-06-17. Riots and a civil-war brewing in Squiyles; trolls
rampage central Squiyles’ farms; Binneth’s fire-breathing ships devastate the Squiylian navy; Zakmed
escapes Binneth custody, confirmed as Gorthak’s son.


MAY 4 4885 — 2019-06-24. Turgythe announces a space program; Squiyles starves under
the war and draft; the Bringska reality-rift incident; Grandmaster Wizard Kirby’s immortality-spell
catastrophe.


MAY 8 4885 — 2019-07-15. Graverobbing and the “Dodgers” gang rise in wartime Squiyles;
Rex Sauvage still missing; Cacoal self-declares the “Changeling Nation”; the “Isle of Death” sighting
near Sawyen/Suenth (see places/Isle of Death Unresolved).


JUNE 1 4885 — 2019-10-07. Squiyles has fallen; Eastern and Western Territories
declare sovereignty; changelings rule the former Squiylian heartland; Rugby’s Gazette relocates to
Stogath, Western Territories; a strange magical tunnel appears in the Howling Gulf.


JULY 4 4885 — 2020-04-13. The miasmic “death cloud” spreads from Sawyen and Suenth
across eastern Binneth, the Orc Lands, and Hawkthorne; the village of Meschen is lost; the Gazette
solicits a replacement for the still-missing Rex Sauvage.


JUNE 7 4885 (two issues, same in-world week, different real-world publication dates) —
2022-12-18 and 2022-12-26. Post-war cleanup continues; changelings rule
former Squiyles with “an iron fist”; an international peace summit is announced, then collapses when
changeling delegates are caught impersonating other nations’ diplomats; the Narfuuuk goblin-kidnapping
story near Balnaskor; Timothy Mantooth succeeds the late Rex Sauvage as field reporter.


DEC 19 4885 — 2023-09-24. The Death-Defying “Rugmandella” magic-carpet race is
announced; a troll-sterilizing alchemical “vaccine” is unveiled; Godoy’s guard shortage and Captain
Cadillac Huggins’ heroic framing (see Cadillac Unresolved); Ray Parker’s mystery-airship
report.
This is the one issue with a direct, dateable tie into a recorded campaign: its Godoy/Cadillac/
Rugmandella content sits alongside the JakeDM campaign’s own session dates (real-world September–
November 2023), though the in-world calendars of the Gazette (4885) and JakeDM’s campaign are never
reconciled — see Cadillac and Godoy for the dramatic-irony cross-reference. No
other issue is force-fit onto a session date; most Gazette content predates every recorded session —
anything before 2019-10-15 belongs to the earliest unrecorded era of the-gang.


Recorded sessions, for reference

First recorded session of any campaign: 2019-10-15 (the-gang). Everything in the
Gazette’s 4885/4900 run predates this real-world date, placing it in the unrecorded pre-history the
campaign page itself flags as “backstory from before this wiki’s transcript coverage begins.”
2019-04-22’s “Dr. Boom” submission is the one piece of Gazette content that reads like it
could be drawn from that unrecorded era — see the-gang Unresolved.
The JakeDM campaign’s sessions run real-world September–November 2023, overlapping the 2023-09-24
Gazette issue’s publication date, though not its in-world date (DEC 19 4885) — see above.
